#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""flood.py - a deliberately boring loop that runs coding-agent CLIs on tasks.

No LLM in the control path. One task = one git worktree on branch <task-id>.
Phases per task: implement -> test -> review -> merge. State lives in one JSON
file; everything else is git. Stdlib only.

Usage:
  flood.py run    [--config flood.json] [--once] [--forever]
  flood.py status [--config flood.json]
  flood.py reset  <task-id> [--config flood.json]   # drop a task back to pending (keeps its branch)
  flood.py wipe   --yes [--config flood.json]        # remove every task's worktree + branch and the state file
  flood.py retest <task-id> --gate-bug [--note why] # a gate/script bug failed it: uncharged, tested first
  flood.py forget <task-id> --yes                   # drop ONE task's state, worktree and branch
  flood.py hygiene                                  # stuck-list sweep (flood also runs it hourly)
  flood.py teststats [--hours 24]                   # test-slot wall time + flaky-rerun rate, this vs previous window
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import base64
import fcntl
import glob
import datetime as dt
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import select
import shlex
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

# Identifies the code this process executes: hashed once at import, so a later edit of flood.py on disk
# does not change what the start events (OMP-584-s03) say the running process is.
CODE_SHA256 = hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

TERMINAL = {"done", "failed", "blocked", "planned", "plan_ready", "owner"}   # owner: waits for mark-done
ACTIVE_PHASES = {"implement", "test", "review"}
# Terminal identity of whatever launched flood (tmux, a terminal emulator) must not reach jobs:
# terminal-aware test suites change behaviour with it (oh-my-pi: 3 TUI tests fail under tmux).
# Every job gets the plain terminal the test baseline was measured with.
TERMINAL_VARS = ("TMUX", "TMUX_PANE", "TERM_PROGRAM", "TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION", "COLORTERM", "STY")
# Credential fence: jobs (implement, test, review, plan) get no way to act on external systems.
# Flood's own batch step runs in flood's process and keeps the operator's credentials.
CREDENTIAL_VARS = ("GH_TOKEN", "GITHUB_TOKEN", "SSH_AUTH_SOCK")
# post-job audit: any trace of these in a job's log is reported as an external call
LEDGER_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"(OMP|HOME)-\d+")      # Work Ledger item keys (slices and local tasks are not)
KEY_LIST_RE = re.compile(r"(OMP|HOME)-\d+(\s*,\s*(OMP|HOME)-\d+)*")   # mark-done --ref of filed package children
# word-bounded: "throu*gh repo*sitory" in an implementer's prose matched gh repo (OMP-522-s07-s06-s05, 2026-10-12)
EXTERNAL_CALL_RE = re.compile(r"\b(gh api|gh pr |gh repo|git push|curl .*github)|api\.github\.com")
# text an agent read rather than ran: search hits ("path:12:..."), JSON, markdown quotes/bullets, and
# source lines it printed: a JS/TS statement (`return { ok: false, detail: "gh api ... failed" }`, 2026-09-24)
# or a shell assignment from a workflow file (`changed_files="$(gh pr diff ...)"` in ci.yml, 2026-09-25),
# numbered file lines (`395:   if gh pr diff ...` from grep -n / cat -n of a workflow file, 2026-09-26; grep's
# context lines `1542-   git push origin HEAD:main`, fix-ci-drift review, 2026-10-10),
# and lines indented 8+ spaces: file content a reviewer printed, e.g. a ci.yml `run: |` block
# (`              git push origin HEAD:main`, OMP-335-s03 review, 2026-09-26),
# and unified-diff lines, "+" or "-" glued to the text (`+git push -q origin HEAD:refs/heads/main` in a
# script the OMP-438 reviewer read in the diff, 2026-09-29); a shell trace ("+ git push") keeps its space;
# numbered markdown list items (`5. **s05 - HTTPS inspection.** So a publish or a git push over HTTPS ...`,
# OMP-431 plan, 2026-09-29)
# a diff line holding a comment ("+   # ... avoiding gh pr diff file caps.", OMP-506-s01-s01 review, 2026-10-01): a set -x
# trace prints "+ cmd", never "+ # ...", so a comment after the diff marker is file content
# a Python/JS assignment with spaces round "=" (`client = GitHubPulls('https://api.github.com', ...)` in a
# python heredoc the OMP-518-s02 reviewer ran against a mocked _request, 2026-10-02): no shell line has that shape
QUOTED_RE = re.compile(r"""^(\s{8,}|[+-](?=[^\s+-])|[+-]\s*#|\s*(\S+:\d+[:-]|\d+(:\s|-\s|\t|\.\s)|(\d+[:-])?\||[{\["'>]|- |#|(return|const|let|var)\b|[A-Za-z_]\w*="\$\(|[A-Za-z_][\w.]*\s+=\s))""")
# prose markers no shell command line carries anywhere: an em dash or "e.g."/"i.e."
# (a plan review reasoning "Wait — issue: if ... (e.g., gh pr diff failure fails the step)", 2026-09-26;
# a review noting "the test hits network (api.github.com) — but ...", 2026-09-30)
PROSE_RE = re.compile(r"\u2014|\b(e\.g|i\.e)\.")
# rows of a tab-separated table an agent printed (an upstream-inventory row whose description says
# "A git push fails and is recorded git_receive_pack", OMP-414-s06-s02 review, 2026-09-30): two or more
# tabs; a shell command line carries none
TABLE_ROW_TABS = 2
# the wrapped tail of such a row: one tab, then the last column's bare word ("...recorded git_receive_pack ...
# raw_egress_refused\tretained", orch-verifier-20261011-s02 implement, 2026-10-11)
TABLE_ROW_TAIL_RE = re.compile(r"\t[\w-]+\s*$")
# prose that names a command to forbid it: "Never call gh pr diff or the list-files API", "No gh pr diff / list-files"
# (OMP-504-s01 plan review, 2026-10-01); no shell line puts never/no/not/without right before a command
NEGATED_RE = re.compile(r"\b(never|no|not|without)\s+((call|run|use)(ing|s)?\s+)?$", re.IGNORECASE)
# a message line a program printed, labelled "error:", "fatal:" or "warning:" (a test helper's
# "error: fixture git push -q origin execution/reliability: ..." against a local bare repo, OMP-556 test,
# 2026-10-10); a shell command line never starts with such a label
MESSAGE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(error|fatal|warning):\s", re.IGNORECASE)


CONTROL_FILES = ["*.py", "*.sh", "flood.json", "OPERATING.md", "~/.zshenv", "~/.zshrc", "~/.bashrc", "~/.gitconfig"]


def external_call(line: str) -> bool:
    """A log line that looks like a call to an external system, ignoring text the agent quoted rather than ran:
    QUOTED_RE shapes, and a match inside an inline code span or a double-quoted string (a plan review discussing
    `git push --force origin <candidate>:<ref>` in prose, 2026-09-25)."""
    m = EXTERNAL_CALL_RE.search(line)
    if not m or QUOTED_RE.match(line) or MESSAGE_RE.match(line) or line.count("\t") >= TABLE_ROW_TABS \
            or TABLE_ROW_TAIL_RE.search(line):
        return False
    before = line[: m.start()]
    return (before.count("`") % 2 == 0 and before.count('"') % 2 == 0 and not PROSE_RE.search(line)
            and not NEGATED_RE.search(before))


# a markdown code fence: lines between an opening and closing fence are file content an agent printed
# (the upstream-intake runbook's ```bash block with `git push origin intake/${C:0:12}`, OMP-401-s06 review,
# 2026-10-01), not commands it ran; shell quote splices may come before it when the agent printed the file
# inside a single-quoted bash -lc script (`"'```bash` in the OMP-597 plan's owner-step block, 2026-10-12)
FENCE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*['\"]*(```|~~~)(\w*)")
# a program's printed hint: indented command lines under a header that ends "manually:" (the oh-my-pi natives
# loader's "If missing, delete ... and re-run, or download manually:" + two `curl -fsSL https://github.com/...`
# lines in a failing test's output, orch-worker-20261011-s07-s05 implement, 2026-10-12)
HINT_RE = re.compile(r"\bmanually:\s*$", re.IGNORECASE)


def external_call_lines(output: str) -> list[str]:
    """Lines of a job's output that external_call flags, skipping the inside of markdown code fences and the
    indented lines of a printed "...manually:" hint (also behind pytest's "E" marker).
    A fence with a language tag always opens one (a closing fence carries none): a reviewer that printed a file
    excerpt starting inside a fence flips the count, and the next tagged fence puts it right (OMP-505 plan review,
    2026-10-01, printed docs/upstream-guardrail.md from line 220, inside a ```bash block)."""
    hits, fenced, hint = [], False, False
    for line in output.splitlines():
        body = line[1:] if line.startswith("E ") else line   # pytest's "E" marker before a failure's text
        hint = (hint and body[:1].isspace()) or bool(HINT_RE.search(line))
        if m := FENCE_RE.match(line):
            fenced = bool(m.group(2)) or not fenced
        elif not fenced and not hint and external_call(line):
            hits.append(line)
    return hits
# A verdict is a line that says only VERDICT: PASS|FAIL (markdown emphasis tolerated).
# Anchoring to the whole line stops the instruction sentence in the echoed prompt
# ("...'VERDICT: PASS' or 'VERDICT: FAIL'") from being mistaken for a verdict.
# oh-my-pi-test.sh prints this when a task run qualifies only the CI subset (no protected path changed)
QUALIFY_SUBSET = "installed qualification mode: subset"
# ... and this line on every task run (FLOOD_PHASE=test), which may skip check groups by scope (OMP-344-s03)
TASK_SCOPE = "gate scope: task"
VERDICT_RE = re.compile(r"^[\s>*_`#-]*VERDICT:\s*(PASS|FAIL)[\s*_`.!]*$", re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE)
# the Work Ledger's contract gate: a branch that changes the contract cannot pass its tests
# until the owner approves the new digest in approval.json, so retrying only burns attempts
UNAPPROVED_CONTRACT_RE = re.compile(r"prospective contract digest ([0-9a-f]{64}) is not approved")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- utils
def now() -> str:
    return dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"{now()} {msg}", flush=True)


# lines that name a failure in a gate or CI log; "(pass)" lines that only mention the word are not failures
FAILURE_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"gate: failed|\bFAILED\b|\(fail\)|✗|^\s*(?:error|Error|ERROR)\b|\bError:|Traceback|"
                             r"panicked|##\[error\]|exit(?:ed with)? code [1-9]|ENOSPC|No space left")


def failure_excerpt(output: str, limit: int = 6000) -> str:
    """The failing lines of a log with a little context, earliest first, then the log's summary tail.
    The plain last 6000 characters of a gate log (fix-main-d744b8a22b, 2026-10-10) held only lint warnings
    and the check names; two implementers found nothing to fix and asked for the omitted errors."""
    lines = [l for l in output.splitlines() if l.strip()]
    hits = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if FAILURE_LINE_RE.search(l) and "(pass)" not in l]
    tail = "\n".join(lines[-25:])[-1500:]
    if not hits:
        return "\n".join(lines)[-limit:]
    keep: list[int] = []
    for i in hits:
        keep.extend(range(max(0, i - 3), min(len(lines), i + 9)))
    keep = sorted(set(keep))
    parts, prev = [], -2
    for i in keep:
        if i != prev + 1:
            parts.append("...")
        parts.append(lines[i])
        prev = i
    body = "\n".join(parts)
    room = max(0, limit - len(tail) - 40)
    if len(body) > room:
        body = body[:room] + "\n... (more failures cut)"
    return f"{body}\n\n--- end of the log ---\n{tail}"


# test files a slice may name ("at least one test named per slice")
SLICE_TEST_RE = re.compile(r"[\w./-]*(?:\.(?:test|spec)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?|(?:^|/|\s|`)test_\w+\.py|_test\.(?:py|go|rs))\b")


def first_line(body: str) -> str:
    return next((l.lstrip("# ").strip() for l in body.splitlines() if l.strip()), "")[:100]


def strip_sections(body: str, headings: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
    """The body without the given '# Heading' sections (each runs to the next '# ' heading)."""
    out, skip = [], False
    for line in body.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("# "):
            skip = line.strip() in headings
        if not skip:
            out.append(line)
    return "\n".join(out).strip()


def is_owner(meta: dict) -> bool:
    return str(meta.get("owner", "")).strip().lower() in ("true", "yes", "1")


# Dependency context is parsed once, before any evidence is extracted.
DEPENDENCY_EXCLUSIONS = {"do not touch", "assumptions", "deferred"}
DEPENDENCY_LABEL_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?:(?:[-+*]|\d+[.)])\s+)?"
    r"(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z -]*):\s*(?P<value>.*)$")
DEPENDENCY_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w./-])[./]*[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_./-]*")


def dependency_tokens(text: str) -> set[str]:
    """Whole path/artifact tokens, never individual characters from a string."""
    text = re.sub(r"(?m)^\s*(?:[-+*]|\d+[.)])\s+", "", text)
    return {token.rstrip(".") for token in DEPENDENCY_TOKEN_RE.findall(text)}


def dependency_label(line: str) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
    """Recognize Markdown headings and plain, emphasized or list-prefixed labels."""
    clean = line.strip().replace("**", "").replace("__", "")
    heading = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$", clean)
    level = len(heading[1]) if heading else 0
    if heading:
        clean = heading[2].rstrip("#").strip()
    clean = re.sub(r"\*([^*]+)\*", r"\1", clean)
    label = DEPENDENCY_LABEL_RE.match(clean)
    if label:
        return level, label["label"].strip().lower(), label["value"]
    plain = re.sub(r"^(?:[-+*]|\d+[.)])\s+", "", clean).lower()
    return level, plain if level or plain in DEPENDENCY_EXCLUSIONS else "", ""


def parse_dependency_context(body: str) -> dict:
    """Separate work from exclusions; nested headings belong to their parent section.

    Inline exclusions continue through prose and lists until a peer label or heading.
    Evidence is read only from the resulting work, so excluded references cannot leak.
    """
    work, excluded = [], []
    exclusion_level = None
    for line in body.splitlines():
        level, label, _ = dependency_label(line)
        if exclusion_level is not None:
            boundary = (level and (exclusion_level == 0 or level <= exclusion_level))
            boundary = boundary or (exclusion_level == 0 and bool(label))
            if not boundary:
                excluded.append(line)
                continue
            exclusion_level = None
        if label in DEPENDENCY_EXCLUSIONS:
            exclusion_level = level
            excluded.append(line)
            continue
        # A label may follow work prose on the same line, e.g. "Done when: ... Do not touch: ...".
        inline = re.search(r"(?i)(?<!\w)(?:\*\*|__|\*)?"
                           r"(?:Do not touch|Assumptions|Deferred)(?:\*\*|__|\*)?:"
                           r"(?:\*\*|__|\*)?", line)
        if inline:
            work.append(line[:inline.start()].rstrip())
            excluded.append(line[inline.start():])
            exclusion_level = 0
        else:
            work.append(line)
    work_text = "\n".join(work).strip()
    evidence, in_evidence = [], False
    for line in work_text.splitlines():
        level, label, value = dependency_label(line)
        if level or label:
            in_evidence = label == "evidence"
            if in_evidence:
                evidence.append(value)
        elif in_evidence:
            evidence.append(line)
    return {"work_text": work_text, "excluded_tokens": dependency_tokens("\n".join(excluded)),
            "evidence": dependency_tokens("\n".join(evidence))}


DEPENDENCY_VERB_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:reads?|reading|imports?|importing|consumes?|consuming|"
    r"extends?|extending|apply|applies|applying)\b", re.I)
DEPENDENCY_NEGATION_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:no|not|never|without|avoid|neither|nor|cannot|fail|fails|failed|"
    r"instead|rather|\w*n't\w*)\b", re.I)

DEPENDENCY_QUALIFIER_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:may|might|could|would|hypothetical|potential|optional|future|later|"
    r"reference|unrelated)\b", re.I)
DEPENDENCY_CLAUSE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\n|;|\.(?=\s|$)|,\s*(?![\s`\'\"]*\x00|\s)|"
    r"\b(?:but|then|while|whereas)\b|\band\b(?!\s+[`\'\"]*\x00|\s+"
    + DEPENDENCY_VERB_RE.pattern + r")", re.I)


def dependency_consumes(work_text: str, tokens: set[str]) -> bool:
    """Bind a producer token and affirmative verb inside one consumption clause."""
    # Mask token contents in prose, keeping offsets and sentence punctuation intact.
    # Path dots are not sentence boundaries; artifact names are not qualifiers/verbs.
    def mask_token(match: re.Match) -> str:
        token = match[0].rstrip(".")
        if token in tokens or "/" in token or "." in token:
            return "\x00" * len(token) + match[0][len(token):]
        return match[0]

    prose = DEPENDENCY_TOKEN_RE.sub(mask_token, work_text)
    start = 0
    for boundary in [*DEPENDENCY_CLAUSE_RE.finditer(prose), None]:
        end = boundary.start() if boundary else len(prose)
        clause = prose[start:end]
        # Negation applies to the entire coordinated consumption clause, including
        # predicates after its targets. Sentence/action boundaries still end scope.
        negated = DEPENDENCY_NEGATION_RE.search(clause)
        verbs = list(DEPENDENCY_VERB_RE.finditer(clause))
        for i, verb in enumerate(verbs):
            # Qualifiers remain local to an action separated by "and"; a reference
            # read can coexist with an affirmative import in the same coordination.
            prefix = re.split(r"\band\b", clause[:verb.start()], flags=re.I)[-1]
            stop = verbs[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(verbs) else len(clause)
            if (negated or DEPENDENCY_QUALIFIER_RE.search(
                    prefix + clause[verb.start():stop])):
                continue
            target = work_text[start + verb.end():start + stop]
            if any(token and re.search(r"(?<![\w./-])" + re.escape(token)
                                       + r"(?![\w./-])", target) for token in tokens):
                return True
        start = boundary.end() if boundary else end
    return False


def dependency_owner_approval(owner: dict, implementer: dict) -> bool:
    """An owner-origin approval command applies only to its named issue's implementer."""
    if not owner["owner"]:
        return False
    commands = [str(owner.get("owner_cmd") or "").strip()]
    in_owner_runs = False
    for line in owner["work_text"].splitlines():
        level, label, value = dependency_label(line)
        if level or label:
            in_owner_runs = label == "owner runs"
        if in_owner_runs:
            command = value if label else line.strip()
            command = re.sub(r"^(?:[-+*]|\d+[.)])\s+", "", command)
            commands.append(command.strip().strip("`"))
    issue = re.match(r"[A-Z]+-\d+", implementer["id"])
    return bool(issue) and any(match[1] == issue[0] for command in commands
                              if (match := re.fullmatch(r"omp-work approve --issue ([A-Z]+-\d+)", command)))


def dependency_edge_violation(consumer: dict, producer: dict, is_union,
                              final_changelog: bool = False) -> str | None:
    """Require shared edits or affirmative consumption, never mere ordering."""
    if consumer["owner"] or final_changelog:
        return None
    if dependency_owner_approval(producer, consumer):
        return None
    excluded = producer["excluded_tokens"] | consumer["excluded_tokens"]
    if producer["owner"]:
        results = (set(producer["outputs"]) | producer["evidence"]) - excluded
        results = {result for result in results if not is_union(result)}
        if dependency_consumes(consumer["work_text"], results):
            return None
        return (f"{consumer['id']}: depends_on {producer['id']} lacks affirmative owner result "
                f"evidence; name an unexcluded output or Evidence result of {producer['id']} "
                "that this slice reads, imports, consumes or extends")
    paths = {fp for fp in producer["files"] if fp not in excluded and not is_union(fp)}
    if paths.intersection(set(consumer["files"]) - excluded):
        return None
    basenames = [Path(fp).name for fp in paths]
    tokens = paths | {name for name in basenames
                      if basenames.count(name) == 1 and name not in excluded}
    tokens.update(output for output in producer["outputs"]
                  if output not in excluded and not is_union(output))
    if dependency_consumes(consumer["work_text"], tokens):
        return None
    return (f"{consumer['id']}: depends_on {producer['id']} orders the slice only; "
            f"leave depends_on empty, edit a file {producer['id']} also edits, or name a file "
            f"or output of {producer['id']} that this slice reads, imports, consumes or extends")


def validate_slices(item: str, pdir: Path, max_slices: int = 8, max_body: int = 2000,
                    max_minutes: float = 90, is_union=lambda fp: False) -> tuple[list[str], list[dict]]:
    """The planner's output checked without a model. Returns (violations, slices)."""
    files = sorted(pdir.glob("*.md")) if pdir.is_dir() else []
    if not files:
        return [f"no slice files in {pdir}"], []
    v: list[str] = []
    if len(files) > max_slices:
        v.append(f"{len(files)} slices; at most {max_slices}")
    id_re = re.compile(rf"{re.escape(item)}-s\d{{2}}")
    slices = []
    for f in files:
        text = f.read_text(errors="replace")
        try:
            meta, body = parse_front_matter(text)
        except ValueError as e:
            v.append(f"{f.name}: front matter does not parse ({e})")
            continue
        sid = meta.get("id")
        if not text.startswith("---") or not sid:
            v.append(f"{f.name}: no front matter with an id")
            continue
        if not id_re.fullmatch(sid):
            v.append(f"{f.name}: id {sid!r} must be {item}-sNN")
        if f.stem != sid:
            v.append(f"{f.name}: file name must be {sid}.md")
        if meta.get("kind", "implement") != "implement":
            v.append(f"{sid}: kind must be implement")
        if float(meta.get("max_minutes", max_minutes)) > max_minutes:
            v.append(f"{sid}: max_minutes {meta['max_minutes']:g} > {max_minutes:g}")
        body = body.strip()
        if len(strip_sections(body, ("# Assumptions", "# Deferred"))) > max_body:
            v.append(f"{sid}: body is {len(strip_sections(body, ('# Assumptions', '# Deferred')))} chars "
                     f"(Assumptions/Deferred not counted); at most {max_body}")
        if "Done when:" not in body:
            v.append(f"{sid}: no \"Done when:\" section")
        if is_owner(meta):              # owner slices: exact commands + what mark-done's --ref must be
            v += [f"{sid}: owner slice has no \"{k}\" section" for k in ("Owner runs:", "Evidence:") if k not in body]
        else:
            if not meta.get("files"):
                v.append(f"{sid}: no `files: [...]` in front matter")
            if "Do not touch" not in body:
                v.append(f"{sid}: no \"Do not touch\" list")
            if not SLICE_TEST_RE.search(body):
                v.append(f"{sid}: names no test file to add or extend")
        context = parse_dependency_context(body)
        slices.append({"id": sid, "depends_on": meta.get("depends_on", []), "file": f,
                       "files": meta.get("files", []), "outputs": meta.get("outputs", []),
                       "body": body, "owner": is_owner(meta), "owner_cmd": meta.get("owner_cmd"), **context})
    ids = [sl["id"] for sl in slices]
    for dup in sorted({i for i in ids if ids.count(i) > 1}):
        v.append(f"duplicate slice id {dup}")
    graph = {sl["id"]: [d for d in sl["depends_on"] if d in ids] for sl in slices}
    for sl in slices:
        v += [f"{sl['id']}: depends on {d}, which is not in this set" for d in sl["depends_on"] if d not in ids]
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}                        # 1 = on the DFS stack, 2 = finished

    def visit(n: str) -> None:
        seen[n] = 1
        for d in graph.get(n, []):
            if seen.get(d) == 1:
                v.append(f"dependency cycle through {n} -> {d}")
            elif not seen.get(d):
                visit(d)
        seen[n] = 2

    for n in graph:
        if not seen.get(n):
            visit(n)

    def ancestors(n: str, acc: set[str] | None = None) -> set[str]:
        acc = set() if acc is None else acc
        for d in graph.get(n, []):
            if d not in acc:
                acc.add(d)
                ancestors(d, acc)
        return acc

    anc = {n: ancestors(n) for n in graph}
    by_file: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for sl in slices:
        for fp in sl["files"]:
            by_file.setdefault(fp, []).append(sl["id"])
    for fp, owners in sorted(by_file.items()):           # a shared file needs an ordering between its editors
        if is_union(fp):                                   # ... unless git merges it by union (merge=union)
            continue
        for i, a in enumerate(owners):
            for b in owners[i + 1:]:
                if a not in anc.get(b, set()) and b not in anc.get(a, set()):
                    v.append(f"{a} and {b} both edit {fp} but neither depends on the other")
    logs = sorted({sl["id"] for sl in slices for fp in sl["files"] if "changelog" in fp.lower()})
    if len(logs) > 1:
        v.append(f"only the last slice may touch the changelog; {', '.join(logs)} all do")
    elif logs and anc.get(logs[0], set()) != set(ids) - {logs[0]}:
        v.append(f"{logs[0]} touches the changelog but is not the last slice (it must depend on every other slice)")
    by_id = {sl["id"]: sl for sl in slices}
    for sl in slices:
        for dep in sl["depends_on"]:
            if dep in by_id:
                final_changelog = (logs == [sl["id"]]
                                   and anc.get(sl["id"], set()) == set(ids) - {sl["id"]}
                                   and all("changelog" in fp.lower() for fp in sl["files"]))
                violation = dependency_edge_violation(sl, by_id[dep], is_union, final_changelog)
                if violation:
                    v.append(violation)
    return v, slices


SEVERE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(High|Critical|Blocker|Blocking|P1|P0)\b")


def review_gist(lines: list[str], verdict: str | None) -> str:
    """Status-column summary of a failed review, read from the reviewer's final message only (codex
    logs echo the prompt and spec before a line "codex"; its final answer follows the last one):
    the first severe finding, else the last substantive line."""
    marks = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.strip() == "codex"]
    final = lines[marks[-1] + 1:] if marks else lines
    if not marks:                             # kimi: each message starts "• "; the final one is last
        kimi = [i for i, l in enumerate(final) if l.startswith("• ")]
        final = final[kimi[-1]:] if kimi else final
    body = [l.strip().removeprefix("• ") for l in final if not VERDICT_RE.match(l) and len(l.strip()) > 20
            and not l.strip().startswith(("tokens used", "To resume this session"))
            and not re.match(r"No (worktree |file )?changes (were )?made", l.strip())]
    return next((l for l in body if SEVERE_RE.search(l)), body[-1] if body else "")


CODACY_ISSUES = "https://app.codacy.com/api/v3/analysis/organizations/gh/{org}/repositories/{name}/pull-requests/{pr}/issues"
CODACY_TEST_RE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(tests?|__tests__|fixtures)/|\.(test|spec)\.")   # same paths as the repo's .codacy.yml
DISK_FULL_RE = re.compile(r"No space left on device|errno 28|DiskFull|ENOSPC", re.I)


def disk_has_room(path: str = "/tmp", min_free: float = 0.25) -> bool:
    """A full disk (ENOSPC) fails every job at once; tests wait for room instead of burning attempts."""
    u = shutil.disk_usage(path)
    v = os.statvfs(path)  # tmpfs also runs out of inodes (2026-09-26: 90 % used while bytes sat at 34 %)
    return u.free >= u.total * min_free and (not v.f_files or v.f_favail >= v.f_files * min_free)


def first_failure(output: str) -> str:
    """First failing test named in a test log (bun's ✗ lines, pytest's FAILED), else an error line."""
    lines = [l.strip() for l in output.splitlines()]
    # the gate passed these files alone ("flaky: <dir>/<file>"); a later step failed, not them
    flaky = {l.split()[1].rsplit("/", 1)[-1] for l in lines if l.startswith("flaky: ")}
    lines = [l for l in lines if not any(f in l for f in flaky)]
    fails = [l for l in lines if l.startswith(("✗", "FAILED", "(fail)"))]
    hit = next((l for l in fails if " — " in l), None) or next(iter(fails), None) \
        or next((l for l in lines if l.startswith(("ERROR:", "error:", "gate: FAILED"))), None) \
        or next((l for l in lines if "Error" in l and "│" not in l), None)
    return (hit or "see log")[:160]


def sh(args: list[str], cwd: str | Path | None = None, check: bool = True,
       timeout: int | None = None, env: dict | None = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd, text=True, capture_output=True,
                          check=check, timeout=timeout, env=env)


def gh_repo_slug(url: str) -> str:
    """owner/name of a GitHub remote URL (https or ssh); "" for anything else."""
    m = re.search(r"github\.com[:/]+([^/\s]+)/([^/\s]+?)(?:\.git)?/?$", url)
    return f"{m[1]}/{m[2]}" if m else ""


APPROVAL_PATH = "python/omp-work/src/omp_work/contracts/v1/approval.json"


def rebase_in_progress(wt: Path) -> bool:
    r = sh(["git", "rev-parse", "--git-path", "rebase-merge", "--git-path", "rebase-apply"], cwd=wt, check=False)
    return any(Path(wt, p).exists() if not os.path.isabs(p) else Path(p).exists() for p in r.stdout.split())


INVENTORY_PATH = "docs/upstream-fork-inventory.tsv"
STAMP_LINE_RE = re.compile(r'^[-+](\s*"generatedAt": |Generated: )')


def stamp_only_change(wt: Path, old: str, new: str, path: str) -> bool:
    """True when `old` -> `new` changes the docs/report file `path` only in its generatedAt/Generated: lines."""
    if not path.startswith("docs/report/"):
        return False
    d = sh(["git", "diff", "-U0", old, new, "--", path], cwd=wt, check=False)
    lines = [ln for ln in d.stdout.splitlines() if ln[:1] in "+-" and not ln.startswith(("+++", "---"))]
    return d.returncode == 0 and bool(lines) and all(STAMP_LINE_RE.match(ln) for ln in lines)


def git(repo: str | Path, *args: str, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return sh(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], check=check)


def atomic_write(path: Path, data: str) -> None:
    tmp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(data)
    os.replace(tmp, path)


# Interim job sandbox (owner 2026-10-10, until jobs run as ompbot; flood.json "sandbox"): bwrap shares the whole
# file system with the job but puts an empty tmpfs over each credential store, /dev/null over each socket or
# credential file, and makes flood's own files and the shell start-up files read-only. The AI CLIs' own login
# dirs stay visible. Owner commands (omp-work approve / schema) and flood's batch step never run in it.
SANDBOX_HIDE = ("~/.ssh", "~/.config/gh", "~/.config/omp", "~/.config/omp-work", "~/.config/flood",
                "~/.aws", "~/.codacy", "~/.docker", "~/.kube", "~/.gnupg", "~/.keychain")
SANDBOX_NULL = ("/run/docker.sock", "~/.git-credentials", "~/.config/neo4j.env")
SANDBOX_READ_ONLY = ("~/flood", "~/.zshenv", "~/.zshrc", "~/.bashrc", "~/.profile", "~/.bash_profile", "~/.gitconfig")
# Owner plugin hooks that write into the job's repo. grok loads every Claude Code plugin's hooks (its Claude Code
# compatibility); arch-docs-verifier's Stop hook rewrites the generatedAt stamp of docs/report/verification.{json,md},
# flood auto-committed it, and each merge of a new stamp made every other stamped branch conflict (OMP-553,
# OMP-344-s01-s01, OMP-569-s02, OMP-569-s05 on 2026-10-10). Glob entries, hidden like SANDBOX_HIDE.
SANDBOX_NO_HOOKS = ("~/.claude/plugins/cache/*/arch-docs-verifier/*/hooks", "~/dev-marketplace/arch-docs-verifier/hooks")
# Network tools an agent job (implement, plan, review) sees as a refusing stub: a codex implement ran
# `curl -I https://github.com/...` for a release asset (fix-gate-nsi6-pg-tests-s01, 2026-10-14 07:01Z). The CLIs
# need the network for their own API, so this is a tool wall, not a network namespace. Test jobs and the gate keep
# the real tools (gate == CI).
SANDBOX_AGENT_DENY = ("/usr/bin/curl", "/usr/bin/wget")
SANDBOX_DENY_STUB = "~/flood/providers/no-egress.sh"


def sandbox_argv(sb: dict | None, writable: list[str], agent: bool = False) -> list[str]:
    """The bwrap prefix for a job, or [] when flood.json "sandbox" is off. Missing paths are skipped (bwrap
    refuses a bind of a missing source). `writable` dirs inside a read-only one (flood's .job-fence) are bound
    back read-write after it. An `agent` job gets the deny stub over each SANDBOX_AGENT_DENY tool."""
    if not sb or not sb.get("enabled"):
        return []
    x = lambda p: os.path.expanduser(p)
    argv = [sb.get("bwrap", "bwrap"), "--dev-bind", "/", "/"]
    hooks = [g for p in sb.get("no_hooks", SANDBOX_NO_HOOKS) for g in sorted(glob.glob(x(p)))]
    for p in [*map(x, sb.get("hide", SANDBOX_HIDE)), *hooks]:
        if os.path.isdir(p):
            argv += ["--tmpfs", p]
        elif os.path.exists(p):
            argv += ["--dev-bind", "/dev/null", p]
    for p in map(x, sb.get("null", SANDBOX_NULL)):
        if os.path.exists(p):
            argv += ["--dev-bind", "/dev/null", p]
    for p in map(x, sb.get("read_only", SANDBOX_READ_ONLY)):
        if os.path.exists(p):
            argv += ["--ro-bind", p, p]
    for p in map(x, writable):
        if os.path.exists(p):
            argv += ["--bind", p, p]
    stub = x(sb.get("deny_stub", SANDBOX_DENY_STUB))
    for p in map(x, sb.get("agent_deny", SANDBOX_AGENT_DENY) if agent else ()):
        if os.path.exists(p):
            argv += ["--ro-bind", stub, p]
    # "extra": raw bwrap arguments, e.g. a path shim for the automation user: an empty /home/thetu with ompbot's
    # copy of a file the repo's AGENTS.md names by its owner path (OMP-402 move, 2026-10-10)
    return [*argv, *[x(str(a)) for a in sb.get("extra", [])], "--"]


SLOT_TAKEN = 75     # `flock -n -E 75`: the test slot flood picked was taken first by a run flood did not start


def slot_free(path: str) -> bool:
    """True when nobody holds this test-slot lock file right now (probe: take it without waiting, release)."""
    try:
        with open(path, "a") as fh:
            fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
            fcntl.flock(fh, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
        return True
    except OSError:
        return False


def pid_alive(pid: int) -> bool:
    try:
        os.kill(pid, 0)
    except ProcessLookupError:
        return False
    except PermissionError:
        return True
    return True


def adopted_status(pid: int) -> tuple[bool, int | None]:
    """(alive, returncode) for a pid we did not spawn in this process (or a
    child left over in this process). Reaps zombies when it can."""
    if not pid:
        return False, None
    try:
        wpid, status = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
        if wpid == pid:
            return False, os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
        return True, None
    except ChildProcessError:
        return pid_alive(pid), None


APPROVAL_MODEL = "python/omp-work/src/omp_work/v1/models.py"


def allow_approval_issue(issue: str, wt: Path, uv: list[str]) -> str | None:
    """The contract lists the issues that may approve it (models.Approval.issue, mirrored in schema.json).
    Naming an issue there is the owner's call, so flood adds a missing key before approving and
    regenerates the schemas; the digest it approves then covers the addition."""
    mp = wt / APPROVAL_MODEL
    if not mp.exists():
        return None
    text = mp.read_text()
    block = re.search(r"(class Approval\(StrictModel\):.*?issue: Literal\[\n)(.*?)(\n    \])", text, re.S)
    if not block or f'"{issue}"' in block[2]:
        return None
    text = text[:block.end(2)] + f'\n        "{issue}",' + text[block.end(2):]
    mp.write_text(text)
    r = subprocess.run([*uv, "schema", "--write"], cwd=wt, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
    return None if r.returncode == 0 else f"schema --write after allowing {issue}: {(r.stdout + r.stderr).strip()[-400:]}"


def gateway_approve(gateway: list[str], issue: str, wt: Path) -> str | None:
    """Contract approval through the owner-action gateway (OMP-546-s03) when flood runs as the automation user:
    the contract files named in manifest.json go to `<gateway> approve --issue K` as data, and its stdout is the
    approval.json. flood never holds the owner key; the gateway never runs code from the worktree."""
    ap = wt / APPROVAL_PATH
    d = ap.parent
    try:
        paths = json.loads((d / "manifest.json").read_text())["paths"]
        files = {rel: base64.b64encode((d / rel).read_bytes()).decode() for rel in ["manifest.json", *paths]
                 if rel != "approval.json"}
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
        return f"gateway approve: cannot read the contract files: {e}"
    r = subprocess.run([*gateway, "approve", "--issue", issue], input=json.dumps({"files": files}).encode(),
                       capture_output=True, timeout=600)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return f"gateway approve rc {r.returncode}: {r.stderr.decode(errors='replace').strip()[-400:]}"
    try:
        payload = json.loads(r.stdout)
    except ValueError:
        return f"gateway approve printed no JSON: {r.stdout.decode(errors='replace')[-200:]}"
    if payload.get("issue") != issue or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", str(payload.get("contract_sha256", ""))):
        return f"gateway approve: unexpected approval {str(payload)[:200]}"
    ap.write_bytes(r.stdout)
    return None


def run_owner_cmd(cmd: str, wt: Path, gateway: list[str] | None = None) -> str | None:
    """The allowlisted owner commands flood knows how to run. `omp-work approve --issue K` insists on a TTY
    and the typed digest: flood computes `omp-work hash`, answers the prompt through `script`, and copies
    the digest into packages/work-client/src/contract.ts. Skipped when approval.json already holds it.
    With `gateway` (flood.json owner_gateway, the automation user) the approval itself comes from the gateway."""
    uv = ["uv", "run", "--project", "python/omp-work", "omp-work"]
    m = re.fullmatch(r"omp-work approve --issue ([A-Z]+-\d+)", cmd)
    if m:
        err = allow_approval_issue(m[1], wt, uv)
        if err:
            return err
        h = subprocess.run([*uv, "hash"], cwd=wt, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
        digest = (h.stdout.strip().splitlines() or [""])[-1]
        if h.returncode != 0 or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", digest):
            return f"omp-work hash: {(h.stdout + h.stderr).strip()[-400:]}"
        ap = wt / APPROVAL_PATH
        cur = json.loads(ap.read_text()) if ap.exists() else {}
        if gateway and (cur.get("contract_sha256") != digest or cur.get("issue") != m[1]):
            err = gateway_approve(gateway, m[1], wt)
            if err:
                return err
            if json.loads(ap.read_text()).get("contract_sha256") != digest:
                return f"gateway approve: approval digest differs from omp-work hash {digest[:12]}"
        elif cur.get("contract_sha256") != digest or cur.get("issue") != m[1]:
            proc = subprocess.Popen(["script", "-qfec", shlex.join([*uv, "approve", "--issue", m[1]]), "/dev/null"],
                                    cwd=wt, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
            seen, deadline = b"", time.time() + 600
            while b"Type the full contract" not in seen and time.time() < deadline and proc.poll() is None:
                r, _, _ = select.select([proc.stdout], [], [], 5)
                if r:
                    seen += os.read(proc.stdout.fileno(), 4096)
            if b"Type the full contract" not in seen:
                proc.kill()
                return f"approve never prompted: {seen.decode(errors='replace')[-400:]}"
            proc.stdin.write(digest.encode() + b"\n")
            proc.stdin.flush()
            out, _ = proc.communicate(timeout=300)
            if proc.returncode != 0 or json.loads(ap.read_text()).get("contract_sha256") != digest:
                return f"approve: {(seen + out).decode(errors='replace')[-400:]}"
        ts = wt / "packages/work-client/src/contract.ts"
        if ts.exists():
            t = ts.read_text()
            ts.write_text(re.sub(r'(WORK_CONTRACT_SHA256 = ")[0-9a-f]{64}(")', rf"\g<1>{digest}\g<2>", t))
        return None
    if cmd == "omp-work schema --write":
        r = subprocess.run([*uv, "schema", "--write"], cwd=wt, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
        return None if r.returncode == 0 else (r.stdout + r.stderr).strip()[-400:]
    return f"flood does not know how to run {cmd!r}"


def model_of(entry: dict, name: str | None) -> str:
    """The model a provider or reviewer entry runs: the value after -m/--model in its cmd, else its name."""
    cmd = entry.get("cmd") or []
    return next((cmd[i + 1] for i, a in enumerate(cmd[:-1]) if a in ("-m", "--model")), name or "")


def family(model: str) -> str:
    """A model's maker: claude-opus-5-5 and claude-sonnet-4-6 are both "claude", grok-4.6 and grok-4.7 both
    "grok". Reviewers are chosen by maker, so a second model of the same maker never checks its sibling's work."""
    return re.split(r"[-/:.]", model.lower(), maxsplit=1)[0]


# Usage windows that name model groups ("Weekly, Fable", "Claude and GPT, weekly") count only for those models.
USAGE_GROUPS = ("fable", "opus", "sonnet", "haiku", "gemini", "claude", "gpt")


def window_applies(label: str, model: str) -> bool:
    """A window that names no model group ("Weekly", "5-hour") counts for every model of its subscription."""
    named = [g for g in USAGE_GROUPS if re.search(rf"\b{g}\b", label, re.I)]
    return not named or any(g in model.lower() for g in named)


# OMP-613: the routing decision as pure functions of logged inputs, so routing.jsonl can replay any choice.
# Tiers: 0 = a usage reading below usage_stop_pct (most allowance left first, 10-point buckets), 1 = no reading
# ("unknown": Kimi's API answers 401, Ollama publishes none, usage.json missing or stale), 2 = at or over
# usage_stop_pct but still allowed on paid credits. Unknown is never read as 0 % or 50 %.
UNKNOWN = "unknown"


def usage_tier(usage, stop_pct: float) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """(tier, bucket) for one candidate's usage reading (a percent, or UNKNOWN). Owner 2026-10-13 (Chris): unknown
    is used until it is not able to run: it ranks with the most allowance left (tier 0, bucket 0), and a rate limit
    benches it like any other provider."""
    if usage is None or usage == UNKNOWN:
        return (0, 0)
    pct = min(float(usage), 100.0)
    return (2 if pct >= stop_pct else 0, int(pct // 10))


def route_blocked(c: dict) -> bool:
    """A known reading at or over the stop percentage stops new jobs unless the subscription runs on credits.
    Unknown never stops a job (owner 2026-10-02: no reading = no stop)."""
    u = c.get("usage")
    return u not in (None, UNKNOWN) and float(u) >= float(c["stop_pct"]) and not c.get("credits_ok")


def choose_provider(names: list[str], cursor: int, cands: dict[str, dict]) -> tuple[list[str], str | None, dict]:
    """Round robin from the cursor, then stable sort by (plan: maker already tried, demoted for recent failures,
    usage tier, bucket); the first
    candidate not cooling down, not usage-blocked and under max_parallel wins. Returns (order, chosen, skipped)."""
    if not names:
        return [], None, {}
    order = [names[(cursor + i) % len(names)] for i in range(len(names))]
    order.sort(key=lambda n: (bool(cands[n].get("tried")), bool(cands[n].get("demoted")),
                              *usage_tier(cands[n].get("usage"), cands[n]["stop_pct"])))
    skipped: dict[str, str] = {}
    for n in order:
        c = cands[n]
        if c.get("cooling"):
            skipped[n] = "cooling down"
        elif route_blocked(c):
            skipped[n] = "usage stop"
        elif int(c.get("load", 0)) >= int(c.get("max_parallel", 1)):
            skipped[n] = "at max_parallel"
        else:
            return order, n, skipped
    return order, None, skipped


def task_role(task: dict) -> str:
    """Plan tasks pick only from role "plan" providers; everything else from role "implement"."""
    return "plan" if task.get("kind") == "plan" else "implement"


def reap_leftovers(pgid: int, tid: str) -> int:
    """Kill processes still in a finished job's process group (test helpers, background tools an
    agent left behind). Only processes carrying this job's FLOOD_TASK marker are touched, so a
    process-group id since reused by something unrelated is never hit."""
    marker, killed = f"FLOOD_TASK={tid}".encode(), 0
    for d in os.listdir("/proc"):
        if not d.isdigit():
            continue
        try:
            fields = open(f"/proc/{d}/stat").read().rsplit(")", 1)[1].split()   # state ppid pgrp ...
            if int(fields[2]) != pgid:
                continue
            env = open(f"/proc/{d}/environ", "rb").read().split(b"\0")
        except (OSError, IndexError, ValueError):
            continue
        if marker in env:
            try:
                os.kill(int(d), signal.SIGKILL)
                killed += 1
            except ProcessLookupError:
                pass
    return killed


def prune_pytest_basetemps(root: Path | None = None, older_than: float = 2 * 3600.0) -> list[tuple[Path, int]]:
    """Remove pytest basetemp dirs (/tmp/pytest-of-<user>/pytest-N) whose .lock names a dead pid and that were
    last modified more than older_than seconds ago. A test process killed by a timeout or a SIGKILL leaves its
    lock behind and pytest never prunes the dir (2026-09-25 18:00Z: 4.2 GB in three dead dirs on the tmpfs every
    job shares, one a 3.7 GB python/omp-work run). Returns (path, bytes) per removed dir."""
    import getpass, tempfile
    root = root or Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"pytest-of-{getpass.getuser()}"
    removed: list[tuple[Path, int]] = []
    if not root.is_dir():
        return removed
    cutoff = time.time() - older_than
    for d in root.glob("pytest-*"):
        lock = d / ".lock"
        try:
            if d.is_symlink() or not d.is_dir() or d.stat().st_mtime > cutoff or not lock.is_file():
                continue
            pid = int(lock.read_text().strip() or 0)
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            continue
        if pid and pid_alive(pid):
            continue
        r = subprocess.run(["du", "-sb", str(d)], capture_output=True, text=True)
        size = int(r.stdout.split()[0]) if r.returncode == 0 and r.stdout.split() else 0
        shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
        if not d.exists():
            removed.append((d, size))
    return removed


def prune_tmp_leaks(prefixes, root: Path = Path("/tmp"), older_than: float = 2 * 3600.0) -> int:
    """Remove top-level entries under root whose name starts with one of prefixes (flood.json tmp_leak_prefixes:
    names only oh-my-pi's tests create), owned by us and last modified more than older_than seconds ago. The
    suites leave ~7,000 such dirs per 6 h; 2026-09-26 07:10Z /tmp held 86k entries at 90 % of its inodes.
    Returns the number removed."""
    prefixes = tuple(p for p in prefixes if p)
    if not prefixes or not root.is_dir():
        return 0
    cutoff, uid, n = time.time() - older_than, os.getuid(), 0
    for e in os.scandir(root):
        if not e.name.startswith(prefixes):
            continue
        try:
            st = e.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
        except OSError:
            continue
        if st.st_uid != uid or st.st_mtime > cutoff:
            continue
        p = Path(e.path)
        if e.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
            shutil.rmtree(p, ignore_errors=True)
            if p.exists():
                # Some suites leave read-only dirs (mgr-test-*: 2,241 entries from 2026-09-13 survived every
                # sweep until 2026-09-30): make every real dir writable, then try again.
                for d, subdirs, _ in os.walk(p):
                    for x in [d] + [os.path.join(d, s) for s in subdirs]:
                        try:
                            if not os.path.islink(x):
                                os.chmod(x, 0o700)
                        except OSError:
                            pass
                shutil.rmtree(p, ignore_errors=True)
        else:
            p.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        n += not os.path.lexists(p)
    return n


def marked_processes(exclude_pgids: set[int] = frozenset()) -> dict[str, list[int]]:
    """Every process carrying a FLOOD_TASK marker, by task id, outside the given process groups."""
    out: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
    for d in os.listdir("/proc"):
        if not d.isdigit():
            continue
        try:
            fields = open(f"/proc/{d}/stat").read().rsplit(")", 1)[1].split()
            if int(fields[2]) in exclude_pgids:
                continue
            env = open(f"/proc/{d}/environ", "rb").read().split(b"\0")
        except (OSError, IndexError, ValueError):
            continue
        for e in env:
            if e.startswith(b"FLOOD_TASK="):
                out.setdefault(e[11:].decode(errors="replace"), []).append(int(d))
                break
    return out


STALE_RUNTIME_RE = r"^({root}/tmp\.[^/]+)/omp-installed-runtime/"


def stale_runtime_pids(procs=None, root: str = "/tmp") -> list[int]:
    """Pids of installed-runtime test servers (bun .../run.ts and `omp_work serve`) whose staging dir is gone.
    The session-system runtime tests stage a copy of the runtime under mktemp -d and start its servers with a
    scrubbed environment (no FLOOD_TASK marker, so reap_leftovers and sweep_strays never see them) in their own
    process group; a pytest killed by a timeout leaves them running after the staging dir is removed (2026-09-26
    00:00Z: two bun+python pairs, 2.6 h and 2 h old, from the 22:46Z and 23:06Z 20-minute kills, ppid = the user
    manager). Stale = argv[0] under a {root}/tmp.*/omp-installed-runtime/ whose tmp dir no longer exists; a live
    test's servers keep their dir. procs: (pid, argv0) pairs, default read from /proc."""
    pat = re.compile(STALE_RUNTIME_RE.format(root=re.escape(root)))
    if procs is None:
        procs = []
        for d in os.listdir("/proc"):
            if not d.isdigit():
                continue
            try:
                argv0 = open(f"/proc/{d}/cmdline", "rb").read().split(b"\0", 1)[0].decode(errors="replace")
            except OSError:
                continue
            procs.append((int(d), argv0))
    out = []
    for pid, argv0 in procs:
        m = pat.match(argv0)
        if m and not os.path.isdir(m.group(1)):
            out.append(pid)
    return sorted(out)


def kill_group(pid: int) -> None:
    for sig in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGKILL):
        try:
            os.killpg(os.getpgid(pid), sig)
        except (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):
            return
        for _ in range(20):
            if not pid_alive(pid):
                return
            time.sleep(0.25)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- tasks
def parse_front_matter(text: str) -> tuple[dict, str]:
    """Tiny front-matter parser: '---' block of 'key: value' lines. Lists are
    '[a, b]' or 'a, b'. No YAML dependency."""
    meta: dict = {}
    if not text.startswith("---"):
        return meta, text
    end = text.find("\n---", 3)
    if end < 0:
        return meta, text
    block, body = text[3:end], text[end + 4:]
    for line in block.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or ":" not in line:
            continue
        k, v = line.split(":", 1)
        k, v = k.strip(), v.strip()
        if k in ("depends_on", "providers", "files", "outputs"):
            v = v.strip("[]")
            meta[k] = [x.strip().strip("'\"") for x in v.split(",") if x.strip()]
        elif k == "max_attempts":
            meta[k] = int(v)
        elif k == "max_minutes":
            meta[k] = float(v)
        else:
            meta[k] = v.strip("'\"")
    return meta, body.lstrip("\n")


def load_tasks(tasks_dir: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
    tasks: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for p in sorted(tasks_dir.glob("*.md")):
        meta, body = parse_front_matter(p.read_text())
        tid = meta.get("id") or p.stem
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+", tid):
            raise SystemExit(f"bad task id {tid!r} in {p}")
        tasks[tid] = {"id": tid, "path": str(p), "body": body.strip(), **meta}
    for t in tasks.values():
        for d in t.get("depends_on", []):
            if d not in tasks:
                raise SystemExit(f"task {t['id']} depends on unknown task {d}")
    return tasks


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- state
class State:
    def __init__(self, path: Path):
        self.path = path
        self.data = {"tasks": {}, "providers": {}}
        if path.exists():
            self.data = json.loads(path.read_text())
            self.data.setdefault("tasks", {})
            self.data.setdefault("providers", {})
            for st in self.data["tasks"].values():      # "needs-human" was renamed "stuck" (owner ruling 2026-09-25)
                if "needs_human" in st:
                    st["stuck"] = st.pop("needs_human")
        if "outcomes" not in self.data:     # merge-rate log; seeded once from the tasks' current end states
            self.data["outcomes"] = sorted(({"task": t, "status": st["status"], "at": st["finished"]}
                                            for t, st in self.data["tasks"].items()
                                            if st.get("status") in ("done", "failed") and st.get("finished")),
                                           key=lambda o: o["at"])

    def outcome(self, tid: str, status: str) -> None:
        """Log a task's end as it happens: a later reset/retest does not erase a failure from the rate."""
        self.data.setdefault("outcomes", []).append({"task": tid, "status": status, "at": now()})

    def save(self) -> None:
        atomic_write(self.path, json.dumps(self.data, indent=2, sort_keys=True))

    def task(self, tid: str) -> dict:
        return self.data["tasks"].setdefault(tid, {
            "status": "pending", "phase": None, "attempts": 0, "history": [],
            "job": None, "branch": tid, "worktree": None, "last_error": None,
        })

    def provider(self, name: str) -> dict:
        return self.data["providers"].setdefault(name, {"cooldown_until": 0, "runs": 0, "failures": 0})


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- flood
class Flood:
    def __init__(self, cfg: dict, cfg_dir: Path):
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.cfg_dir = cfg_dir
        self.cfg_file = cfg_dir / "flood.json"      # main() sets the real one; the planner's check-plan line names it
        self.repo =Path(cfg["repo"]).expanduser().resolve()
        self.main = cfg.get("main_branch", "main")
        self.wt_dir = Path(cfg.get("worktrees_dir", self.repo.parent / (self.repo.name + "-wt"))).expanduser().resolve()
        self.tasks_dir = (cfg_dir / cfg.get("tasks_dir", "tasks")).resolve()
        self.logs_dir = (cfg_dir / cfg.get("logs_dir", "flood-logs")).resolve()
        self.state = State((cfg_dir / cfg.get("state_file", "flood-state.json")).resolve())
        self.slots = int(cfg.get("slots", 2))
        # flood hands out the shared test lock itself: slot 0 is `test_lock` (the file manual runs flock on),
        # slot i is `test_lock.i`. Without test_lock every test job waits blind on its own command's flock.
        self.test_lock = cfg.get("test_lock")
        self.test_slots = int(cfg.get("test_slots", 2)) if self.test_lock else 1
        self.poll = float(cfg.get("poll_seconds", 5))
        self.providers: dict[str, dict] = cfg["providers"]
        # "reviewer": one entry or a list; each review goes to one whose model did not write the change
        rv = cfg.get("reviewer")
        self.reviewers: list[dict] = rv if isinstance(rv, list) else [rv] if rv else []
        self.rate_re = re.compile("|".join(cfg.get("rate_limit_patterns", [
            r"rate.?limit", r"\b429\b", r"quota", r"usage limit", r"overloaded"])), re.I)
        self.procs: dict[str, subprocess.Popen] = {}   # task id -> child process (this run only)
        self.fence = self.write_fence(cfg_dir / ".job-fence")
        # flood's own fetch/push authenticate through gh on the command line; nothing goes into the
        # clone's .git/config (worktrees and so fenced jobs would inherit it)
        gh = shutil.which("gh")
        self.remote_auth = ["-c", "credential.helper=", "-c", f"credential.helper=!{gh} auth git-credential"] if gh else []
        # gh takes a remote named "upstream" as its default repository over origin: after the 07Z pass added
        # upstream = can1357/oh-my-pi (OMP-401-s07, 2026-10-01), batch 217 read can1357's PR #257 as merged and
        # 28 PR creates went there. Every gh call names the push remote's repository.
        slug = gh_repo_slug(git(self.repo, "remote", "get-url", (cfg.get("push") or {}).get("remote", "origin"),
                                check=False).stdout.strip())
        if slug:
            os.environ["GH_REPO"] = slug
        self.findings_file = (cfg_dir / cfg.get("findings_file", "FINDINGS.md")).resolve()
        # flood's own code, config and gate, plus the shell rc files a job once edited (grok, ~/.zshenv,
        # 2026-09-26). No job may write them: OMP-392's implementer (deepseek, 2026-09-28 06:45Z) added a
        # check to ~/flood/oh-my-pi-test.sh from outside its worktree, unreviewed. Checked around every job.
        self.control_globs = [str(cfg_dir / g) if not g.startswith(("/", "~")) else os.path.expanduser(g)
                              for g in cfg.get("control_files", CONTROL_FILES)]
        # owner-facing symlinks no job may retarget (link -> approved target), checked by readlink after every job:
        # a launcher copy elsewhere hashes the same, so control_globs would not catch a retarget (OMP-441)
        self.global_links = {os.path.expanduser(k): os.path.expanduser(v) for k, v in cfg.get("global_links", {}).items()}
        self.rider_dir = Path(cfg.get("rider_dir", Path.home() / ".omp/agent/work-rider-batches")).expanduser()
        # the session system reads one batch per working directory: <sha256(realpath(cwd))[:16]>.json
        # (session-system/extensions/workflow/rider-batch.ts riderBatchPath); oh-my-pi sessions run in ~/oh-my-pi
        rider_cwd = os.path.realpath(os.path.expanduser(cfg.get("rider_cwd", "~/oh-my-pi")))
        self.rider_file = self.rider_dir / f"{hashlib.sha256(rider_cwd.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]}.json"
        self.rr = int(self.state.data.get("rr", 0))    # round-robin cursor, persisted so a restart continues it
        self.bench_logged = 0.0
        self.tasks = load_tasks(self.tasks_dir)
        self.wt_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.logs_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.check_repo()

    @staticmethod
    def write_fence(d: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
        """An empty gh config dir and a git config with the operator's identity only (no
        credential helpers), plus the env overrides every job gets."""
        (d / "gh").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        ident = {k: sh(["git", "config", "--global", "--get", f"user.{k}"], check=False).stdout.strip() or "flood"
                 for k in ("name", "email")}
        gitconfig = d / "gitconfig"
        gitconfig.write_text(f"[user]\n\tname = {ident['name']}\n\temail = {ident['email']}\n")
        # Bun's global bin and link dirs go to a scratch dir, so `bun link` or scripts/link-omp.sh in a job cannot
        # retarget the owner's ~/.bun/bin/omp (OMP-434's implement did, 2026-09-28; OMP-441). The package cache
        # stays shared so installs stay warm and offline.
        cache = os.environ.get("BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR") or \
            str(Path(os.environ.get("BUN_INSTALL") or Path.home() / ".bun") / "install" / "cache")
        return {"GH_CONFIG_DIR": str(d / "gh"), "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL": str(gitconfig), "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM": "1",
                "GIT_SSH_COMMAND": "/bin/false", "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT": "0",
                "BUN_INSTALL": str(d / "bun"), "BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR": cache}

    def sandbox_prefix(self, writable: list[str] = (), agent: bool = False) -> list[str]:
        return sandbox_argv(self.cfg.get("sandbox"), [str(self.cfg_dir / ".job-fence"), *writable], agent)

    # ---- ledger write-back: rider batches the owner's /summary -> /done consumes ---------------
    def rider_keys(self) -> set[str]:
        """Keys already staged or consumed in any rider batch, plus the ones flood wrote."""
        keys = set(self.state.data.get("rider_keys", []))
        for f in self.rider_dir.glob("*.json*") if self.rider_dir.is_dir() else []:
            try:
                keys |= {e["key"] for e in json.loads(f.read_text()) if isinstance(e, dict) and "key" in e}
            except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
                continue
        return keys

    def write_rider(self, entries: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> list[str]:
        """Stage (key, ref, evidence) for Chris's next /summary as one rider batch file; never the
        same key twice; only Work Ledger keys. Returns the keys written."""
        done = self.rider_keys()
        fresh, seen = [], set()
        for key, ref, evidence in entries:
            if LEDGER_KEY_RE.fullmatch(key) and key not in done and key not in seen:
                fresh.append((key, ref, evidence))
                seen.add(key)
        if not fresh:
            return []
        pending = json.loads(self.rider_file.read_text()) if self.rider_file.exists() else []   # add to it
        body = json.dumps(pending + [{"key": k, "evidence": ev} for k, _, ev in fresh], indent=2) + "\n"
        self.rider_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        atomic_write(self.rider_file, body)
        self.state.data["rider_keys"] = sorted(set(self.state.data.get("rider_keys", [])) | seen)
        self.state.save()
        for key, ref, _ in fresh:
            log(f"[ledger] {key} done ref={ref}")
        return [k for k, _, _ in fresh]

    def task_title(self, tid: str) -> str:
        body = (self.tasks.get(tid) or {}).get("body", "")
        return next((l.lstrip("# ").strip() for l in body.splitlines() if l.strip()), tid)[:100]

    def ride_merged_batch(self, n: int, pr: str, merge_sha: str, carried: list[str], upstream: str) -> None:
        ref = f"PR #{pr}"
        entries = [(t, ref, f"{ref} merged as {merge_sha[:10]} (flood batch {n}); {self.task_title(t)}") for t in carried]
        entries += self.parents_complete(upstream, f"last via {ref} ({merge_sha[:10]})")
        if self.write_rider(entries):
            self.close_delivered()

    def close_delivered(self) -> None:
        """Loop item 4: close staged rider entries in the ledger (flood.json ledger_close_cmd, operator env)."""
        cmd = self.cfg.get("ledger_close_cmd")
        if not cmd:
            return
        r = sh(["bash", "-lc", cmd], cwd=self.repo, check=False)
        out = (r.stdout + r.stderr).strip().splitlines()
        log(f"[ledger] ledger_close_cmd rc={r.returncode}: {out[-1][:200] if out else ''}")

    def post_merge(self) -> None:
        """Deploy after GitHub main moved (flood.json post_merge_cmd, run in the clone, operator env)."""
        cmd = self.cfg.get("post_merge_cmd")
        if not cmd:
            return
        r = sh(["bash", "-lc", cmd], cwd=self.repo, check=False)
        log(f"[deploy] post_merge_cmd rc={r.returncode}: {(r.stdout + r.stderr).strip().splitlines()[-1][:200] if (r.stdout + r.stderr).strip() else ''}")

    def parents_complete(self, upstream: str, how: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
        """Planned parents whose every slice is merged upstream or marked done (owner steps)."""
        def leaves(tid: str) -> list[str]:
            # a slice converted to a plan has slices of its own and a done_ref set on LOCAL completion, so only its
            # leaves say whether it reached GitHub main (2026-10-01: OMP-506 closed via an unrelated batch)
            sub = self.state.task(tid).get("slices") or []
            return [lf for sl in sub for lf in leaves(sl)] if sub else [tid]

        def delivered(lf: str) -> bool:
            t = self.state.task(lf)
            return bool(self._is_ancestor(t["merged_sha"], upstream)) if t.get("merged_sha") else bool(t.get("done_ref"))
        out = []
        # a snapshot: state.task() adds an entry for a slice with no state yet (a fresh plan's slices), and a
        # dict that grows during the loop raised and ended flood mid-ride (2026-10-13 20:47Z, batch 319)
        for tid, st in list(self.state.data["tasks"].items()):
            slices = st.get("slices") or []
            flat = [lf for sl in slices for lf in leaves(sl)]
            if slices and all(delivered(lf) for lf in flat):
                # name every merged slice's commit: a parent finished by an owner step (no commit of its own)
                # otherwise stays staged forever, since ledger close needs a commit on GitHub main (OMP-335)
                shas = [self.state.task(lf)["merged_sha"][:12] for lf in flat if self.state.task(lf).get("merged_sha")]
                merged = f"; slices merged {' '.join(shas)}" if shas else ""
                out.append((tid, how, f"all {len(slices)} slices done; {how}{merged}; {self.task_title(tid)}"))
                # package children an owner step filed (mark-done --ref "OMP-579,OMP-580"): the parent's slices
                # built them, so they close with it (2026-10-10: OMP-528..531, OMP-571..576 stayed open)
                # only a ref that is nothing but keys: free-text refs name other, open items ("run 3 failed: OMP-511")
                refs = [(self.state.task(lf).get("done_ref") or "") for lf in flat
                        if not self.state.task(lf).get("merged_sha")]
                kids = [m.group(0) for r in refs if KEY_LIST_RE.fullmatch(r) for m in LEDGER_KEY_RE.finditer(r)]
                if shas:
                    out += [(k, how, f"package child of {tid}, filed by its owner step; built by its slices{merged}")
                            for k in kids]
        return out

    def control_snapshot(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        snap = {}
        for g in self.control_globs:
            for f in sorted(glob.glob(g)):
                try:
                    snap[f] = hashlib.sha256(Path(f).read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
                except OSError:
                    continue
        return snap

    def committed_hash(self, f: str) -> str | None:
        """control_snapshot's hash of f as committed at HEAD of flood's own git repo, or None."""
        try:
            rel = Path(f).resolve().relative_to(Path(self.cfg_dir).resolve())
        except ValueError:
            return None
        r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(self.cfg_dir), "show", f"HEAD:{rel}"], capture_output=True)
        return hashlib.sha256(r.stdout).hexdigest()[:16] if r.returncode == 0 else None

    def audit_control_files(self, tid: str, phase: str, job: dict) -> None:
        """Flag control files that changed while the job ran. Jobs overlap and the operator edits these files in
        its pass, so the flag names the window, not a culprit; the operator triages it.
        Not flagged (2026-10-10, hundreds of lines per owner edit, one per running job): a change whose new content
        is committed in flood's own git repo (the owner or operator made it and recorded it), and a change already
        flagged once for another job."""
        before = job.get("control")
        if before is None:           # a job started before this check existed
            return
        after = self.control_snapshot()
        seen = self.state.data.setdefault("control_flagged", {})
        for f in sorted(set(before) | set(after)):
            if before.get(f) != after.get(f):
                if after.get(f) and after.get(f) == self.committed_hash(f):
                    continue
                if f in seen and seen[f] == after.get(f):
                    continue
                seen[f] = after.get(f)
                log(f"[{tid}] CONTROL FILE CHANGED during {phase} job: {f}")
                self._report_due = f"audit flag: {tid}"
                with open(self.findings_file, "a") as fh:
                    fh.write(f"- {now()} CONTROL FILE CHANGED during {tid} {phase} job "
                             f"({Path(job.get('log', '')).name}): {f}\n")

    def audit_global_links(self, tid: str, phase: str, job: dict) -> None:
        """Put back any global_links entry that no longer points at its approved target and record it. Like the
        control-file flag, this names the job's window, not a culprit."""
        for link, target in self.global_links.items():
            try:
                cur = os.readlink(link)
            except OSError:
                cur = None
            if cur == target:
                continue
            tmp = f"{link}.flood-repair"
            try:
                Path(tmp).unlink(missing_ok=True)
                os.symlink(target, tmp)
                os.replace(tmp, link)
                done = "restored"
            except OSError as e:
                done = f"repair failed: {e}"
            log(f"[{tid}] GLOBAL LINK CHANGED during {phase} job: {link} -> {cur}; {done} -> {target}")
            self._report_due = f"audit flag: {tid}"
            with open(self.findings_file, "a") as fh:
                fh.write(f"- {now()} GLOBAL LINK CHANGED during {tid} {phase} job ({Path(job.get('log', '')).name}): "
                         f"{link} before: {cur}; after: {target} ({done})\n")

    def audit_job(self, tid: str, phase: str, logf: str, output: str) -> None:
        """Report every line of a job's log that looks like a call to an external system (once each)."""
        st = self.state.task(tid)
        seen = set(st.get("audited", []))
        for line in external_call_lines(output):
            key = hashlib.sha256(line.strip().encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
            if key in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            log(f"[{tid}] EXTERNAL CALL: {line.strip()[:200]}")
            self._report_due = f"audit flag: {tid}"
            with open(self.findings_file, "a") as fh:
                fh.write(f"- {now()} EXTERNAL CALL in {tid} {phase} job ({Path(logf).name}): {line.strip()[:300]}\n")
        st["audited"] = sorted(seen)

    # ---- repo -----------------------------------------------------------------
    def check_repo(self) -> None:
        if not (self.repo / ".git").exists():
            raise SystemExit(f"{self.repo} is not a git repo")
        head = git(self.repo, "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD").stdout.strip()
        if head != self.main:
            raise SystemExit(f"{self.repo} is on {head!r}; check out {self.main!r} first")
        dirty = git(self.repo, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no").stdout.strip()
        if dirty:
            log(f"WARNING: {self.repo} has uncommitted tracked changes; fast-forward merges may fail")

    def worktree_path(self, tid: str) -> Path:
        return self.wt_dir / tid

    def ensure_worktree(self, tid: str) -> Path:
        wt = self.worktree_path(tid)
        if (wt / ".git").exists():
            return wt
        git(self.repo, "worktree", "prune", check=False)   # forget worktree dirs that were rm -rf'd
        branches = git(self.repo, "branch", "--list", tid).stdout.strip()
        if branches:
            r = git(self.repo, "worktree", "add", str(wt), tid, check=False)
        else:
            r = git(self.repo, "worktree", "add", "-b", tid, str(wt), self.main, check=False)
        if r.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"git worktree add failed for {tid}: {(r.stderr or r.stdout).strip()}")
        return wt

    def drop_worktree_and_branch(self, tid: str) -> None:
        self.remove_worktree(tid)
        git(self.repo, "branch", "-D", tid, check=False)

    def remove_worktree(self, tid: str) -> None:
        wt = self.worktree_path(tid)
        if wt.exists():
            git(self.repo, "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(wt), check=False)
        git(self.repo, "worktree", "prune", check=False)

    # ---- scheduling ---------------------------------------------------------------
    def max_attempts(self, task: dict) -> int:
        """Per-task max_attempts, else 3 for plan tasks (plans iterate on review), else the config default."""
        default = 3 if task.get("kind") == "plan" else self.cfg.get("max_attempts", 2)
        return int(task.get("max_attempts", default))

    def ready_tasks(self) -> list[dict]:
        out = []
        for t in self.tasks.values():
            st = self.state.task(t["id"])
            if is_owner(t) and st["status"] == "pending":     # flood never launches an owner step
                st.update(status="owner")
                self.state.save()
                log(f"[{t['id']}] {self.owner_wait(t)}")
            if st["status"] != "pending":
                continue
            if st.get("wait_main"):
                if self.state.task(st["wait_main"]).get("status") != "done" and self.red_main_fix():
                    continue
                st.pop("wait_main")
                self.state.save()
            if st.get("wait_disk"):
                if not disk_has_room():
                    continue
                st.pop("wait_disk")
                self.state.save()
            if st["attempts"] >= self.max_attempts(t) and not st.get("retest"):
                continue
            stale = self.spec_stale(t["id"])
            if stale:
                if st.get("spec_hold") != stale:
                    st["spec_hold"] = stale
                    self.state.save()
                    log(f"[{t['id']}] not started: {stale}")
                continue
            if st.pop("spec_hold", None):
                self.state.save()
            if all(self.dep_met(d) for d in t.get("depends_on", [])):
                out.append(t)
        # a fix task holds every batch (and, while main is red, every task's tests): it goes first;
        # then highest priority; sorted() is stable, so file order breaks ties
        return sorted(out, key=lambda t: (not t["id"].startswith(("fix-main-", "fix-ci-")), -self.priority(t)))

    def priority(self, t: dict) -> int:
        """Front matter `priority:` (default 0). A slice without one inherits its planned parent's."""
        if "priority" in t:
            return int(t["priority"])
        parent = next((p for p, st in self.state.data["tasks"].items() if t["id"] in (st.get("slices") or [])), None)
        return self.priority(self.tasks[parent]) if parent in self.tasks else 0

    # ---- spec revisions (owner decision 6, 2026-10-13): ledger2tasks.py writes ledger-revs.json (each item's
    # current ledger revision) and spec-sync.json (the revision its task files were last synced to). A task file
    # is never overwritten, so an amendment reaches flood only when the operator syncs it; until then the item's
    # new starts and plan promotions wait, and a PASS given against an older revision is reviewed again.
    def _spec_json(self, name: str) -> dict:
        p = self.cfg_dir / self.cfg.get(f"{name}_file", name.replace("_", "-") + ".json")
        try:
            mt = p.stat().st_mtime_ns
        except OSError:
            return {}
        cache = self.__dict__.setdefault("_spec_cache", {})
        if cache.get(name, (None,))[0] != mt:
            try:
                cache[name] = (mt, json.loads(p.read_text()))
            except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
                log(f"[spec] {p.name} unreadable, spec revisions not checked: {e}")
                cache[name] = (mt, {})
        return cache[name][1]

    def spec_binding(self, tid: str) -> dict | None:
        """{key, ledger_rev, synced_rev, task_sha256} for the ledger item a task (or slice) belongs to; None when
        flood has no revision for it (fix tasks, items never exported by the live exporter)."""
        tasks = getattr(self, "tasks", None) or {}   # oh-my-pi test harnesses build Flood without tasks
        task = tasks.get(tid) or {}
        item, cur_id = task.get("item"), tid
        while not item and not re.match(r"[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-\d+", cur_id):   # a fix task's slice inherits its `item:`
            states = getattr(getattr(self, "state", None), "data", {}).get("tasks", {})
            cur_id = next((p for p, st in states.items() if cur_id in (st.get("slices") or [])), None)
            if cur_id is None:
                break
            item = (tasks.get(cur_id) or {}).get("item")
        m = re.match(r"[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-\d+", str(item or tid))   # a fix task names its item: `item: OMP-604`
        if not m:
            return None
        key = m.group(0)
        cur = (self._spec_json("ledger_revs").get("items") or {}).get(key)
        synced = self._spec_json("spec_sync").get(key)
        if not cur:
            return None
        sha = hashlib.sha256(Path(task["path"]).read_bytes()).hexdigest() if task.get("path") and Path(task["path"]).exists() else None
        return {"key": key, "ledger_rev": cur.get("rev"), "synced_rev": (synced or {}).get("rev"), "task_sha256": sha}

    def spec_stale(self, tid: str) -> str | None:
        b = self.spec_binding(tid)
        if not b or b["synced_rev"] is None or b["ledger_rev"] is None or b["ledger_rev"] <= b["synced_rev"]:
            return None
        return (f"spec behind ledger: {b['key']} is at r{b['ledger_rev']}, its task files at r{b['synced_rev']}; "
                f"held until the operator syncs them (ledger2tasks.py --synced {b['key']})")

    def spec_recheck(self, task: dict, phase: str) -> bool:
        """At a PASS (review before merge, plan review before promotion): True when the verdict cannot be
        accepted because the spec moved. Stale: the task waits in review-wait (spec_hold) and is reviewed
        again once synced. Synced to a newer revision since the review started: reviewed again now. Uncharged."""
        tid, st = task["id"], self.state.task(task["id"])
        bound = (st.get("job") or {}).get("spec") or {}
        stale = self.spec_stale(tid)
        if stale:
            log(f"[{tid}] {phase} PASS at r{bound.get('synced_rev')} not accepted: {stale}")
            st.update(status="running", phase="review-wait",
                      job={"phase": "review-wait", "review": phase, "queued": time.time(), "spec_hold": stale})
            self.state.save()
            return True
        cur = self.spec_binding(tid)
        start = "plan-start" if phase == "plan-review" else "implement-start"
        made = next((e.get("spec") for e in reversed(st.get("history") or []) if e.get("phase") == start), None) or {}
        if cur and made.get("synced_rev") is not None and made["synced_rev"] != cur["synced_rev"]:
            # worker, reviewer and merge are bound to one revision (reviewer guidance 2026-10-13): a change written
            # against an older text goes back to its maker with the amended text, uncharged
            st["attempts"] = max(0, st["attempts"] - 1)
