            self.requeue(task, f"spec amended since this change was written: {cur['key']} task files r{made['synced_rev']} "
                               f"-> r{cur['synced_rev']}; continue the work against the amended text (no attempt charged)")
            return True
        if bound and cur and cur["synced_rev"] != bound.get("synced_rev"):
            log(f"[{tid}] {phase} PASS was given against r{bound.get('synced_rev')}; task files now synced to "
                f"r{cur['synced_rev']}: reviewing again against the amended criteria, no attempt charged")
            self.resume_review(task, phase)
            return True
        return False

    def parent_criteria(self, tid: str, key: str) -> list[str]:
        """The ledger item's acceptance list from its own task file, for a slice: a slice's text alone left the
        2026-10-13 amendments out of every first-attempt prompt (OMP-604-s02-s03-s01 merged a 3-state verdict)."""
        parent = self.tasks.get(key)
        if tid == key or not parent:
            return []
        out, inside = [], False
        for line in parent["body"].splitlines():
            if line.strip() == "Acceptance:":
                inside = True
            elif inside and line.startswith("- "):
                out.append(line)
            elif inside and out:
                break
        return out

    def spec_note(self, task: dict, judge: bool = True) -> list[str]:
        b = self.spec_binding(task["id"])
        if not b or b["synced_rev"] is None:
            return []
        crit = self.parent_criteria(task["id"], b["key"])
        return [f"Spec revision: ledger item {b['key']} r{b['synced_rev']}; the task text is synced to it.",
                *([f"The item's acceptance criteria at r{b['synced_rev']} (this task is part of it; where the task "
                   "text conflicts with them, they win unless an operator ruling in the task text says otherwise):",
                   *crit,
                   "A criterion the task text does not take on belongs to another task of the item: its absence",
                   "from this change is not a defect; a change that contradicts a criterion is."] if crit else []),
                *(["Judge against the task text as it stands now and the criteria above. Operator rulings in the",
                   "task text stand; they are not defects of the change."] if judge else []), ""]

    def owner_wait(self, t: dict) -> str:
        """What an owner slice waits for. Never 'flood can't': flood runs allowlisted commands itself,
        the hourly operator pass (flood-operator.timer, OnCalendar=hourly) runs the rest."""
        if self.owner_cmd_allowed(t):
            host = ", ".join(self.owner_hosts_left(t) or t.get("depends_on", [])) or t["id"]
            return f"owner step: flood runs `{t['owner_cmd']}` in {host} after its rebase, before its tests"
        if t["id"] in self.cfg.get("chris_steps", {}):
            return f"on REPORT.md's Deferred list: {self.cfg['chris_steps'][t['id']]}"
        reason = self.deferred_reason(t)
        if reason is not None:   # any deferred step, Chris named or not (11Z pass 2026-10-10: OMP-537-s03 read "queued")
            return f"on REPORT.md's Deferred list: {reason}"
        nxt =(dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc) + dt.timedelta(hours=1)).strftime("%H:00Z")
        return f"owner step queued for {nxt} pass"

    def deferred_reason(self, t: dict) -> str | None:
        """deferred.json's reason for the step or the ledger item it belongs to; None when it is not deferred."""
        dfile = self.findings_file.parent / "deferred.json"
        keys = json.loads(dfile.read_text()) if dfile.exists() else {}
        return next((str(r) for k, r in keys.items() if t["id"] == k or t["id"].startswith(k + "-")), None)

    def chris_step(self, t: dict) -> bool:
        """OPERATING.md "Report and mandate work": an owner slice is Chris's, never the operator's, when its body
        names him, when flood.json chris_steps lists it (a credential flood does not hold), or when it is a
        contract approval the allowlist leaves out (none since D44, 2026-09-29: flood approves every contract)."""
        if re.search(r"\bChris\b", t.get("body", "")) or t["id"] in self.cfg.get("chris_steps", {}):
            return True
        cmd = str(t.get("owner_cmd", "")).strip()
        return bool(re.fullmatch(r"omp-work approve --issue [A-Z]+-\d+", cmd)) and not self.owner_cmd_allowed(t)

    def dep_met(self, d: str) -> bool:
        """OMP-460 (owner 2026-09-29: "nothing is ever waiting on me"): a dependency is met when it is done, or
        when it is a planned parent whose only unfinished slices are Chris's leaf steps (owner slices that are his
        and that no sibling slice depends on: a check, a decision, a doctrine edit). The parent stays planned and
        its ledger item stays open until he takes the step; work built on its merged code goes ahead. A task that
        needs the step itself names that slice in depends_on and keeps waiting."""
        st = self.state.task(d)
        if st["status"] == "done":
            return True
        if st["status"] != "planned":
            return False
        slices = st.get("slices") or []
        left = [sl for sl in slices if self.state.task(sl)["status"] != "done"]
        return bool(left) and all(self.detached_chris_step(sl, slices) for sl in left)

    def detached_chris_step(self, sid: str, siblings: list[str]) -> bool:
        t = self.tasks.get(sid)
        if not t or not is_owner(t) or not self.chris_step(t):
            return False
        return not any(sid in (self.tasks.get(o) or {}).get("depends_on", []) for o in siblings if o != sid)

    def chris_holds(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """Chris's steps that can start now, each with the queued (pending) tasks that wait on nothing but
        Chris's steps and whose wait reaches this one: {step: [held task ids]}."""
        memo: dict[str, frozenset] = {}

        def roots(tid: str, trail: frozenset) -> frozenset:
            """What finally holds tid: Chris steps, or ('other', id) for anything else (a running or
            failed task, an operator step, a ready task waiting for a slot)."""
            if tid in memo:
                return memo[tid]
            t, st = self.tasks.get(tid), self.state.task(tid)
            if t and is_owner(t) and st["status"] == "owner":
                out = frozenset([tid]) if self.chris_step(t) else frozenset([("other", tid)])
            elif t and self.parked_on_chris(tid):          # tests stopped at Chris's contract approval
                out = frozenset(self.parked_on_chris(tid))
            elif st["status"] == "planned" or (st["status"] == "failed" and st.get("slices")):
                left = [sl for sl in st.get("slices") or [] if self.state.task(sl)["status"] != "done"]
                out = frozenset().union(*(roots(sl, trail | {tid}) for sl in left if sl not in trail)) if left else frozenset()
            elif st["status"] in ("pending", "blocked") and t:
                unmet = [d for d in t.get("depends_on", []) if not self.dep_met(d) and d not in trail]
                out = (frozenset().union(*(roots(d, trail | {tid}) for d in unmet)) if unmet
                       else frozenset([("other", tid)]))
            else:
                out = frozenset([("other", tid)])
            memo[tid] = out
            return out

        holds: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for tid, t in self.tasks.items():
            if self.state.task(tid)["status"] not in ("pending", "blocked") or is_owner(t):
                continue
            unmet = [d for d in t.get("depends_on", []) if not self.dep_met(d)]
            if not unmet:
                continue
            r = frozenset().union(*(roots(d, frozenset([tid])) for d in unmet))
            if r and all(isinstance(x, str) for x in r):
                for step in r:
                    holds.setdefault(step, []).append(tid)
        return {s: held for s, held in holds.items()
                if all(self.dep_met(d) or s in self.parked_on_chris(d) for d in self.tasks[s].get("depends_on", []))}

    def parked_on_chris(self, tid: str) -> list[str]:
        """Chris's approval slices a task's tests stopped at (PARKED: contract digest ... Chris's approval).
        Such a slice depends on the parked task but is the step that unblocks it, so it can start now."""
        st, t = self.state.task(tid), self.tasks.get(tid)
        if not t or st["status"] != "failed" or not str(st.get("last_error") or "").startswith(
                "tests need Chris's contract approval"):
            return []
        return [o["id"] for o in self.owner_steps(t) if self.chris_step(o)]

    def owner_hold_check(self) -> None:
        """OMP-460: flag idle slots while queued work waits only on Chris. The flag goes to flood.log and REPORT.md
        lists the step; there is no push alert (Grok Bot is no longer used, owner 2026-10-10)."""
        holds = self.chris_holds()
        idle = self.slots - self.occupied_slots()
        sig = json.dumps(holds, sort_keys=True) if holds and idle > 0 else ""
        if sig != self.state.data.get("owner_hold_sig", ""):
            self.state.data["owner_hold_sig"] = sig
            for k in ("chris_notified", "chris_alert_error"):    # state of the removed Grok Bot alert
                self.state.data.pop(k, None)
            self.state.save()
            if sig:
                n = len({t for held in holds.values() for t in held})
                log(f"[owner-hold] {idle} of {self.slots} slots idle; {n} queued task(s) wait only on Chris's steps: "
                    + "; ".join(f"{s} holds {len(h)}" for s, h in sorted(holds.items())))

    def running_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        return [tid for tid, st in self.state.data["tasks"].items() if st["status"] == "running"]

    def provider_load(self) -> dict[str, int]:
        load: dict[str, int] = {}
        for tid in self.running_ids():
            job = self.state.task(tid)["job"] or {}
            p = job.get("provider")
            if p:
                load[p] = load.get(p, 0) + 1
        return load

    def eligible_providers(self, task: dict, role: str = "implement") -> list[str]:
        wanted = task.get("providers") or ([task["provider"]] if task.get("provider") else None)
        return [n for n in self.providers if self.providers[n].get("role", "implement") == role
                and (not wanted or n in wanted)]

    def pick_provider(self, task: dict, role: str = "implement") -> str | None:
        names = self.eligible_providers(task, role)
        if not names:
            return None
        load, t = self.provider_load(), time.time()
        # a task whose implementer timed out waits for another implementer; the one that timed out is the
        # fallback only while every other eligible provider is cooling down
        avoid = self.state.task(task["id"]).get("avoid_provider")
        if avoid in names and any(self.state.provider(n)["cooldown_until"] <= t for n in names if n != avoid):
            names = [n for n in names if n != avoid]
        else:
            avoid = None
        # Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (docs/adr/0001): the subscription with the most allowance left goes first
        # (10-point buckets, round robin inside a bucket); a failed plan's next attempt prefers a maker that
        # has not written the task yet. OMP-613: no reading ranks after every known one below its stop
        # (usage_tier), and every choice is logged with its inputs (routing.jsonl, replay with choose_provider).
        tried = {family(a) for a in self.state.task(task["id"]).get("authors") or []} if role == "plan" else set()
        cands = {n: dict(self.route_inputs(self.providers[n]), tried=family(model_of(self.providers[n], n)) in tried,
                         cooling=self.state.provider(n)["cooldown_until"] > t, load=load.get(n, 0),
                         max_parallel=int(self.providers[n].get("max_parallel", 1)),
                         recent_failures=len(self.recent_failures(n)), demoted=self.demoted(n))
                 for n in names}
        cursor = self.rr
        order, chosen, skipped = choose_provider(names, cursor, cands)
        self.log_route(task["id"], role, names, cursor, cands, order, chosen, skipped, avoided=avoid)
        if chosen is None:
            return None
        self.rr = (names.index(chosen) + 1) % len(names)
        self.state.data["rr"] = self.rr
        self.state.save()
        return chosen

    # ---- subscription usage (owner ruling 2026-10-02, docs/adr/0001) ---------------------------
    def usage_status(self) -> dict:
        """{"state": fresh|stale|missing|unreadable, "age_sec": int|None} of usage.json (OMP-613)."""
        path = self.cfg_dir / "usage.json"
        try:
            age = time.time() - path.stat().st_mtime
        except OSError:
            return {"state": "missing", "age_sec": None}
        if age > self.cfg.get("usage_stale_sec", 1800):
            return {"state": "stale", "age_sec": round(age)}
        try:
            self.usage_snapshot(path)
        except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            return {"state": "unreadable", "age_sec": round(age)}
        return {"state": "fresh", "age_sec": round(age)}

    def usage_snapshot(self, path: Path) -> dict:
        mt = path.stat().st_mtime
        if getattr(self, "_usage_mt", None) != mt:
            self._usage, self._usage_mt = json.loads(path.read_text()).get("subscriptions", {}), mt
        return self._usage

    def usage(self) -> dict:
        """{subscription: {"rows": [[window, percent used]], "credits_ok": bool}} from usage.json, which
        `dashboard.py --usage-json` writes (refresh_usage). Missing, unreadable or older than usage_stale_sec = {}:
        every provider is then "unknown" (OMP-613); each change of that state is logged once as a warning."""
        st = self.usage_status()
        if st["state"] != getattr(self, "_usage_state", "fresh"):
            if st["state"] != "fresh":
                age = f" (age {st['age_sec']} s, limit {self.cfg.get('usage_stale_sec', 1800)} s)" if st["age_sec"] else ""
                log(f"[usage] WARNING usage.json is {st['state']}{age}: every provider's usage is unknown and "
                    "ranks after every provider with a reading below its stop")
            else:
                log("[usage] usage.json is fresh again")
            self._usage_state = st["state"]
        if st["state"] != "fresh":
            return {}
        return self._usage

    def usage_pct(self, entry: dict) -> float | None:
        snap = self.usage().get(entry.get("subscription") or "")
        model = model_of(entry, entry.get("provider") or "")
        rows = [p for w, p in (snap or {}).get("rows", []) if p is not None and window_applies(w, model)]
        return max(rows) if rows else None

    # ---- failure history (owner 2026-10-13, Chris: recent failures affect routing, and he hears about it) ----------
    # Quality failures of a provider's own work: its implement or plan job timed out, the tests of its change
    # failed, or the review of its change said FAIL. Rate limits and start errors bench a provider already
    # (cooldown) and are not counted. failure_demote {count, window_h} in flood.json; default 3 in 6 h.
    def demote_cfg(self) -> tuple[int, float]:
        c = self.cfg.get("failure_demote") or {}
        return int(c.get("count", 3)), float(c.get("window_h", 6))

    def recent_failures(self, provider: str) -> list[dict]:
        _, hours = self.demote_cfg()
        cut = time.time() - hours * 3600
        return [e for e in self.state.provider(provider).get("recent", []) if e["at"] >= cut]

    def demoted(self, provider: str) -> bool:
        return len(self.recent_failures(provider)) >= self.demote_cfg()[0]

    def note_failure(self, provider: str | None, kind: str, tid: str) -> None:
        if not provider:
            return
        p = self.state.provider(provider)
        was = self.demoted(provider)
        p["recent"] = [e for e in p.get("recent", []) if e["at"] >= time.time() - 86400]
        p["recent"].append({"at": time.time(), "when": now(), "kind": kind, "task": tid})
        if self.demoted(provider) and not was:
            n, hours = self.demote_cfg()
            fails = self.recent_failures(provider)
            p["demoted_at"] = now()
            log(f"[route] {provider} DEMOTED for Chris's attention: {len(fails)} failures in {hours:g} h "
                f"({', '.join(e['kind'] + ' ' + e['task'] for e in fails[-n:])}); it ranks after every provider "
                "without recent failures until they age out (REPORT.md, Provider failures)")
            self.write_report(f"provider demoted: {provider}", save=False)

    def route_inputs(self, entry: dict) -> dict:
        """The usage inputs of one routing candidate, as routing.jsonl logs them: usage = percent or "unknown"."""
        pct = self.usage_pct(entry)
        snap = self.usage().get(entry.get("subscription") or "") or {}
        return {"subscription": entry.get("subscription"), "usage": UNKNOWN if pct is None else pct,
                "stop_pct": self.cfg.get("usage_stop_pct", 95), "credits_ok": bool(snap.get("credits_ok"))}

    def usage_blocked(self, entry: dict) -> bool:
        """No new job once a window that applies to the model reaches usage_stop_pct, unless the
        subscription still runs on paid credits (owner: ChatGPT credits allowed). No reading = no stop."""
        return route_blocked(self.route_inputs(entry))

    def usage_rank(self, entry: dict) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Sort key (tier, bucket): a reading below the stop first, then unknown, then over the stop on credits.
        Before OMP-613 no reading ranked as 50 % used."""
        c = self.route_inputs(entry)
        return usage_tier(c["usage"], c["stop_pct"])

    def log_route(self, tid: str, role: str, names: list[str], cursor: int, cands: dict, order: list[str],
                  chosen: str | None, skipped: dict, avoided: str | None = None) -> None:
        """OMP-613: one JSON line per routing decision in <logs_dir>/routing.jsonl (replayable with
        choose_provider) and one flood.log line. A decision that chose nobody is logged once per change, not
        every tick. Each candidate's failure count is logged for the owner's pending decision; it does not
        affect the choice."""
        us = self.usage_status()
        rec = {"at": now(), "task": tid, "role": role, "cursor": cursor, "candidates": names,
               "inputs": {n: {**cands[n], "rank": order.index(n) + 1 if n in order else None,
                              "failures": self.state.provider(n)["failures"]} for n in names},
               "order": order, "chosen": chosen, "skipped": skipped, "avoided": avoided,
               "usage_json": us, "policy": "unknown ranks with the most allowance left; recent failures demote"}
        idle = self.__dict__.setdefault("_route_idle", {})
        if chosen is None:
            sig = json.dumps([role, names, skipped, us["state"]], sort_keys=True)
            if idle.get(tid) == sig:
                return
            idle[tid] = sig
        else:
            idle.pop(tid, None)
        try:
            with open(self.logs_dir / "routing.jsonl", "a") as fh:
                fh.write(json.dumps(rec, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
        except OSError as e:
            log(f"[{tid}] routing log not written: {e}")
        use = lambda n: UNKNOWN if cands[n]["usage"] == UNKNOWN else f"{cands[n]['usage']:g}%"
        head = (f"chose {chosen} (usage {use(chosen)}, rank {order.index(chosen) + 1} of {len(order)}, cursor {cursor})"
                if chosen else "no candidate free")
        line = f"[{tid}] route {role}: {head}; " + ", ".join(
            f"{n}={use(n)}" + (f" [{skipped[n]}]" if n in skipped else "") for n in (order or names))
        if us["state"] != "fresh":
            line += f"; WARNING usage.json {us['state']}: every usage unknown"
        log(line)

    def refresh_usage(self) -> None:
        """Start `dashboard.py --usage-json usage.json` in the background unless the last one still runs."""
        dash = self.cfg_dir / "dashboard.py"
        proc = getattr(self, "_usage_proc", None)
        if not dash.exists() or (proc and proc.poll() is None):
            return
        with open(self.logs_dir / "usage-refresh.log", "w") as fh:
            self._usage_proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, str(dash), "--usage-json", str(self.cfg_dir / "usage.json")],
                                                cwd=self.cfg_dir, stdout=fh, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                                                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)

    def pick_reviewer(self, task: dict) -> dict | None:
        """Owner rule 2026-09-26: a change is never reviewed by a model that wrote it. Round-robin over the
        reviewers whose maker (family) is not among the task's authors' makers, preferring ones not cooling down;
        among those the lowest usage_rank (OMP-613: unknown after every reading below its stop). Logged like
        pick_provider; here the cursor is review_rr and "order" lists the reviewers tied at the lowest rank."""
        wrote = {family(a) for a in self.state.task(task["id"]).get("authors") or []}
        ok = [r for r in self.reviewers if family(model_of(r, r.get("provider"))) not in wrote and not self.usage_blocked(r)]
        t = time.time()
        ready = [r for r in ok if self.state.provider(r.get("provider") or "reviewer")["cooldown_until"] <= t] or ok
        name = lambda r: r.get("provider") or "reviewer"
        # the reviewer that gave this task no verdict (a timeout, 2026-10-14 OMP-607-s01) re-runs it only alone
        avoid = self.state.task(task["id"]).get("avoid_reviewer")
        ready = [r for r in ready if name(r) != avoid] or ready
        cands = {name(r): dict(self.route_inputs(r), cooling=self.state.provider(name(r))["cooldown_until"] > t,
                               wrote=family(model_of(r, r.get("provider"))) in wrote) for r in self.reviewers}
        why = lambda c: "wrote the change" if c["wrote"] else "usage stop" if route_blocked(c) else "cooling down"
        n = int(self.state.data.get("review_rr", 0))
        if not ready:
            self.log_route(task["id"], "review", list(cands), n, cands, [], None, {k: why(c) for k, c in cands.items()})
            return None
        low = min(self.usage_rank(r) for r in ready)        # most allowance left first (owner 2026-10-02)
        ready = [r for r in ready if self.usage_rank(r) == low]
        self.state.data["review_rr"] = n + 1
        rv = ready[n % len(ready)]
        tied, okn = [name(r) for r in ready], {name(r) for r in ok}
        skipped = {}
        for k, c in cands.items():
            if k == name(rv):
                continue
            skipped[k] = (why(c) if k not in okn else "not its turn" if k in tied
                          else "cooling down" if c["cooling"] else "higher usage rank")
        self.log_route(task["id"], "review", list(cands), n, cands, tied, name(rv), skipped)
        return rv

    # ---- prompts ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def implement_prompt(self, task: dict, st: dict, wt: Path, conflicts: list[str] | None = None,
                         provider: str | None = None) -> str:
        # No full gate here: every implementer run of it took a turn on the shared test slot that flood's
        # own test phase then repeats on the commit (owner ruling 2026-09-26).
        lines = [
            "You are implementing exactly one task inside an isolated git worktree.",
            f"Work only inside this directory: {wt}",
            f"You are on branch '{task['id']}'. Do not switch branches, do not touch other worktrees, do not push.",
            "During your work, run only the test files relevant to your change (bun test <file>). Do not run the",
            "full suite or the gate script; flood runs it after you commit.",
            "Make sure what you ran passes, then commit everything with: git add -A && git commit -m \""
            + task["id"] + ": <one-line summary>\"",
            "Keep the change minimal and focused on the task. Add or update tests for what you change.",
            "Do not add files unrelated to the task. If your tooling auto-generates report, plan or verification",
            "files (for example docs/report/*, *.plan.md, verification.json), delete them before committing;",
            "an independent reviewer will reject the change if unrelated files are in the diff.",
            *self.prompt_notes(),
            *self.provider_notes(provider),
            *(["", "# Branch conflict", f"Your branch conflicts with {self.main} in: {', '.join(conflicts)}.",
               f"First run `git rebase {self.main}`, resolve the conflicts, `git rebase --continue`; then do the task."]
              if conflicts else []),
            "", f"# Task: {task['id']}", "", task["body"], "", *self.spec_note(task, judge=False),
        ]
        if st["attempts"] > 0 or st.get("last_error"):     # last_error alone: a plain reset kept the reason
            status = sh(["git", "status", "--short"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip()
            prev = (f"This is attempt {st['attempts'] + 1}. Attempt {st['attempts']} ended with:" if st["attempts"]
                    else "This task was reset for another try. The previous attempt ended with:")
            lines += [
                "# Continuation",
                f"{prev} {st.get('last_error') or 'unknown'}.",
                "The worktree already contains your earlier changes. CONTINUE from them; do not start over.",
                *([f"Owner's instruction: {st['note']}"] if st.get("note") else []),
                "Current git status --short:", status or "(clean)", "",
            ]
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def prompt_notes(self) -> list[str]:
        """Repository conventions from flood.json "prompt_notes", shown to implementer AND reviewer
        (a reviewer that does not know a convention flags the rows it requires)."""
        notes = self.cfg.get("prompt_notes") or []
        return ["", "# Repository notes", *notes, ""] if notes else []

    def provider_notes(self, provider: str | None) -> list[str]:
        """A provider entry's "prompt_notes": limits of that worker CLI, shown only to implementers running on it
        (2026-09-26: Qwen Code's shell tool hard-refuses command substitution - `$()`, `<()`, `>()` - with no
        config to allow it; 26 deepseek implement logs by 00:00Z show the refusal, several looping on it until
        the 90-minute timeout). The reviewer does not see these: they describe the tool, not the repository."""
        notes = (self.providers.get(provider) or {}).get("prompt_notes") if provider else None
        return ["", f"# Limits of your tools ({provider})", *notes, ""] if notes else []

    def owner_approval_note(self, wt: Path) -> list[str]:
        """Commits on the branch that change approval.json are the operator's owner approval of the
        new contract digest (OPERATING.md # Owner), not the implementer's work: tell the reviewer."""
        r = git(wt, "log", "--format=%h %s", f"{self.main}..HEAD", "--", APPROVAL_PATH, check=False)
        commits = [c for c in r.stdout.splitlines() if c.strip()] if r.returncode == 0 else []
        if not commits:
            return []
        return ["Owner approval commits (sanctioned, not scope violations): " + "; ".join(commits),
                "They were made by the owner, not the implementer. Their edits to approval.json, the issue",
                "key added to models.Approval.issue and schema.json, the",
                "WORK_CONTRACT_SHA256 literal in packages/work-client/src/contract.ts and the matching",
                "docs/upstream-fork-inventory.tsv rows are required for the tests to pass; a task text saying",
                "'do not touch approval.json' binds the implementer, not the owner. Judge everything else.", ""]

    def review_prompt(self, task: dict, wt: Path, diff_file: Path, test_log: str) -> str:
        return "\n".join([
            "You are an independent reviewer. You did not write this change.",
            f"Task: {task['id']}", "", task["body"], "",
            f"The full diff against '{self.main}' is in: {diff_file}",
            f"The worktree with the change checked out is: {wt} (read it, run things, but do not modify it).",
            "Test run output (tail):", "```", test_log[-4000:], "```", "",
            *self.spec_note(task),
            *self.prompt_notes(),
            *self.owner_approval_note(wt),
            "Judge: does the diff implement the task correctly and completely, with tests, without unrelated changes",
            "or damage to existing behaviour? Be concrete about defects.",
            # OMP-393 attempt 1 (2026-09-28) passed review with a stub WorkService that answered every command
            # "applied" and accepted a hardcoded bearer; the eval would have measured the stub.
            "FAIL any stub, fake or fallback that stands in for the real system the task names outside a test file",
            "(canned responses, health or readiness forced true, errors swallowed into a fake), and any credential,",
            "token or auth bypass accepted by default in non-test code.",
            "End your response with exactly one line: 'VERDICT: PASS' or 'VERDICT: FAIL'.",
        ])

    # ---- launching ----------------------------------------------------------------
    def render_cmd(self, template: list[str], **fmt: str) -> list[str]:
        return [part.format(**fmt) for part in template]

    def prompt_delivery(self, provider: str, prompt: str, pf: Path) -> tuple[str, Path | None]:
        """How a provider gets its prompt. Default: rendered into {prompt} on the command line. With
        "prompt_stdin": true the prompt file is the job's stdin and {prompt} renders as a one-line pointer,
        so no process's command line carries the prompt text: on 2026-09-25 12:10Z one implementer's
        `pkill -f <pattern>` matched text of the shared prompt inside every other job's wrapper argv and
        killed all six jobs at once (OMP-293)."""
        if self.providers[provider].get("prompt_stdin"):
            return "The task follows on stdin.", pf
        return prompt, None

    def start_event(self, tid: str, phase: str) -> dict:
        """History event for a successful plan/implement start (OMP-584-s03). Pure measurement: every count
        comes from existing helpers and nothing here decides scheduling."""
        event = {"phase": f"{phase}-start", "at": now(), "attempt": self.state.task(tid)["attempts"],
                 "code_sha256": CODE_SHA256}
        if phase == "implement":
            jobs = {t: self.state.task(t)["job"] or {} for t in self.running_ids()}
            load = self.provider_load()
            event.update(
                running_implementers=sum(1 for t, j in jobs.items() if j.get("phase") == "implement"
                                         and j.get("pid") and pid_alive(j["pid"])),
                slots=self.slots, occupied_slots=self.occupied_slots(), test_slots=self.test_slots,
                start_gap_sec=float(self.cfg.get("start_gap_sec") or 0),
                providers={n: {"max_parallel": int(self.providers[n].get("max_parallel", 1)), "load": load.get(n, 0)}
                           for n in self.eligible_providers({})})
        return event

    def spawn(self, task: dict, phase: str, provider: str | None, argv: list[str], cwd: Path,
              max_minutes: float, stdin_file: Path | None = None) -> bool:
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        attempt = st["attempts"] + (1 if phase in ("implement", "plan") else 0)
        logf = self.logs_dir / f"{task['id']}.{phase}.{attempt}.log"
        # A retest reuses its attempt's log name; this job's output starts at log_offset.
        log_offset = logf.stat().st_size if logf.exists() else 0
        fh = open(logf, "ab")
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in TERMINAL_VARS + CREDENTIAL_VARS}
        env.update(self.fence, TERM="xterm-256color", FLOOD_TASK=task["id"], FLOOD_PHASE=phase, FLOOD_WORKTREE=str(cwd))
        # The job writes its own exit code next to its log, so a flood.py restart that adopts it
        # (and so cannot wait() on it) still learns how it ended instead of re-running it.
        rc_file = logf.with_suffix(".rc")
        rc_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        # The rc wrapper stays outside the sandbox: the rc file is under ~/flood, which the job sees read-only.
        # A planner writes its slice files into tasks/proposed/<id> (under ~/flood): that one dir stays writable
        # (OMP-544 failed 3 plans on a read-only proposed dir, 2026-10-10).
        writable = [str(self.proposed_dir(task["id"]))] if phase == "plan" else []
        wrapped = ["sh", "-c", '"$@"; rc=$?; printf %s "$rc" > "$0"; exit "$rc"', str(rc_file),
                   *self.sandbox_prefix(writable, agent=phase != "test"), *argv]
        stdin = open(stdin_file, "rb") if stdin_file else subprocess.DEVNULL
        try:
            exe = argv[0] if os.path.isabs(argv[0]) or "/" not in argv[0] else str(Path(cwd) / argv[0])
            if shutil.which(exe, path=env.get("PATH")) is None:   # the sh wrapper would hide this as rc 127
                raise FileNotFoundError(2, "No such file or directory", argv[0])
            proc = subprocess.Popen(wrapped, cwd=cwd, stdout=fh, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                                    stdin=stdin, start_new_session=True, env=env)
        except OSError as e:            # e.g. the CLI is not installed / not on PATH
            fh.close()
            if stdin_file:
                stdin.close()
            msg = f"cannot start {phase} command {argv[0]!r}: {e}"
            log(f"[{task['id']}] {msg}")
            if provider:
                p = self.state.provider(provider)
                p["cooldown_until"] = time.time() + 3600
                p["failures"] += 1
            st.update(status="pending", phase=None, job=None, last_error=msg)
            self.state.save()
            return False
        fh.close()
        if stdin_file:
            stdin.close()
        self.procs[task["id"]] = proc
        self._last_start = time.time()
        st.update(status="running", phase=phase, worktree=str(self.worktree_path(task["id"])),
                  job={"pid": proc.pid, "provider": provider, "phase": phase, "argv": argv, "cwd": str(cwd),
                       "log": str(logf), "log_offset": log_offset, "rc_file": str(rc_file), "control": self.control_snapshot(),
                       "started": time.time(), "deadline": time.time() + max_minutes * 60,
                       "budget": max_minutes * 60, "spec": self.spec_binding(task["id"])})
        if phase in ("implement", "plan"):
            st["attempts"] = attempt
            st["maker_provider"] = provider
            model = model_of(self.providers.get(provider) or {}, provider)
            if model and model not in st.setdefault("authors", []):
                st["authors"].append(model)
        if provider:
            self.state.provider(provider)["runs"] += 1
        if phase in ("implement", "plan"):
            # no "spec" key without a binding: oh-my-pi's test_flood_start_metrics.py pins the plain event shape
            st["history"].append({**self.start_event(task["id"], phase),
                                  **({"spec": st["job"]["spec"]} if st["job"]["spec"] else {})})
        self.state.save()
        log(f"[{task['id']}] {phase} started pid={proc.pid} provider={provider} log={logf.name}")
        return True

    # ---- planner: kind: plan tasks split an item into implement slices ------------------------
    def proposed_dir(self, tid: str) -> Path:
        return self.tasks_dir / "proposed" / tid

    def plan_worktree(self, tid: str) -> Path:
        return self.wt_dir / f"{tid}--plan"

    def fresh_plan_worktree(self, tid: str) -> Path:
        wt = self.plan_worktree(tid)
        if wt.exists():
            git(self.repo, "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(wt), check=False)
        git(self.repo, "worktree", "prune", check=False)
        r = git(self.repo, "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(wt), self.main, check=False)
        if r.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"git worktree add failed for {tid} plan: {(r.stderr or r.stdout).strip()}")
        return wt

    def prior_findings(self, tid: str, limit: int = 6000) -> str:
        """Review findings from this item's earlier implement attempts (review logs + last_error)."""
        parts = []
        for f in sorted(self.logs_dir.glob(f"{tid}.review.*.log")) + sorted(self.logs_dir.glob(f"{tid}.plan-review.*.log")):
            lines = [l for l in f.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines() if l.strip()]
            cut = next((i for i in range(len(lines) - 1, -1, -1) if VERDICT_RE.match(lines[i])), len(lines))
            body = lines[max(0, cut - 45):cut + 1]
            half = len(body) // 2                     # codex prints its final message twice
            if half and body[:half] == body[half:2 * half]:
                body = body[:half]
            parts.append(f"## {f.name}\n" + "\n".join(body))
        return "\n\n".join(parts)[-limit:]

    def start_plan(self, task: dict, provider: str) -> bool:
        tid, st = task["id"], self.state.task(task["id"])
        wt = self.fresh_plan_worktree(tid)
        pdir = self.proposed_dir(tid)
        makers = {family(model_of(r, r.get("provider"))) for r in self.reviewers}
        wrote = {family(a) for a in st.get("authors") or []} | {family(model_of(self.providers[provider], provider))}
        if makers and makers <= wrote:   # this draft would leave no reviewer: start it blank (OMP-544, 6 makers)
            shutil.rmtree(pdir, ignore_errors=True)
            st["authors"] = []
            log(f"[{tid}] every reviewer's maker drafted this plan: drafts cleared, the next plan starts blank")
        pdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        st["plan_base"] = git(self.repo, "rev-parse", self.main).stdout.strip()
        prompt = self.plan_prompt(task, st, wt, pdir)
        pf = self.logs_dir / f"{tid}.plan-prompt.{st['attempts'] + 1}.md"
        pf.write_text(prompt)
        prompt_arg, stdin_file = self.prompt_delivery(provider, prompt, pf)
        argv = self.render_cmd(self.providers[provider]["cmd"], worktree=str(wt), prompt_file=str(pf),
                               prompt=prompt_arg, task=tid)
        return self.spawn(task, "plan", provider, argv, wt, float(task.get("max_minutes", 60)), stdin_file=stdin_file)

    def plan_prompt(self, task: dict, st: dict, wt: Path, pdir: Path) -> str:
        tid = task["id"]
        lines = [
            "You are planning, not implementing. Split the work item below into small implementation slices",
            "that independent agents can each finish in one sitting (at most 90 minutes).",
            f"This directory is a fresh checkout of {self.main}: {wt}. Read the code; do not modify anything here.",
            f"Write each slice as its own file {pdir}/{tid}-sNN.md (s01, s02, ...) and write nothing else anywhere.",
            "Slice file format:", "```", "---", f"id: {tid}-sNN", f"depends_on: [{tid}-s01]   # only ids from this set",
            "max_minutes: 90                # at most 90", "kind: implement", "---",
            "<body, at most 2000 characters>", "```",
            "Every body must contain: what to change; a line \"Done when:\" followed by observable, testable",
            "conditions; the test file(s) to add or extend, by path; and a \"Do not touch:\" list.",
            "Rules: at most 8 slices. Each slice must be implementable and verifiable from its own text alone.",
            "No slice may edit an existing test unless its body names that test and says why.",
            "The \"Do not touch\" list never includes docs/upstream-fork-inventory.tsv: every slice updates its own rows.",
            "Any step only the owner can do (contract approvals, credentials, external systems such as GitHub",
            "settings, services, deployments) goes in its own owner slice: add `owner: true` to its front matter;",
            "its body has \"Owner runs:\" with the exact commands, \"Evidence:\" naming what to pass to",
            "`flood.py mark-done <id> --ref`, and \"Done when:\". Only slices that use the owner step's result depend on it.",
            "A check, choice or sign-off that no later slice needs gets no dependents, so the rest of the work (and",
            "work built on this item) goes ahead while it waits (OMP-460). Implementer slices never pause or wait for the owner.",
            "A contract approval is an owner slice with `owner_cmd: omp-work approve --issue <KEY>` in its front",
            "matter that depends ONLY on the one implement slice changing the contract: flood itself runs it in that",
            "slice's worktree before its tests (hash, approve, contract.ts digest, inventory) and marks it done at",
            "merge. Do not add a separate slice to sync contract.ts. Flood runs no other owner slice.",
            "Implement the item as specified. Where the spec is ambiguous, take the narrower reading and list each",
            "assumption under '# Assumptions' at the top of s01. Do not add capabilities, recovery paths or actors",
            "the spec does not name; put them under '# Deferred' (also in s01) instead.",
            "Every implementer slice lists the files it edits in its front matter as `files: [path, path]`.",
            "Two slices that edit the same file must be ordered by depends_on. Only the last slice (the one that",
            "depends on every other slice) touches a changelog.",
            "Slices without a dependency run at the same time, and each dependency waits for the other slice's",
            "full test run and merge. Add a depends_on only when the slices edit the same file or one uses",
            "something the other creates; otherwise leave depends_on empty. Do not chain slices just for order.",
            "For a slice that uses something another creates, its text names that file or output with a verb",
            "outside its Do not touch, Assumptions and Deferred lists: 'reads src/x.ts', 'imports', 'consumes', 'extends'.",
            f"Before you finish, run `python3 {Path(__file__).resolve()} check-plan {tid} --config {self.cfg_file}`",
            "(the same format check flood applies to your files) and fix every line it prints until it prints OK.",
            "Together the slices must cover the whole item. Earlier one-sitting attempts at this item failed",
            "review; plan around the defects listed below.",
            *self.prompt_notes(),
            *(["This item fixes a red main. Each slice is tested alone on that red main and must pass the full",
               "gate, so every fix that one test or gate check needs goes into one slice; split only causes that",
               "different tests check (fix-ci-89ddee83a8, 2026-10-11)."] if tid.startswith(("fix-main-", "fix-ci-")) else []),
            "", f"# Item {tid}", "", task["body"], "", *self.spec_note(task, judge=False),
        ]
        findings = self.prior_findings(tid)
        if findings:
            lines += ["# Review findings from earlier implementation attempts", "", findings, ""]
        # only after a real planning attempt (also one before a reset); implement failures arrive via the findings
        if st["attempts"] > 0 or any(h.get("phase") in ("plan-gate", "plan-review") for h in st.get("history", [])):
            lines += ["# Continuation", f"The previous planning attempt ended with: {st.get('last_error') or 'unknown'}",
                      f"Your earlier slice files are still in {pdir}; fix them rather than starting over.",
                      *([f"Owner's instruction: {st['note']}"] if st.get("note") else []), ""]
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def check_plan(self, tid: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[dict]]:
        """The plan gate on the proposed slices; `flood.py check-plan` gives the planner the same check."""
        return validate_slices(tid, self.proposed_dir(tid), is_union=lambda fp: sh(
            ["git", "check-attr", "merge", "--", fp], cwd=self.repo, check=False).stdout.strip().endswith(": union"))

    def plan_rate_limited(self, task: dict, output: str) -> bool:
        """A planner out of quota exits non-zero with a limit error and writes nothing. Before, after_plan ran
        the gate on the drafts of an earlier attempt: kimi-planner's weekly-limit 403 (2026-10-14 06:44Z) charged
        OMP-604-s02-s04 a failed gate and sent OMP-607-s01's old drafts to review again (FAIL, charged). Bench
        the planner, charge nothing, plan again on another one. Only a failed run's tail is read."""
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        provider = (st["job"] or {}).get("provider")
        if not provider or not self.rate_re.search(output[-3000:]):
            return False
        cool = int(self.providers.get(provider, {}).get("cooldown_sec", 900))
        self.state.provider(provider)["cooldown_until"] = time.time() + cool
        self.state.provider(provider)["failures"] += 1
        st["attempts"] -= 1
        self.requeue(task, f"planner {provider} rate-limited; cooldown {cool}s, no attempt charged")
        return True

    def after_plan(self, task: dict) -> None:
        tid, st = task["id"], self.state.task(task["id"])
        wt = self.plan_worktree(tid)
        violations, slices = self.check_plan(tid)
        dirty = sh(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip()
        head = sh(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip()
        if dirty or head != st.get("plan_base"):
            violations.append("the planner changed the repository checkout; it may only write slice files")
        st["history"].append({"phase": "plan-gate", "ok": not violations, "at": now(), "attempt": st["attempts"]})
        if violations:
            self.requeue(task, "plan gate failed:\n- " + "\n- ".join(violations))
            return
        log(f"[{tid}] plan gate passed: {len(slices)} slices")
        self.start_plan_review(task)

    def start_plan_review(self, task: dict) -> None:
        if not self.reviewers:
            self.plan_passed(task)
            return
        tid = task["id"]
        rv = self.pick_reviewer(task)
        if not rv:
            self.requeue(task, "no reviewer on a model other than the planner's")
            return
        if self.reviewer_benched(rv):
            self.hold_review(task, "plan-review")
            return
        pdir, wt = self.proposed_dir(tid), self.plan_worktree(tid)
        slice_text = "\n\n".join(f"--- {f.name} ---\n{f.read_text(errors='replace')}" for f in sorted(pdir.glob("*.md")))
        prompt = "\n".join([
            "You are an independent reviewer of an implementation plan. You did not write it.",
            f"The worktree {wt} is a fresh checkout of {self.main} (read it, do not modify it).",
            *self.prompt_notes(),
            "", f"# Item {tid}", "", task["body"], "", *self.spec_note(task), f"# Proposed slices ({pdir})", "", slice_text, "",
            "Judge coverage against the spec AND the stated assumptions (under '# Assumptions' in s01). Do not fail",
            "a plan for omitting something listed under '# Deferred'; do fail it if an assumption contradicts the spec.",
            "Implementers have no credentials and no access outside the worktree. Steps that need them (hosted CI",
            "runs, GitHub, outside or owner reviews, deployments, credentials, provenance records kept elsewhere)",
            "belong in owner slices or under '# Deferred'. A plan that leaves such a step out of implementer slices",
            "is not incomplete for that reason; do not fail it for that.",
            "Answer concretely: (1) does the union of the slices cover the item's spec, and what is missing?",
            "(2) is each slice independently implementable and verifiable from its own text alone?",
            "End your response with exactly one line: 'VERDICT: PASS' or 'VERDICT: FAIL'.",
        ])
        pf = self.logs_dir / f"{tid}.plan-review-prompt.{self.state.task(tid)['attempts']}.md"
        pf.write_text(prompt)
        argv = self.render_cmd(rv["cmd"], worktree=str(wt), prompt_file=str(pf), prompt=prompt,
                               diff_file=str(pdir), task=tid)
        if not self.spawn(task, "plan-review", rv.get("provider"), argv, wt, float(rv.get("max_minutes", 30))):
            self.requeue(task, self.state.task(tid)["last_error"] or "could not start plan reviewer")

    def after_plan_review(self, task: dict, output: str) -> None:
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        m = VERDICT_RE.findall(output)
        verdict = m[-1].upper() if m else None
        st["history"].append({"phase": "plan-review", "verdict": verdict, "at": now(), "attempt": st["attempts"],
                              "spec": (st.get("job") or {}).get("spec")})
        if verdict is None and self.review_rate_limited(task, output, "plan-review"):
            return
        if verdict is None and not st.get("no_verdict_rerun"):          # reviewer defect: see after_review
            st["no_verdict_rerun"] = True
            st["avoid_reviewer"] = (st.get("job") or {}).get("provider")
            log(f"[{task['id']}] plan review gave no verdict (reviewer defect); re-running it, no attempt charged")
            self.start_plan_review(task)
            return
        st.pop("no_verdict_rerun", None)
        st.pop("avoid_reviewer", None)
        if verdict == "PASS" and self.spec_recheck(task, "plan-review"):
            return
        if verdict == "PASS":
            self.plan_passed(task)
            return
        lines = [l for l in output.strip().splitlines() if l.strip()]
        self.requeue(task, f"plan review {verdict or 'gave no verdict'}: {review_gist(lines, verdict)[:120]}\n"
                     + "\n".join(lines[-25:]))

    def plan_passed(self, task: dict) -> None:
        tid, st = task["id"], self.state.task(task["id"])
        if self.cfg.get("plan_promotion", "auto") == "auto":
            self.promote_plan(task)
            return
        st.update(status="plan_ready", phase=None, job=None)
        self.state.save()
        log(f"[{tid}] plan ready: slices in {self.proposed_dir(tid)}; promote with `flood.py promote {tid}`")

    def promote_plan(self, task: dict) -> None:
        tid, st = task["id"], self.state.task(task["id"])
        stale = self.spec_stale(tid)
        if stale:
            log(f"[{tid}] promotion held: {stale}; the plan is reviewed again against the amended spec after sync")
            st.update(status="running", phase="review-wait",
                      job={"phase": "review-wait", "review": "plan-review", "queued": time.time(), "spec_hold": stale})
            self.state.save()
            return
        violations, _ = self.check_plan(tid)
        if violations:
            st.update(status="plan_ready", phase=None, job=None,
                      last_error="plan gate failed:\n- " + "\n- ".join(violations))
            self.state.save()
            return
        pdir = self.proposed_dir(tid)
        files = sorted(pdir.glob("*.md"))
        clash = [f.name for f in files if (self.tasks_dir / f.name).exists()]
        if clash:
            st.update(status="plan_ready", phase=None, job=None, last_error=f"promotion blocked: tasks/ already has {clash}")
            self.state.save()
            log(f"[{tid}] promotion blocked: tasks/ already has {', '.join(clash)}")
            return
        for f in files:
            old = self.state.data["tasks"].get(f.stem)
            if old:      # state of a dropped plan's slice with the same id: its status (OMP-612-s02 "owner") and
                job = old.get("job") or {}          # branch (OMP-612-s01) must not carry over to the new slice
                if job.get("pid"):
                    kill_group(int(job["pid"]))
                self.forget(f.stem)
                log(f"[{tid}] {f.stem}: state, branch and worktree of the earlier plan's slice dropped")
            shutil.move(str(f), str(self.tasks_dir / f.name))
        (pdir / "PROMOTE").unlink(missing_ok=True)
        st.update(status="planned", phase=None, job=None, slices=[f.stem for f in files], planned_at=now())
        self.state.save()
        git(self.repo, "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(self.plan_worktree(tid)), check=False)
        self.tasks = load_tasks(self.tasks_dir)
        log(f"[{tid}] planned: promoted {len(files)} slices ({', '.join(f.stem for f in files)})")
        self.write_report(f"plan promoted: {tid}")

    def settle_plans(self) -> None:
        """Promote approved plans; a planned parent is done when all its slices are, failed if one fails."""
        for tid, task in list(self.tasks.items()):
            st = self.state.task(tid)
            if st["status"] == "plan_ready" and (self.proposed_dir(tid) / "PROMOTE").exists():
                self.promote_plan(task)
            if st["status"] != "planned":
                continue
            states = [self.state.task(sl)["status"] for sl in st.get("slices", [])]
            if states and all(x == "done" for x in states):
                last = max(st["slices"], key=lambda sl: self.state.task(sl).get("finished", ""))
                st.update(status="done", done_ref=f"slices; last {last} {str(self.state.task(last).get('merged_sha', ''))[:12]}",
                          finished=now())
                self.state.save()
                log(f"[{tid}] DONE: all {len(states)} slices done")
                self.write_report(f"parent completed: {tid}")
            elif any(x in ("failed", "blocked") for x in states):
                bad = [sl for sl in st["slices"] if self.state.task(sl)["status"] in ("failed", "blocked")]
                st.update(status="failed", last_error=f"slice(s) failed: {', '.join(bad)}")
                self.state.save()
                log(f"[{tid}] FAILED: slice(s) {', '.join(bad)} failed")

    def rebase_onto_main(self, wt: Path, task: dict | None = None) -> list[str] | None:
        """Replay the worktree's branch on current local main. None on success; otherwise the
        rebase is aborted and the conflicted files (or the failure text) are returned. With a task, a
        conflict confined to the generated contract files is repaired (repair_derived_rebase)."""
        tip = sh(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip()
        rb = sh(["git", "-c", "user.name=flood", "-c", "user.email=flood@localhost", "rebase", self.main],
                cwd=wt, check=False)
        if rb.returncode == 0:
            self.drop_stamp_only(task, wt)
            return None
        files = sh(["git", "diff", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=U"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.split()
        if task and files and (self.repair_derived_rebase(task, wt, files, tip) or self.repair_stamp_rebase(task, wt)):
            self.drop_stamp_only(task, wt)
            return None
        if rebase_in_progress(wt):
            sh(["git", "rebase", "--abort"], cwd=wt, check=False)
        sh(["git", "reset", "-q", "--hard", tip], cwd=wt, check=False)
        return files or [(rb.stdout + rb.stderr).strip().splitlines()[-1][:200] if (rb.stdout + rb.stderr).strip() else "?"]

    def repair_derived_rebase(self, task: dict, wt: Path, files: list[str], tip: str) -> bool:
        """A rebase that conflicts only in the generated contract files (flood.json rebase_repair.derived:
        approval.json, contract.ts, schema.json, api-schema.json) is the "two contract changes in flight"
        case of OPERATING.md # Owner: whichever rebases second takes main's copies, regenerates the schemas
        and is approved again for its own item. Before (OMP-266-s03 attempt 2, OMP-266-s04 14:54Z) that
        conflict burned attempts and re-plans, and the implementer resolved it by hand-writing approval.json.
        Only when the branch itself carries an approval for the task's item; anything else is a real conflict."""
        rep = self.cfg.get("rebase_repair") or {}
        derived = set(rep.get("derived", []))
        m = re.match(r"([A-Z]+-\d+)", task["id"])
        if not derived or not m or any(f not in derived for f in files):
            return False
        issue = m[1]
        shown = sh(["git", "show", f"{tip}:{APPROVAL_PATH}"], cwd=wt, check=False)
        try:
            branch_issue = json.loads(shown.stdout).get("issue") if shown.returncode == 0 else None
        except ValueError:
            branch_issue = None
        if branch_issue != issue:
            return False
        taken = []
        while rebase_in_progress(wt):
            cur = sh(["git", "diff", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=U"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.split()
            if not cur or any(f not in derived for f in cur):
                return False
            for f in cur:                                  # --ours during a rebase = the upstream side = main
                if sh(["git", "checkout", "--ours", "--", f], cwd=wt, check=False).returncode != 0:
                    return False
            sh(["git", "add", "--", *cur], cwd=wt, check=False)
            taken.extend(f for f in cur if f not in taken)
            env = {**os.environ, "GIT_EDITOR": "true"}
            r = subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "user.name=flood", "-c", "user.email=flood@localhost", "rebase", "--continue"],
                               cwd=wt, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
            if r.returncode != 0 and not sh(["git", "diff", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=U"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip():
                return False
        for cmd in rep.get("regen", []):
            r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-lc", cmd], cwd=wt, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
            if r.returncode != 0:
                log(f"[{task['id']}] rebase repair: `{cmd}` failed: {(r.stdout + r.stderr).strip()[-300:]}")
                return False
        gw = self.cfg.get("owner_gateway")       # the automation user: approvals come from the owner-action gateway
        err = run_owner_cmd(f"omp-work approve --issue {issue}", wt, gw) if gw else \
            run_owner_cmd(f"omp-work approve --issue {issue}", wt)
        if err:
            log(f"[{task['id']}] rebase repair: approval failed: {err[-300:]}")
            return False
        for post in self.cfg.get("owner_cmd_post", []):
            r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-lc", post], cwd=wt, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
            if r.returncode != 0:
                log(f"[{task['id']}] rebase repair: `{post}` failed: {(r.stdout + r.stderr).strip()[-300:]}")
                return False
        if sh(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip():
            sh(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=wt)
            sh(["git", "-c", "user.name=flood-owner", "-c", "user.email=flood@localhost", "commit", "-q", "-m",
                f"{task['id']}: re-approve contract for {issue} after rebase (flood rebase_repair)"], cwd=wt)
        log(f"[{task['id']}] rebase repaired: took {self.main}'s {', '.join(taken)}, regenerated and re-approved for {issue}")
        return True

    def repair_stamp_rebase(self, task: dict, wt: Path) -> bool:
        """A rebase conflict where the replayed commit changes each conflicted file only in its report stamp
        (STAMP_LINE_RE: the "generatedAt"/"Generated:" lines of docs/report) loses nothing when main's copy is
        taken. Branches stamped by an owner plugin hook before SANDBOX_NO_HOOKS conflicted in turn as each
        stamp merged (2026-10-10). Anything else is a real conflict: False, and the caller aborts."""
        taken = []
        while rebase_in_progress(wt):
            cur = sh(["git", "diff", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=U"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.split()
            if not cur or not all(stamp_only_change(wt, "REBASE_HEAD^", "REBASE_HEAD", f) for f in cur):
                return False
            for f in cur:                                  # --ours during a rebase = the upstream side = main
                if sh(["git", "checkout", "--ours", "--", f], cwd=wt, check=False).returncode != 0:
                    return False
            sh(["git", "add", "--", *cur], cwd=wt, check=False)
            taken.extend(f for f in cur if f not in taken)
            env = {**os.environ, "GIT_EDITOR": "true"}
            r = subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "user.name=flood", "-c", "user.email=flood@localhost", "rebase", "--continue"],
                               cwd=wt, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
            if r.returncode != 0 and not sh(["git", "diff", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=U"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip():
                return False
        log(f"[{task['id']}] rebase repaired: took {self.main}'s {', '.join(taken)} (stamp-only change)")
        return True

    def drop_stamp_only(self, task: dict | None, wt: Path) -> None:
        """After a rebase, a branch whose whole change to a docs/report file is its stamp takes main's copy back,
        and main's inventory row for it: a merged stamp only makes the next stamped branch conflict, and a stamp
        left on the branch makes its inventory row stale in the tests (OMP-569-s02, 2026-10-10)."""
        names = sh(["git", "diff", "--name-only", self.main, "HEAD", "--", "docs/report/"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.split()
        drop = [f for f in names if stamp_only_change(wt, self.main, "HEAD", f)]
        if not drop:
            return
        sh(["git", "checkout", self.main, "--", *drop], cwd=wt, check=False)
        inv = Path(wt, INVENTORY_PATH)
        shown = sh(["git", "show", f"{self.main}:{INVENTORY_PATH}"], cwd=wt, check=False)
        if inv.exists() and shown.returncode == 0:
            main_rows = {ln.split("\t", 1)[0]: ln for ln in shown.stdout.splitlines()}
            lines = inv.read_text().splitlines()
            new = [main_rows.get(ln.split("\t", 1)[0], ln) if ln.split("\t", 1)[0] in drop else ln for ln in lines]
            if new != lines:
                inv.write_text("\n".join(new) + "\n")
        sh(["git", "add", "-A", "--", *drop, *([INVENTORY_PATH] if inv.exists() else [])], cwd=wt, check=False)
        sh(["git", "-c", "user.name=flood", "-c", "user.email=flood@localhost", "commit", "-q", "-m",
            f"{(task or {}).get('id', 'flood')}: drop stamp-only change to {', '.join(drop)} (flood)"], cwd=wt, check=False)
        log(f"[{(task or {}).get('id', '-')}] dropped stamp-only change: {', '.join(drop)}")

    def start_implement(self, task: dict) -> bool:
        provider = self.pick_provider(task, task_role(task))
        if not provider:
            return False
        if task.get("kind") == "plan":
            return self.start_plan(task, provider)
        wt = self.ensure_worktree(task["id"])
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        conflicts = self.rebase_onto_main(wt, task)  # start every attempt from current main when it can
        prompt = self.implement_prompt(task, st, wt, conflicts, provider=provider)
        pf = self.logs_dir / f"{task['id']}.prompt.{st['attempts'] + 1}.md"
        pf.write_text(prompt)
        prompt_arg, stdin_file = self.prompt_delivery(provider, prompt, pf)
        argv = self.render_cmd(self.providers[provider]["cmd"], worktree=str(wt), prompt_file=str(pf),
                               prompt=prompt_arg, task=task["id"])
        max_min = float(task.get("max_minutes", self.cfg.get("default_max_minutes", 90)))
        return self.spawn(task, "implement", provider, argv, wt, max_min, stdin_file=stdin_file)

    # ---- test slots and the gate-result cache ----------------------------------------
    def slot_path(self, i: int) -> str:
        return self.test_lock if i == 0 else f"{self.test_lock}.{i}"

    def slotted(self, cmd: str | None) -> str | None:
        """The command without its `flock <test_lock>` prefix when flood schedules it on a test slot, else None."""
        prefix = f"flock {self.test_lock} "
        return cmd[len(prefix):] if self.test_lock and cmd and cmd.startswith(prefix) else None

    def gate_sha(self, cmd: str) -> str | None:
        """Identity of the gate itself: the command plus every script in `gate_scripts`. None: caching is off."""
        scripts = self.cfg.get("gate_scripts")
        if not scripts:
            return None
        h = hashlib.sha256(cmd.encode())
        for s in scripts:
            h.update((self.cfg_dir / s).read_bytes())
        return h.hexdigest()

    def tree_of(self, cwd: str | Path, rev: str = "HEAD") -> str:
        return sh(["git", "rev-parse", f"{rev}^{{tree}}"], cwd=cwd, check=False).stdout.strip()

    @staticmethod
    def qualified_subset(logf: str | None) -> bool:
        """The run took the installed-qualification subset, or was a task-scoped run (`gate scope: task`, the
        exact line), or its log is gone and cannot show otherwise."""
        try:
            text = Path(logf or "").read_text(errors="replace")
        except OSError:
            return True
        return QUALIFY_SUBSET in text or TASK_SCOPE in text.splitlines()

    def cache_get(self, tree: str, cmd: str) -> dict | None:
        """A green result for this exact tree and gate, or None. Red results never skip a run (flaky)."""
        gsha = tree and self.gate_sha(cmd)
        hit = gsha and self.state.data.get("gate_cache", {}).get(f"{tree}:{gsha}")
        return hit if hit and hit.get("ok") else None

    def cache_put(self, tree: str | None, cmd: str | None, ok: bool, logf: str | None) -> None:
        gsha = tree and cmd and self.gate_sha(cmd)
        if not gsha:
            return
        cache = self.state.data.setdefault("gate_cache", {})
        cache[f"{tree}:{gsha}"] = {"ok": ok, "at": now(), "log": logf}
        for k in list(cache)[:-500]:              # ponytail: keep the newest 500 results, plenty for a day's merges
            del cache[k]

    def start_test(self, task: dict) -> None:
        """Every test run goes through here (first run, retry, lost-rc rerun, retest). A run on the shared
        test slot waits in flood's own queue (phase test-wait) and schedule_tests starts it; anything else
        runs now."""
        if self.slotted(task.get("test") or self.cfg.get("default_test")) is not None:
            st = self.state.task(task["id"])
            st.update(status="running", phase="test-wait", job={"phase": "test-wait", "queued": time.time()})
            self.state.save()
            log(f"[{task['id']}] tests queued for a test slot")
            return
        self.run_test(task, None)

    def run_test(self, task: dict, slot: int | None) -> bool:
        """Start one test run (on `slot` when given). False when it used no slot: requeued, or a cache hit."""
        wt = self.worktree_path(task["id"])
        # test what would actually merge: the branch replayed on current local main, not the main it started from
        self.discard_test_leftovers(task["id"], wt)
        before = sh(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip()
        conflicts = self.rebase_onto_main(wt, task)
        if conflicts:
            self.requeue(task, f"rebase conflict with {self.main} before tests in: {', '.join(conflicts)}")
            return False
        self.repair_after_test_rebase(task, wt, before)
        self.run_pre_test_repairs(task, wt)
        err = self.run_owner_cmds(task, wt)
        if err:
            self.requeue(task, err)
            return False
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        test_cmd = task.get("test") or self.cfg.get("default_test")
        if not test_cmd:
            st["job"] = {"phase": "test", "skipped": True}
            self.after_test(task, ok=True, output="(no test command configured)")
            return False
        cmd = self.slotted(test_cmd) or test_cmd
        tree = self.tree_of(wt)
        hit = self.cache_get(tree, cmd)
        if hit:
            log(f"[{task['id']}] tests skipped: tree {tree[:12]} already passed this gate at {hit['at']}")
            st["job"] = {"phase": "test", "cached": True}
            try:
                tail = Path(hit["log"]).read_text(errors="replace")[-3000:]
            except (OSError, TypeError):
                tail = ""
            self.after_test(task, ok=True, output=f"(this exact tree passed the same gate at {hit['at']}; "
                                                  f"log {hit['log']})\n{tail}")
            return False
        run = cmd if slot is None else f"flock -n -E {SLOT_TAKEN} {shlex.quote(self.slot_path(slot))} {cmd}"
        if not self.spawn(task, "test", None, ["bash", "-lc", run], wt, float(self.cfg.get("test_max_minutes", 20))):
            self.requeue(task, st["last_error"] or "could not start tests")
            return False
        st["job"].update(slot=slot, tree=tree, cmd=cmd)
        self.state.save()
        return True

    def schedule_tests(self) -> None:
        """Hand free test slots out by priority: pre-batch gate, then retests of tasks a gate bug failed,
        then priority >= 10 (and fix tasks), then everyone else in arrival order. The gate goes first only
        when no task waits or it has waited gate_max_wait_min (default 45); before that it takes a slot
        left over after every waiting task (owner 2026-09-28: it ran 36x/day ahead of the queue). A slot
        held by a run flood did not start is skipped; no second run starts while the 1-minute load exceeds the cores."""
        if not self.test_lock:
            return
        b = self.state.data.get("batch") or {}
        g = b.get("gate") or {}
        ours = {(self.state.task(t)["job"] or {}).get("slot") for t in self.running_ids()}
        if g.get("pid") and "ok" not in g:
            ours.add(g.get("slot"))
        free = [i for i in range(self.test_slots) if i not in ours and slot_free(self.slot_path(i))]
        busy = self.test_slots - len(free)
        waiting = sorted((t for t in self.running_ids() if self.state.task(t).get("phase") == "test-wait" and t in self.tasks),
                         key=lambda t: (not self.state.task(t).get("gate_bug"),
                                        not (self.priority(self.tasks[t]) >= 10 or t.startswith(("fix-main-", "fix-ci-"))),
                                        (self.state.task(t)["job"] or {}).get("queued", 0)))
        want = bool(b.get("gate_want"))
        aged = want and (not waiting or time.time() - b.get("gate_want_at", 0) >= 60 * float(self.cfg.get("gate_max_wait_min", 45)))
        for tid in ([None] if aged else []) + waiting + ([None] if want and not aged else []):
            if not free or not self.start_gap_open():
                return
            if tid is None and not disk_has_room():   # a gate on a full /tmp only fails again (11:46Z 2026-10-10)
                if time.time() - getattr(self, "_gate_room_said", 0) > 1800:   # it waited silently 00:51-02Z 2026-10-14
                    self._gate_room_said = time.time()
                    log("[batch] pre-batch gate waits: /tmp has under 25 % of its space or inodes free; task tests go first")
                continue
            if busy and os.getloadavg()[0] > (os.cpu_count() or 1):
                if time.time() - getattr(self, "_load_said", 0) > 300:
                    self._load_said = time.time()
                    log(f"[tests] load {os.getloadavg()[0]:.1f} > {os.cpu_count()} cores: no second test run for now")
                return
            if tid is None:
                want_at = b.pop("gate_want_at", None)
                self._start_gate(b, b.pop("gate_want"), free[0])
                b["gate"]["want_at"] = want_at   # a run lost to a restart keeps its place in line (_gate_lost)
                self.state.save()
                used = True
            else:
                used = self.run_test(self.tasks[tid], free[0])
            if used:
                free.pop(0)
                busy += 1

    # ---- a reviewer out of quota (owner question 2026-09-30: kimi near its weekly limit) ----------------
    def reviewer_benched(self, rv: dict) -> bool:
        return self.state.provider(rv.get("provider") or "reviewer")["cooldown_until"] > time.time()

    def review_rate_limited(self, task: dict, output: str, phase: str) -> bool:
        """A reviewer out of quota answers with a limit error and no verdict. That is the reviewer's state,
        not the change's defect: bench that reviewer and review again, uncharged, on another one, or wait
        (phase review-wait) until one may review it. Only the reply's tail is read, so a review that merely
        discusses rate limits is not taken for one."""
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        provider = (st["job"] or {}).get("provider")
        if not provider or not self.rate_re.search(output[-3000:]):
            return False
        rv = next((r for r in self.reviewers if r.get("provider") == provider), {})
        cool = int(rv.get("cooldown_sec", 3600))
        p = self.state.provider(provider)
        p["cooldown_until"] = time.time() + cool
        p["failures"] += 1
        st["history"][-1]["rate_limited"] = provider
        log(f"[{task['id']}] {phase} by {provider} hit a usage limit; {provider} benched {cool}s, "
            "reviewing again, no attempt charged")
        self.resume_review(task, phase)
        return True

    def hold_review(self, task: dict, phase: str) -> None:
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        if st.get("phase") != "review-wait":
            log(f"[{task['id']}] {phase} waits: every reviewer it may use is benched for a usage limit")
        st.update(status="running", phase="review-wait", job={"phase": "review-wait", "review": phase, "queued": time.time()})
        self.state.save()

    def resume_review(self, task: dict, phase: str) -> None:
        if phase == "plan-review":
            self.start_plan_review(task)
            return
        test_log = self.logs_dir / f"{task['id']}.test.{self.state.task(task['id'])['attempts']}.log"
        self.start_review(task, test_log.read_text(errors="replace") if test_log.exists() else "(no test log)")

    def schedule_reviews(self) -> None:
        """Start the reviews waiting in review-wait once a reviewer is off the bench, and those held for a
        stale spec (spec_hold) once the item's task files are synced."""
        benched = all(self.reviewer_benched(r) for r in self.reviewers)
        for tid in self.running_ids():
            job = self.state.task(tid)["job"] or {}
            if job.get("phase") != "review-wait" or tid not in self.tasks:
                continue
            if job.get("spec_hold"):
                if self.spec_stale(tid):
                    continue
                log(f"[{tid}] spec synced: reviewing again against the amended criteria")
            elif benched:
                continue
            self.resume_review(self.tasks[tid], job.get("review", "review"))

    def start_review(self, task: dict, test_log: str) -> None:
        if not self.reviewers:
            self.finish_merge(task)
            return
        rv = self.pick_reviewer(task)
        if not rv:
            self.requeue(task, "no reviewer on a model other than the ones that wrote this change")
            return
        if self.reviewer_benched(rv):
            self.hold_review(task, "review")
            return
        wt = self.worktree_path(task["id"])
        diff = git(self.repo, "diff", f"{self.main}...{task['id']}").stdout
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        diff_file = self.logs_dir / f"{task['id']}.diff.{st['attempts']}.patch"
        diff_file.write_text(diff)
        prompt = self.review_prompt(task, wt, diff_file, test_log)
        pf = self.logs_dir / f"{task['id']}.review-prompt.{st['attempts']}.md"
        pf.write_text(prompt)
        argv = self.render_cmd(rv["cmd"], worktree=str(wt), prompt_file=str(pf),
                               prompt=prompt, diff_file=str(diff_file), task=task["id"])
        if not self.spawn(task, "review", rv.get("provider"), argv, wt, float(rv.get("max_minutes", 30))):
            self.requeue(task, self.state.task(task["id"])["last_error"] or "could not start reviewer")

    # ---- completion handlers ---------------------------------------------------------
    def commit_worktree(self, task: dict) -> None:
        wt = self.worktree_path(task["id"])
        if sh(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip():
            sh(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=wt, check=False)
            sh(["git", "-c", "user.name=flood", "-c", "user.email=flood@localhost", "commit", "-q", "-m",
                f"{task['id']}: flood auto-commit (attempt {self.state.task(task['id'])['attempts']})"],
               cwd=wt, check=False)

    def after_implement(self, task: dict, rc: int | None, output: str) -> None:
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        provider = (st["job"] or {}).get("provider")
        if provider and self.rate_re.search(output[-20000:]):
            cool = int(self.providers.get(provider, {}).get("cooldown_sec", 900))   # a removed provider's adopted job
            self.state.provider(provider)["cooldown_until"] = time.time() + cool
            self.state.provider(provider)["failures"] += 1
            st["attempts"] -= 1            # rate limits do not consume an attempt
            self.requeue(task, f"provider {provider} rate-limited; cooldown {cool}s")
            return
        self.commit_worktree(task)
        has_change = bool(git(self.repo, "diff", "--stat", f"{self.main}...{task['id']}").stdout.strip())
        if not has_change:
            self.requeue(task, f"implementer exited rc={rc} with no changes")
            return
        st["history"].append({"phase": "implement", "rc": rc, "at": now(), "attempt": st["attempts"]})
        if self.wait_for_red_main(task, "implemented"):
            return
        self.start_test(task)

    def red_main_fix(self) -> str | None:
        """The fix task a red local main (pre-batch gate) or red CI is held on, while it has not merged."""
        fix = (self.state.data.get("batch") or {}).get("hold_fix")
        if fix and fix.startswith(("fix-main-", "fix-ci-")) and self.state.task(fix).get("status") != "done":
            return fix
        return None

    def wait_for_red_main(self, task: dict, what: str) -> bool:
        """While main is red every task's tests fail on main's own breakage (rebase-before-test), a
        systemic cause that must not burn attempts: the task waits, uncharged, and retests on its
        worktree once the fix task merges."""
        fix = self.red_main_fix()
        if not fix or task["id"].startswith(("fix-main-", "fix-ci-")):
            return False
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        last = (st.get("history") or [{}])[-1]
        if last.get("phase") == "test" and last.get("ok") is False:
            last["main_red"] = fix     # never charged: retest --gate-bug looks past it (OMP-594-s04, 2026-10-12)
        st.update(status="pending", job=None, phase=None, retest=True, wait_main=fix,
                  last_error=f"{what} while main is red; retest after {fix} merges (no attempt charged)")
        st.pop("test_retry", None)
        st.pop("flaky_first", None)
        self.state.save()
