        log(f"[{task['id']}] {what} while main is red: waiting for {fix}, then retest (no attempt charged)")
        return True

    def after_test(self, task: dict, ok: bool, output: str) -> None:
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        job = st.get("job") or {}
        entry = {"phase": "test", "ok": ok, "at": now(), "attempt": st["attempts"]}
        if job.get("cached"):
            entry["cached"] = True
        elif job.get("started"):      # measurement: slot-held wall time, and whether this run was the flaky rerun
            entry.update(secs=round(time.time() - job["started"]), rerun=bool(st.get("test_retry")), slots=self.test_slots)
        st["history"].append(entry)
        st.pop("gate_bug", None)
        m = None if ok else UNAPPROVED_CONTRACT_RE.search(output)
        if m and any(self.owner_cmd_allowed(o) for o in self.owner_steps(task)):
            m = None       # flood approved the contract right before these tests: a digest still demanded is a code defect
        if m and m[1] in st.get("auto_approved", {}).get(str(st["attempts"]), []):
            m = None       # flood approved exactly this digest already: still demanded is a code defect
        if m and self.approve_own_contract(task, st):
            return
        if m:
            key = re.match(r"[A-Z]+-\d+", task["id"])
            who = "Chris's" if key and self.chris_step({"id": "", "owner_cmd": f"omp-work approve --issue {key[0]}"}) \
                else "the operator's"
            self.state.outcome(task["id"], "failed")
            st.update(status="failed", job=None, phase=None, finished=now(),
                      last_error=f"tests need {who} contract approval: digest {m[1]}",
                      stuck=f"contract digest {m[1]} awaits {who} owner approval (approval.json); "
                            "tests cannot pass before it, attempts not charged further")
            st.pop("test_retry", None)
            self.state.save()
            log(f"[{task['id']}] PARKED: contract digest {m[1][:12]} needs owner approval")
            return
        if not ok and DISK_FULL_RE.search(output):
            st.update(status="pending", job=None, phase=None, retest=True, wait_disk=True,
                      last_error="tests hit a full disk; retest once /tmp has room (no attempt charged)")
            st.pop("test_retry", None)
            st.pop("flaky_first", None)
            self.state.save()
            log(f"[{task['id']}] tests hit a full disk (systemic): retest once /tmp has room (no attempt charged)")
            return
        if not ok and st.get("test_retry", 0) < int(self.cfg.get("test_retries", 0)):
            st["test_retry"] = st.get("test_retry", 0) + 1
            st["flaky_first"] = first_failure(output)
            log(f"[{task['id']}] tests failed ({st['flaky_first']}); re-running once before charging the attempt")
            self.start_test(task)
            return
        if not ok and self.wait_for_red_main(task, f"tests failed ({first_failure(output)[:120]})"):
            return
        if not ok:
            self.note_failure(st.get("maker_provider"), "tests failed", task["id"])
            self.requeue(task, f"tests failed: {first_failure(output)[:120]}\n" + output[-1500:])
            return
        if st.pop("test_retry", 0):
            log(f"[{task['id']}] tests flaky: {st.pop('flaky_first', 'see log')}")
        self.start_review(task, output)

    def revert_reviewer_changes(self, tid: str, phase: str, job: dict) -> None:
        """The reviewer (kimi) has no read-only sandbox: whatever it left uncommitted is thrown away."""
        wt = Path(job.get("cwd") or (self.plan_worktree(tid) if phase == "plan-review" else self.worktree_path(tid)))
        if not (wt / ".git").exists():
            return
        if sh(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip():
            sh(["git", "checkout", "--", "."], cwd=wt, check=False)
            sh(["git", "clean", "-fd"], cwd=wt, check=False)
            log(f"[{tid}] reviewer modified the worktree; reverted")

    def after_review(self, task: dict, rc: int | None, output: str) -> None:
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        m = VERDICT_RE.findall(output)
        verdict = m[-1].upper() if m else None
        st["history"].append({"phase": "review", "verdict": verdict, "rc": rc, "at": now(), "attempt": st["attempts"],
                              "spec": (st.get("job") or {}).get("spec")})
        if verdict is None and self.review_rate_limited(task, output, "review"):
            return
        # A reply with no verdict line is the reviewer's defect, not the change's (OMP-482, 2026-09-30: a
        # PASS-shaped review with no VERDICT line cost the last attempt): one uncharged re-run first.
        if verdict is None and not st.get("no_verdict_rerun"):
            st["no_verdict_rerun"] = True
            st["avoid_reviewer"] = (st.get("job") or {}).get("provider")
            log(f"[{task['id']}] review gave no verdict (reviewer defect); re-running it, no attempt charged")
            test_log = self.logs_dir / f"{task['id']}.test.{st['attempts']}.log"
            self.start_review(task, test_log.read_text(errors="replace") if test_log.exists() else "(no test log)")
            return
        st.pop("no_verdict_rerun", None)
        st.pop("avoid_reviewer", None)
        if verdict == "PASS":
            self.finish_merge(task)
        else:
            lines = [l for l in output.strip().splitlines() if l.strip()]
            tail = lines[-25:]
            gist = review_gist(lines, verdict)
            head = f"review {verdict or 'gave no verdict'}: {gist[:120]}"
            if verdict == "FAIL":
                self.note_failure(st.get("maker_provider"), "review FAIL", task["id"])
            self.requeue(task, head + "\n" + "\n".join(tail))

    def discard_test_leftovers(self, tid: str, wt: Path) -> None:
        """Before a test or merge rebase the implementer's work is committed, so tracked files still
        modified are what a test run rewrote (Python tooling rewrites omp_work.egg-info); left in place
        they make the rebase refuse ("Please commit or stash them") and burn an attempt."""
        dirty = sh(["git", "diff", "--name-only", "HEAD"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.split()
        if dirty:
            sh(["git", "checkout", "HEAD", "--", "."], cwd=wt, check=False)
            log(f"[{tid}] discarded test leftovers before rebasing: {', '.join(dirty[:5])}")

    def finish_merge(self, task: dict) -> None:
        tid, wt, st = task["id"], self.worktree_path(task["id"]), self.state.task(task["id"])
        if self.spec_recheck(task, "review"):     # the merge is bound to the revision the worker and reviewer used
            return
        self.merge_now(task)

    def merge_now(self, task: dict) -> None:
        tid, wt, st = task["id"], self.worktree_path(task["id"]), self.state.task(task["id"])
        self.discard_test_leftovers(tid, wt)
        tested = sh(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip()
        conflicts = self.rebase_onto_main(wt, task)
        if conflicts:
            self.requeue(task, f"rebase conflict with {self.main} before merge in: {', '.join(conflicts)}")
            return
        # main moved since the tests: a clean text rebase can still break a check (batch 28: two slices
        # each added the same inventory rows and the rebase kept both). Run the cheap merge checks.
        if self.cfg.get("merge_check_cmd") and sh(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip() != tested:
            mc = sh(["sh", "-c", self.cfg["merge_check_cmd"]], cwd=wt, check=False, timeout=600)
            if mc.returncode != 0:
                mc = self.repair_merge_check(task, wt, mc)
            if mc.returncode != 0 and not self.wait_for_red_main(task, "merge check failed"):
                # A concurrent merge broke the combination (OMP-233-s02, OMP-219-s04: both sides added rows to the
                # derived inventory TSV). The first time is not the task's defect: the implementer repairs it on the
                # rebased worktree, uncharged. A repeat is charged.
                free = not st.get("merge_check_free")
                if free:
                    st["merge_check_free"] = True
                    st["attempts"] -= 1
                self.requeue(task, f"merge check failed after rebasing onto moved {self.main} "
                                   f"(`{self.cfg['merge_check_cmd']}`)" + (" (no attempt charged)" if free else "")
                                   + ":\n" + (mc.stdout + mc.stderr)[-1500:])
            if mc.returncode != 0:
                return
        err = self.run_owner_cmds(task, wt)          # main may have moved since the tests: approve what merges
        if err:
            self.requeue(task, err)
            return
        mg = git(self.repo, "merge", "--ff-only", tid, check=False)
        if mg.returncode != 0:
            self.requeue(task, "fast-forward merge failed:\n" + (mg.stdout + mg.stderr)[-1500:])
            return
        sha = git(self.repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD").stdout.strip()
        for o in self.owner_steps(task):
            if not self.owner_cmd_allowed(o):         # not flood's to run: it waits for the operator
                continue
            left = self.owner_hosts_left(o, but=tid)
            if left:                                  # more contract-changing slices to approve in
                log(f"[{o['id']}] owner step `{o['owner_cmd']}` ran on {tid} (merged {sha[:12]}); "
                    f"still runs in {', '.join(left)}")
                continue
            ost = self.state.task(o["id"])
            ost.update(status="done", phase=None, job=None, finished=now(),
                       done_ref=f"flood ran `{o['owner_cmd']}` on {tid} (merged {sha[:12]})")
            log(f"[{o['id']}] DONE by flood: `{o['owner_cmd']}` ran on {tid}")
        st.update(status="done", phase=None, job=None, merged_sha=sha, finished=now())
        self.state.outcome(task["id"], "done")
        self.state.save()
        self.remove_worktree(tid)
        log(f"[{tid}] DONE merged {sha[:12]} into {self.main}")

    def convert_to_plan(self, task: dict, reason: str) -> None:
        """Implement failed at max attempts on a real defect (including a rebase conflict the implementer could
        not resolve): the task becomes a plan task; the old file is kept as <id>.md.failed (OPERATING.md)."""
        tid, st = task["id"], self.state.task(task["id"])
        src = Path(task["path"])
        if not src.exists():
            return
        text = src.read_text()
        meta, body = parse_front_matter(text)
        src.rename(src.with_name(src.name + ".failed"))
        findings = reason.strip()[-3000:]
        fm = ["---", f"id: {tid}", f"depends_on: [{', '.join(meta.get('depends_on', []))}]", "max_minutes: 60", "kind: plan"]
        fm += [f"{k}: {meta[k]}" for k in ("item", "priority") if k in meta]   # spec binding and order survive (05:00Z)
        atomic_write(src, "\n".join([*fm, "---", body.rstrip(), "",
                                      f"## Findings from {st['attempts']} failed implement attempt(s) (flood)", "",
                                      "```", findings, "```", ""]))
        new_meta, new_body = parse_front_matter(src.read_text())
        self.tasks[tid] = {"id": tid, "path": str(src), "body": new_body.strip(), **new_meta}
        st.update(status="pending", phase=None, job=None, attempts=0, history=[],
                  note=f"Converted to plan after {st['attempts']} failed implement attempt(s). Plan around this failure:\n"
                       + findings[-1500:])
        self.remove_worktree(tid)
        log(f"[{tid}] converted to a plan task ({src.name}.failed kept)")

    def owner_hosts(self, o: dict) -> list[str]:
        """The implement slices an owner slice's command runs in: its depends_on, where a dependency that
        was re-planned into slices stands for those slices (recursively), so a re-plan never orphans the
        owner step (OMP-283-s01 -> s01-s01..s03, 2026-09-25)."""
        out, todo, seen = [], list(o.get("depends_on", [])), set()
        while todo:
            d = todo.pop(0)
            if d in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(d)
            sub = self.state.task(d).get("slices") or []
            if sub:
                todo.extend(sub)
            else:
                out.append(d)
        return out

    def owner_hosts_left(self, o: dict, but: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
        return [h for h in self.owner_hosts(o) if h != but and self.state.task(h)["status"] != "done"]

    def owner_scope(self, o: dict) -> list[str]:
        """Every implement slice of the owner slice's own item upstream of it: its hosts and what they depend
        on, transitively. A contract change can land in any of them, not only the slice right before the owner
        step (OMP-266-s05 parked on its digest 2026-09-26 12:08Z while OMP-266-s09 approved only in s08)."""
        fam = re.sub(r"(-s\d+)+$", "", o["id"]) + "-"
        hosts = self.owner_hosts(o)
        out, todo, seen = [], list(hosts), set()
        while todo:
            d = todo.pop(0)
            if d in seen or d not in self.tasks or (d not in hosts and not d.startswith(fam)):
                continue
            seen.add(d)
            sub = self.state.task(d).get("slices") or []
            if sub:
                todo.extend(sub)
                continue
            if not is_owner(self.tasks[d]):
                out.append(d)
            todo.extend(self.tasks[d].get("depends_on", []))
        return out

    def owner_steps(self, task: dict) -> list[dict]:
        """Owner slices with an owner_cmd that apply to this task: its own owner_cmd, and every owner
        slice of its item whose scope (owner_scope) includes it and that is not done yet. The owner slice
        itself is done only once its hosts merge (owner_hosts_left)."""
        own = [task] if task.get("owner_cmd") and not is_owner(task) else []
        return own + [t for t in self.tasks.values() if is_owner(t) and t.get("owner_cmd")
                      and task["id"] in self.owner_scope(t) and self.state.task(t["id"])["status"] != "done"]

    def owner_cmd_allowed(self, o: dict) -> bool:
        return any(re.fullmatch(r, str(o.get("owner_cmd", "")).strip()) for r in self.cfg.get("owner_cmd_allowlist", []))

    def repair_after_test_rebase(self, task: dict, wt: Path, before: str) -> None:
        """The test rebase leaves the same derived-row errors a merge rebase does when main moved (two slices
        each re-hashed the same inventory paths: salvage-omp-work-dirty-s07, 2026-09-25, 25 min of tests and an
        attempt lost on 4 duplicate/stale rows). Run the cheap merge check now; repair what merge_check_repair
        covers so the tests run on the tree that would merge. Anything else is left for the tests to report."""
        if not (self.cfg.get("merge_check_cmd") and self.cfg.get("merge_check_repair")):
            return
        if sh(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip() == before:
            return                                     # main did not move: nothing a rebase could have duplicated
        mc = sh(["sh", "-c", self.cfg["merge_check_cmd"]], cwd=wt, check=False, timeout=600)
        if mc.returncode != 0:
            self.repair_merge_check(task, wt, mc, where="test rebase check")

    def run_pre_test_repairs(self, task: dict, wt: Path) -> None:
        """flood.json pre_test_repair: commands that regenerate a derived file the task's own change left stale
        (a prompt added without refreshing the CPK-0 prompt list: OMP-299-s06, OMP-298-s02/s03, every attempt
        failed on it). Each runs in the worktree before the tests; whatever it changes is committed. A command
        that fails is undone and the tests report the problem as before."""
        for cmd in self.cfg.get("pre_test_repair", []):
            before = sh(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip()
            r = sh(["sh", "-c", cmd], cwd=wt, check=False, timeout=600)
            if r.returncode != 0:
                sh(["git", "reset", "-q", "--hard", before], cwd=wt, check=False)
                sh(["git", "clean", "-fdq"], cwd=wt, check=False)
                log(f"[{task['id']}] pre-test repair `{cmd}` failed rc={r.returncode}; undone")
                continue
            if sh(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip():
                sh(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=wt)
                sh(["git", "-c", "user.name=flood", "-c", "user.email=flood@localhost", "commit", "-q", "-m",
                    f"{task['id']}: regenerate derived files before tests (flood pre_test_repair)"], cwd=wt)
                log(f"[{task['id']}] pre-test repair committed by `{cmd}`")

    def repair_merge_check(self, task: dict, wt: Path, mc, where: str = "merge check"):
        """A merge check that failed only with errors flood.json merge_check_repair.only_errors covers (duplicate
        or stale rows of a derived file, left by a clean rebase over a concurrent merge) is repaired mechanically:
        run its cmd, commit, re-check. Returns the result to act on: the re-check, or the original failure."""
        rep = self.cfg.get("merge_check_repair")
        errs = [l for l in (mc.stdout + mc.stderr).splitlines() if l.startswith("ERROR:")]
        if not rep or not errs or not all(re.search(rep["only_errors"], l) for l in errs):
            return mc
        before = sh(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip()
        fx = sh(["sh", "-c", rep["cmd"]], cwd=wt, check=False, timeout=600)
        if fx.returncode != 0:
            sh(["git", "reset", "-q", "--hard", before], cwd=wt, check=False)
            return mc
        if sh(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip():
            sh(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=wt)
            sh(["git", "-c", "user.name=flood", "-c", "user.email=flood@localhost", "commit", "-q", "-m",
                f"{task['id']}: reconcile derived rows after rebase (flood merge_check_repair)"], cwd=wt)
        again = sh(["sh", "-c", self.cfg["merge_check_cmd"]], cwd=wt, check=False, timeout=600)
        if again.returncode == 0:
            log(f"[{task['id']}] {where} repaired: {len(errs)} error(s) fixed by `{rep['cmd']}`")
            return again
        sh(["git", "reset", "-q", "--hard", before], cwd=wt, check=False)   # not repairable: leave the task's own tree
        return mc

    def run_owner_cmds(self, task: dict, wt: Path) -> str | None:
        """Run allowlisted owner commands (flood.json owner_cmd_allowlist) in the task's worktree with
        flood's own environment, then owner_cmd_post, and commit. Returns an error, or None."""
        ran = []
        for o in self.owner_steps(task):
            cmd = str(o["owner_cmd"]).strip()
            if not self.owner_cmd_allowed(o):
                continue                              # not allowlisted: waits for the operator, as before
            gw = self.cfg.get("owner_gateway")
            err = run_owner_cmd(cmd, wt, gw) if gw else run_owner_cmd(cmd, wt)
            if err:
                return f"owner step `{cmd}` ({o['id']}) failed: {err}"
            ran.append(cmd)
        if not ran:
            return None
        for post in self.cfg.get("owner_cmd_post", []):
            r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-lc", post], cwd=wt, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
            if r.returncode != 0:
                return f"owner post step `{post}` failed: {(r.stdout + r.stderr).strip()[-800:]}"
        if sh(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=wt, check=False).stdout.strip():
            sh(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=wt)
            sh(["git", "-c", "user.name=flood-owner", "-c", "user.email=flood@localhost", "commit", "-q", "-m",
                f"{task['id']}: owner step by flood: " + "; ".join(ran)], cwd=wt)
            log(f"[{task['id']}] owner step committed: {'; '.join(ran)}")
        return None

    def approve_own_contract(self, task: dict, st: dict) -> bool:
        """A task with no owner slice whose tests demand approval of the contract it changed (OMP-323,
        2026-09-26: parked an hour for the operator). `omp-work approve --issue <its item>` is allowlisted,
        so flood runs it in the worktree, commits, and re-runs the tests; no attempt charged. A rebase onto a
        moved contract gets a new digest and a new approval, at most 3 per attempt."""
        key = re.match(r"[A-Z]+-\d+", task["id"])
        cmd = f"omp-work approve --issue {key[0]}" if key else ""
        done = st.setdefault("auto_approved", {}).setdefault(str(st["attempts"]), [])
        if not key or not self.owner_cmd_allowed({"owner_cmd": cmd}) or len(done) >= 3:
            return False
        wt = self.worktree_path(task["id"])
        err = self.run_owner_cmds({"id": task["id"], "owner_cmd": cmd}, wt)
        if err:
            log(f"[{task['id']}] own contract approval failed, parking for the operator: {err[:300]}")
            return False
        ap = wt / APPROVAL_PATH
        done.append(json.loads(ap.read_text()).get("contract_sha256", "") if ap.exists() else "")
        st.update(status="running", job=None, phase=None)
        st.pop("test_retry", None)
        self.state.save()
        log(f"[{task['id']}] tests demanded approval of its own contract: flood ran `{cmd}`, re-running tests (no attempt charged)")
        self.start_test(task)
        return True

    def requeue(self, task: dict, reason: str) -> None:
        st = self.state.task(task["id"])
        st.update(last_error=reason, job=None, phase=None)
        st.pop("test_retry", None)
        st.pop("flaky_first", None)
        limit = self.max_attempts(task)
        if st["attempts"] >= limit:
            st["status"] = "failed"
            st["finished"] = now()
            self.state.outcome(task["id"], "failed")
            log(f"[{task['id']}] FAILED after {st['attempts']} attempts: {reason.splitlines()[0]}")
            if task.get("kind", "implement") == "implement" and not is_owner(task) and self.cfg.get("convert_failed", True):
                self.convert_to_plan(task, reason)
        else:
            st["status"] = "pending"
            log(f"[{task['id']}] requeued (attempt {st['attempts']}/{limit}): {reason.splitlines()[0]}")
        self.state.save()

    # ---- main loop -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # ---- stuck-list hygiene (flood runs it hourly; `flood.py hygiene` shows or applies it) ----------
    def rider_ref(self, key: str) -> str | None:
        """Where a key's delivery is recorded in a rider batch: its evidence up to the first ';'."""
        for f in sorted(self.rider_dir.glob("*.json*")) if self.rider_dir.is_dir() else []:
            try:
                for e in json.loads(f.read_text()):
                    if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get("key") == key:
                        return str(e.get("evidence") or f.name).split(";")[0].strip()
            except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
                continue
        return None

    def forget(self, tid: str) -> None:
        """Drop ONE task from state, with its worktree and branch (never `wipe`, which drops them all)."""
        self.drop_worktree_and_branch(tid)
        self.state.data["tasks"].pop(tid, None)

    def drop_slices(self, tid: str) -> list[str]:
        """A task whose file is an implement task again drops the slices of its old plan: their jobs end, their
        files are parked as <id>.md.dropped and their state goes. Without this the slices ran next to the
        restored task, and the stale `slices` list kept its parent from ever completing (OMP-315-s05-s02,
        2026-10-10)."""
        out = []
        for sl in self.state.task(tid).pop("slices", None) or []:
            out += self.drop_slices(sl)
            job = self.state.task(sl).get("job") or {}
            if job.get("pid"):
                kill_group(int(job["pid"]))
            path = self.tasks_dir / f"{sl}.md"
            if path.exists():
                path.rename(path.with_name(path.name + ".dropped"))
            self.tasks.pop(sl, None)
            self.forget(sl)
            out.append(sl)
        return out

    def hygiene(self, apply: bool = True) -> list[str]:
        """The stuck list holds only what is really stuck: a delivered task file whose state is not done is
        marked done with its rider ref; a probe or test-only job idle for over 24 h leaves state."""
        acts, tasks = [], self.state.data["tasks"]
        files = {p.name.split(".md")[0]: p for p in self.tasks_dir.glob("*.md*")
                 if p.name.endswith((".md", ".md.delivered"))}

        def probe(tid: str) -> bool:
            meta = parse_front_matter(files[tid].read_text())[0] if tid in files else {}
            return "probe" in tid or str(meta.get("test", "")).strip().lower() == "false"

        def last(st: dict) -> float:
            at = st.get("finished") or next((h.get("at") for h in reversed(st.get("history") or []) if h.get("at")), None)
            try:
                return dt.datetime.strptime(at, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc).timestamp()
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                return 0.0
        for tid, st in sorted(tasks.items()):
            if st["status"] == "running":
                continue
            if probe(tid):
                if time.time() - last(st) > 86400:
                    acts.append(f"{tid}: probe/test-only job idle over 24 h, removed from state")
                    if apply:
                        self.forget(tid)
                continue
            p = files.get(tid)
            if p and p.name.endswith(".md.delivered") and st["status"] != "done":
                ref = self.rider_ref(tid)
                if not ref:
                    acts.append(f"{tid}: task file marked delivered but no rider entry names it; left for the operator")
                    continue
                acts.append(f"{tid}: task file marked delivered, state was {st['status']}; marked done ({ref})")
                if apply:
                    st.update(status="done", phase=None, job=None, done_ref=ref, finished=now())
                    st.pop("stuck", None)
        if apply and acts:
            self.state.save()
        return acts

    # ---- measurement: test-slot wall time and flaky reruns -------------------------------
    def teststats(self, start: float, end: float) -> dict:
        """Test runs in [start, end): wall time holding a slot, and the flaky-rerun rate. Runs recorded
        before 2026-09-26 carry no `secs`; their time is estimated from finish-to-finish gaps, which is
        exact for the old single serial lock line (always busy)."""
        def ts(at):
            try:
                return dt.datetime.strptime(at, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc).timestamp()
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                return None
        runs = [h for st in self.state.data["tasks"].values() for h in st.get("history") or []
                if h.get("phase") == "test" and not h.get("cached") and (t := ts(h.get("at"))) and start <= t < end]
        secs = sorted(h["secs"] for h in runs if "secs" in h)
        estimated = False
        if not secs:
            fins = sorted(os.path.getmtime(f) for f in [*self.logs_dir.glob("*.test.*.rc"), *self.logs_dir.glob("_main-gate.*.rc")]
                          if start <= os.path.getmtime(f) < end)
            secs = sorted(round(b - a) for a, b in zip(fins, fins[1:]) if b - a < 2 * 60 * float(self.cfg.get("test_max_minutes", 20)))
            estimated = True
        text = ""
        logf = self.cfg_dir / "flood.log"
        if logf.exists():
            text = logf.read_text(errors="replace")
        def count(pat):
            return sum(1 for l in text.splitlines() if pat in l and (t := ts(l[:20])) and start <= t < end)
        started, reruns, flaky = count("] test started"), count("re-running once before charging"), count("tests flaky:")
        pct = lambda q: secs[min(len(secs) - 1, int(q * len(secs)))] if secs else None
        return {"runs": started, "reruns": reruns, "flaky": flaky, "flaky_rate": round(flaky / started, 3) if started else None,
                "rerun_rate": round(reruns / started, 3) if started else None,
                "median_s": pct(0.5), "p90_s": pct(0.9), "timed": len(secs), "estimated": estimated,
                "cached_hits": sum(1 for st in self.state.data["tasks"].values() for h in st.get("history") or []
                                   if h.get("cached") and (t := ts(h.get("at"))) and start <= t < end)}

    def drop_orphan_job(self, tid: str, job: dict) -> None:
        """A running state entry whose task no longer exists: end its job's process group, collect it, drop it."""
        pid = int(job.get("pid", 0) or 0)
        if pid:
            kill_group(pid)
        proc = self.procs.pop(tid, None)
        if proc is not None:
            try:
                proc.wait(timeout=10)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                pass
        elif pid:                       # a child started before an in-place reload: no Popen handle to wait on
            try:
                os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
            except ChildProcessError:
                pass
        self.state.data["tasks"].pop(tid, None)
        self.state.save()
        log(f"[{tid}] task file gone while its {job.get('phase') or 'job'} ran: job ended, state dropped")

    def reap(self) -> None:
        for tid in self.running_ids():
            task, st = self.tasks.get(tid), self.state.task(tid)
            job = st["job"] or {}
            if task is None:            # its task file was parked or removed while the job ran (2026-10-10: OMP-514
                self.drop_orphan_job(tid, job)   # kept a planner slot and a zombie after the owner cancelled it)
                continue
            if job.get("phase") in ("test-wait", "review-wait"):   # no process yet: schedule_tests / schedule_reviews start it
                continue
            proc = self.procs.get(tid)
            if proc is not None:
                rc = proc.poll()
                alive = rc is None
            else:                       # adopted from a previous flood.py process
                alive, rc = adopted_status(int(job.get("pid", 0) or 0))
                if not alive and rc is None and job.get("rc_file"):
                    try:
                        rc = int(Path(job["rc_file"]).read_text().strip())
                    except (OSError, ValueError):
                        pass
            budget = job.get("budget", job.get("deadline", 0) - job.get("started", 0))
            if job.get("phase") == "test":      # a raised test_max_minutes applies to jobs already in the lock line
                budget = max(float(budget or 0), 60 * float(self.cfg.get("test_max_minutes", 20)))
            if alive and job.get("phase") == "test" and time.time() - job.get("started", 0) < self.lock_line_cap(budget):
                # The test command waits in line for the shared test lock with no output; the clock
                # starts when the gate gets the lock and writes its first line (wait capped by line length).
                try:
                    if Path(job["log"]).stat().st_size <= job.get("log_offset", 0):
                        job["deadline"] = time.time() + budget
                except (KeyError, OSError):
                    pass
            if alive and time.time() > job.get("deadline", 1e18):
                log(f"[{tid}] {job['phase']} exceeded {budget:.0f}s after {time.time() - job.get('started', 0):.0f}s; killing")
                kill_group(int(job["pid"]))
                alive, rc = False, -9
                st["last_error"] = f"{job['phase']} timed out"
                if job.get("phase") in ("implement", "plan"):
                    self.note_failure(job.get("provider"), f"{job['phase']} timeout", tid)
            if alive:
                continue
            if rc in (128 + signal.SIGINT, 128 + signal.SIGTERM):
                # the CLI caught SIGINT/SIGTERM from outside flood and exited 128+n (a flood stop under the OMP-537
                # KillMode=control-group drop-in charged OMP-560, OMP-544 and OMP-532-s03 on 2026-10-10): a signal death
                rc = -(rc - 128)
            outside = rc is None or (rc < 0 and rc != -9)     # -9: flood's own timeout kill
            self.procs.pop(tid, None)
            output = ""
            try:
                with open(job["log"], "rb") as lf:
                    lf.seek(job.get("log_offset", 0))
                    output = lf.read().decode(errors="replace")
            except (KeyError, OSError):
                pass
            phase = job.get("phase")
            left = reap_leftovers(int(job.get("pid", 0) or 0), tid) if job.get("pid") else 0
            if left:
                log(f"[{tid}] killed {left} leftover process(es) from its {phase} job")
            self.audit_job(tid, phase, job.get("log", ""), output)
            self.audit_control_files(tid, phase, job)
            self.audit_global_links(tid, phase, job)
            if phase in ("review", "plan-review"):
                self.revert_reviewer_changes(tid, phase, job)
            log(f"[{tid}] {phase} finished rc={rc} in {time.time() - job.get('started', time.time()):.0f}s")
            if phase == "implement":
                if rc == -9:
                    self.commit_worktree(task)
                    self.state.task(tid)["avoid_provider"] = job.get("provider")   # retry on another implementer
                    self.requeue(task, "implementer timed out (worktree kept for continuation)")
                elif rc is None or rc < 0:
                    # killed by something other than flood (a stray SIGTERM, 2026-09-25 12:10Z, or the wrapper
                    # died without writing its rc): partial work is not a failed attempt
                    self.commit_worktree(task)
                    st["attempts"] -= 1
                    self.requeue(task, f"implementer killed from outside flood (rc={rc}); worktree kept, "
                                       "no attempt charged")
                else:
                    self.after_implement(task, rc, output)
            # rc is None only for a job adopted from a previous flood.py: its exit code died with that process
            elif phase == "test" and outside:
                log(f"[{tid}] test exit code lost across restart or killed from outside flood (rc={rc}); re-running tests")
                self.start_test(task)
            elif phase == "test" and rc == SLOT_TAKEN and job.get("slot") is not None:
                log(f"[{tid}] test slot {job['slot']} was taken by a run flood did not start; queued again")
                self.start_test(task)
            elif phase == "test":
                self.cache_put(job.get("tree"), job.get("cmd"), rc == 0, job.get("log"))
                self.after_test(task, ok=(rc == 0), output=output)
            elif phase == "review" and outside and not VERDICT_RE.search(output):
                log(f"[{tid}] review exit code lost across restart and no verdict in its log; re-running review")
                test_log = self.logs_dir / f"{tid}.test.{st['attempts']}.log"
                self.start_review(task, test_log.read_text(errors="replace") if test_log.exists() else "(no test log)")
            elif phase == "review":
                self.after_review(task, rc, output)
            elif phase == "plan" and rc == -9:
                self.requeue(task, "planner timed out")
            elif phase == "plan" and outside:
                st["attempts"] -= 1
                self.requeue(task, f"planner killed from outside flood (rc={rc}); no attempt charged")
            elif phase == "plan" and rc != 0 and self.plan_rate_limited(task, output):
                pass
            elif phase == "plan":
                self.after_plan(task)
            elif phase == "plan-review" and outside and not VERDICT_RE.search(output):
                log(f"[{tid}] plan review exit code lost across restart and no verdict; re-running it")
                self.start_plan_review(task)
            elif phase == "plan-review":
                self.after_plan_review(task, output)

    def lock_line_cap(self, budget: float) -> float:
        """How long a job may wait silently for the shared suite lock: one budget per job that can be
        ahead of it (every test-phase job plus a pre-batch gate), never under three. A fixed 3x cap
        killed every waiter of a 16-deep line at ~4800 s on 2026-09-25 (seven kills 21:26Z-22:00Z),
        including the holder mid-run, so nothing finished."""
        phases = [(self.state.task(tid)["job"] or {}).get("phase") for tid in self.running_ids()]
        return max(3, sum(1 for ph in phases if ph == "test") + 2) * budget

    def occupied_slots(self) -> int:
        """Running jobs that occupy a slot. Test-phase jobs serialize on the shared suite lock, so
        all but one of them sit idle in the lock line: they count as one slot together, otherwise a
        long line (9 waiters at 2026-09-25 21:00Z) fills every slot while ready implement work idles."""
        phases = [(self.state.task(tid)["job"] or {}).get("phase") for tid in self.running_ids()]
        tests = sum(1 for ph in phases if ph == "test")
        waits = sum(1 for ph in phases if ph in ("test-wait", "review-wait"))   # queued: no process, no seat
        return len(phases) - tests - waits + min(tests, self.test_slots)

    def start_gap_open(self) -> bool:
        """OMP-551 software wall (pve reset twice when a restarted flood began every job in one tick): no new
        implement, plan, test or gate run starts within start_gap_sec (flood.json, default 0 = off) of the
        last job start. A restart ramps up one job per gap, so the 1-minute load guard sees each test run."""
        return time.time() - getattr(self, "_last_start", 0.0) >= float(self.cfg.get("start_gap_sec") or 0)

    def fill(self) -> None:
        for task in self.ready_tasks():
            if self.occupied_slots() >= self.slots or not self.start_gap_open():
                return
            try:
                if self.state.task(task["id"]).pop("retest", False):
                    log(f"[{task['id']}] retest: re-running tests on the existing worktree (no new attempt)")
                    self.start_test(task)
                    continue
                self.start_implement(task)
            except (RuntimeError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as e:
                # repo/worktree trouble is not the task's fault and will not fix itself:
                # fail it without charging an attempt so `reset` can retry after you look.
                err = getattr(e, "stderr", None) or str(e)
                st = self.state.task(task["id"])
                st.update(status="failed", phase=None, job=None, last_error=f"git error: {str(err).strip()[:300]}")
                self.state.save()
                log(f"[{task['id']}] FAILED (git): {str(err).strip().splitlines()[0][:120]}")

    def unblock_dependents(self, tid: str) -> list[str]:
        """Dependents blocked because of tid get another chance (after reset/retest of tid)."""
        out, todo, seen = [], [tid], {tid}
        while todo:                                  # walk depends_on downstream: the whole chain comes back
            cur = todo.pop()
            for t in self.tasks.values():
                if cur in t.get("depends_on", []) and t["id"] not in seen:
                    seen.add(t["id"])
                    todo.append(t["id"])
                    st = self.state.task(t["id"])
                    if st["status"] == "blocked":
                        st.update(status="pending", last_error=None)
                        out.append(t["id"])
        return out

    def reopen_parents(self, tid: str) -> list[str]:
        """A slice given another chance (reset/retest) reopens its failed parent, and what was blocked on it."""
        out, todo = [], [tid]
        while todo:                                  # a reopened parent reopens its own failed parent
            cur = todo.pop()
            for pid, pst in self.state.data["tasks"].items():
                if cur in pst.get("slices", []) and pst["status"] == "failed":
                    pst.update(status="planned", last_error=None)
                    out += [pid] + self.unblock_dependents(pid)
                    todo.append(pid)
        return out

    def block_orphans(self) -> None:
        """A pending task whose dependency failed/blocked can never run; say so."""
        for t in self.tasks.values():
            st = self.state.task(t["id"])
            if st["status"] != "pending":
                continue
            bad = [d for d in t.get("depends_on", []) if self.state.task(d)["status"] in ("failed", "blocked")]
            if bad:
                st.update(status="blocked", last_error=f"dependency failed: {', '.join(bad)}")
                self.state.save()
                log(f"[{t['id']}] BLOCKED: dependency failed: {', '.join(bad)}")

    def tick(self) -> None:
        self.reap()
        self.sweep_strays()
        if getattr(self, "_report_due", None):
            self.write_report(self._report_due)
            self._report_due = None
        self.settle_plans()
        if time.time() - getattr(self, "_usage_at", 0) >= self.cfg.get("usage_refresh_sec", 300):
            self._usage_at = time.time()
            self.refresh_usage()
        self.fill()
        self.block_orphans()
        if not self.running_ids():
            self.log_benched()
        self.batch_step()
        self.schedule_tests()
        self.schedule_reviews()
        if time.time() - getattr(self, "_hold_at", 0) >= self.cfg.get("owner_hold_check_sec", 300):
            self._hold_at = time.time()
            self.owner_hold_check()
        if time.time() - getattr(self, "_hygiene_at", 0) >= 3600:
            self._hygiene_at = time.time()
            for line in self.hygiene():
                log(f"[hygiene] {line}")
            for line in self.codacy_sweep():
                log(f"[codacy] {line}")

    def codacy_findings(self, pr: str) -> list[dict] | None:
        """New Codacy findings on a merged PR (public repo, no key needed); None while Codacy has not analysed it."""
        url, found, cursor = CODACY_ISSUES.format(org=self.cfg["codacy_repo"].split("/")[0], name=self.cfg["codacy_repo"].split("/")[1], pr=pr), [], None
        while True:
            q = f"?limit=100" + (f"&cursor={cursor}" if cursor else "")
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url + q, timeout=30) as r:
                d = json.load(r)
            if not d.get("analyzed", True):
                return None
            found += [x["commitIssue"] for x in d.get("data") or [] if x.get("deltaType") == "Added"]
            cursor = (d.get("pagination") or {}).get("cursor")
            if not cursor:
                return found

    def codacy_sweep(self) -> list[str]:
        """Owner ruling 2026-09-26: Codacy checks only Security and ErrorProne rules and skips test files. After a
        batch merges, what it found in program code becomes one task. The filter repeats Codacy's own settings so an
        analysis made before a settings change still only files real findings."""
        acts, due = [], self.state.data.get("codacy_due") or []
        for pr in list(due):
            try:
                found = self.codacy_findings(pr)
            except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
                acts.append(f"PR #{pr}: Codacy not reachable ({e}); retried next hour")
                continue
            if found is None:
                acts.append(f"PR #{pr}: Codacy has not analysed it yet; retried next hour")
                continue
            due.remove(pr)
            real = [f for f in found if f["patternInfo"]["category"] in ("Security", "ErrorProne")
                    and not CODACY_TEST_RE.search(f["filePath"])]
            if not real:
                acts.append(f"PR #{pr}: {len(found)} new Codacy finding(s), none in program code; nothing filed")
                continue
            tid, files = f"codacy-pr{pr}", sorted({f["filePath"] for f in real})
            path = self.tasks_dir / f"{tid}.md"
            if not any(self.tasks_dir.glob(f"{tid}.md*")):
                lines = "\n".join(f"- `{f['filePath']}:{f['lineNumber']}` {f['patternInfo']['id']}: {f['message']}"
                                  for f in real)
                path.write_text(f"---\nid: {tid}\ndepends_on: []\nmax_minutes: 45\n---\n"
                                f"# Fix what Codacy found in program code merged by PR #{pr}\n\n"
                                f"Codacy (Security and ErrorProne rules only, test files skipped) found:\n\n{lines}\n\n"
                                "Fix each finding in the code, keeping behaviour the same. If a finding is a false alarm, "
                                "leave the code and say why in the commit message.\n"
                                "- This task is explicitly allowed to edit only these existing files: "
                                + ", ".join(f"`{x}`" for x in files) + ".\n\nAcceptance:\n"
                                "- [ ] Each finding above is fixed or explained in the commit message.\n"
                                "- [ ] The normal test command passes.\n")
            acts.append(f"PR #{pr}: {len(real)} Codacy finding(s) in program code; filed {tid}")
        self.state.save()
        return acts

    def sweep_strays(self, every: float = 300.0) -> int:
        """Kill processes a finished job left outside its process group (reap_leftovers only sees the group):
        2026-09-25 a pytest postgres server of OMP-262-s02 and an ssh ControlMaster of the salvage plan job
        were still running 17 h after their tasks merged. A process is a stray when its FLOOD_TASK marker names
        a task of ours with no running job (or an unknown task); the gate has its own pid tracking."""
        if time.time() < getattr(self, "_sweep_at", 0):
            return 0
        self._sweep_at = time.time() + every
        live = {int(st["job"]["pid"]) for st in self.state.data["tasks"].values()
                if st.get("job") and st["job"].get("pid")}
        killed = 0
        leaks = prune_tmp_leaks(self.cfg.get("tmp_leak_prefixes", []),   # tmp_leak_root: the automation user's jobs
                                Path(self.cfg.get("tmp_leak_root", "/tmp")))  # see a private /tmp (sandbox extra)
        if leaks:
            log(f"[tmp] pruned {leaks} leaked test tmp entr{'y' if leaks == 1 else 'ies'} older than 2 h")
        import getpass
        # jobs run pytest under the private /tmp (tmp_leak_root): only flood's own /tmp was swept, and by
        # 2026-10-14 02Z 13 dead basetemps there held 252k of /tmp's inodes, under disk_has_room's 25 % floor
        pruned = prune_pytest_basetemps() + prune_pytest_basetemps(
            Path(self.cfg.get("tmp_leak_root", "/tmp")) / f"pytest-of-{getpass.getuser()}")
        if pruned:
            log(f"[tmp] pruned {len(pruned)} dead pytest basetemp dir(s), {sum(b for _, b in pruned) / 1e9:.1f} GB: "
                + ", ".join(d.name for d, _ in pruned))
        stale = stale_runtime_pids()
        for pid in stale:
            try:
                os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                killed += 1
            except ProcessLookupError:
                pass
        if stale:
            log(f"[tmp] killed {len(stale)} installed-runtime test server(s) whose staging dir is gone: pids {stale}")
        for tid, pids in marked_processes(exclude_pgids=live).items():
            if tid == "_main-gate":
                continue
            st = self.state.data["tasks"].get(tid)
            if st is None or st.get("job") or tid not in self.tasks:
                continue        # running job: its processes, not strays. Unknown task: not ours to kill (another
                                # flood instance, a test run of flood.py, or a marker set by hand) - 2026-09-25 14:20Z
                                # a test instance's sweep killed six real jobs by treating every real task as unknown.
            for pid in pids:
                try:
                    os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                    killed += 1
                except ProcessLookupError:
                    pass
            if pids:
                log(f"[{tid}] killed {len(pids)} stray process(es) left by a finished job")
        return killed

    def log_benched(self) -> None:
        """Nothing running: say which ready tasks are waiting out provider cooldowns, so a
        bench reads differently from a hang. At most once a minute."""
        t = time.time()
        if t - self.bench_logged < 60:
            return
        for task in self.ready_tasks():
            names = self.eligible_providers(task, task_role(task))
            until = {n: self.state.provider(n)["cooldown_until"] for n in names}
            if names and all(u > t for u in until.values()):
                self.bench_logged = t
                benched = ", ".join(f"{n} until {dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(u, dt.timezone.utc):%H:%M:%SZ}"
                                    for n, u in until.items())
                log(f"[{task['id']}] waiting: providers benched ({benched})")

    # ---- integration batches ------------------------------------------------------------
    # The remote base branch is PR-protected, so local main ships in batch PRs, one open at a
    # time. Local task merges keep landing on local main meanwhile and ride the next batch;
    # nothing is ever pushed to an open batch branch (that would restart CI) and local main is
    # never reset.
    def batch_step(self) -> None:
        push = self.cfg.get("push")
        if not push:
            return
        b = self.state.data.setdefault("batch", {"n": 0, "pr": None})
        t = time.time()
        if t >= b.get("next_at", 0):
            b["next_at"] = t + float(push.get("poll_seconds", 120))
            try:
                self._batch(push.get("remote", "origin"), push.get("base", self.main),
                            push.get("branch_prefix", "flood/batch-"), b)
            except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, OSError, ValueError, KeyError) as e:   # gh/git/network: retry next poll
                log(f"[batch] error, retrying next poll: {(getattr(e, 'stderr', '') or str(e)).strip()[:300]}")
            self.state.save()
        if t >= b.get("nightly_next_at", 0):
            b["nightly_next_at"] = t + float(push.get("nightly_poll_seconds", 1800))
            try:
                self._nightly(push.get("base", self.main), b)
            except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, OSError, ValueError, KeyError) as e:
                log(f"[nightly] error, retrying next poll: {(getattr(e, 'stderr', '') or str(e)).strip()[:300]}")
            self.state.save()
        if b.get("held") and t - b.get("held_said", 0) >= 60:     # a held batch says so once a minute
            b["held_said"] = t
            log(b["held"])
            self.state.save()

    def _nightly(self, base: str, b: dict) -> None:
        """Watch CI's nightly run on GitHub main, the only place the full installed qualification runs since the
        pre-batch gate takes the batch PR's own choice (owner 2026-09-28). Red: re-run the failed jobs once (known
        flaky jobs), still red: a fix-ci-nightly-<sha> task (top priority by its fix-ci- prefix). Batches keep flowing."""
        runs = json.loads(sh(["gh", "run", "list", "--workflow", (self.cfg.get("push") or {}).get("nightly_workflow", "ci.yml"),
                              "--event", "schedule", "--branch", base, "--limit", "1",
                              "--json", "databaseId,status,conclusion,headSha,url"], cwd=self.repo).stdout or "[]")
        if not runs or str(runs[0].get("status")) != "completed" or str(runs[0]["databaseId"]) == b.get("nightly_seen"):
            return
        r, rid = runs[0], str(runs[0]["databaseId"])
        if str(r.get("conclusion") or "").upper() not in ("FAILURE", "TIMED_OUT", "STARTUP_FAILURE", "ERROR"):
            b["nightly_seen"] = rid
            return
        if b.get("nightly_rerun") != rid:
            b["nightly_rerun"] = rid
            if sh(["gh", "run", "rerun", rid, "--failed"], cwd=self.repo, check=False).returncode == 0:
                log(f"[nightly] run {rid} on {r['headSha'][:12]} red, re-running failed jobs once: {r['url']}")
                return
        jobs = json.loads(sh(["gh", "run", "view", rid, "--json", "jobs"], cwd=self.repo).stdout).get("jobs") or []
        checks = [{"name": j.get("name"), "conclusion": j.get("conclusion"), "detailsUrl": j.get("url")} for j in jobs]
        text = self._ci_failure_text(r["url"], checks)
        b["nightly_seen"] = rid
        if re.search(self.RUNNER_DISK, text):     # the self-hosted runner's disk, not the code: nothing to fix in a task
            b["nightly_runner_disk"] = {"run": rid, "sha": r["headSha"][:12], "url": r["url"], "at": now()}
            log(f"[nightly] run {rid} red because the CI runner is out of disk (no space left on device): "
                f"not a code defect, no fix task; the runner host is Chris's ({r['url']})")
            return
        b.pop("nightly_runner_disk", None)
        tid = self._fix_task(f"fix-ci-nightly-{r['headSha'][:10]}",
                             f"CI's nightly full run fails on GitHub main {r['headSha'][:12]} ({r['url']})", text)
        log(f"[nightly] run {rid} still red after a re-run: fix task {tid}")

    def _is_ancestor(self, a: str, b: str) -> bool:
        return git(self.repo, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", a, b, check=False).returncode == 0

    def _sync_main(self, upstream: str, b: dict) -> bool:
        """Bring local main up to the remote base (fast-forward, or a real merge when both moved)."""
        if not self._is_ancestor(upstream, self.main):
            mg = git(self.repo, "-c", "user.name=flood", "-c", "user.email=flood@localhost",
                     "merge", "--no-edit", upstream, check=False)
            if mg.returncode != 0:
                git(self.repo, "merge", "--abort", check=False)
                b["held"] = f"[batch] merge conflict with {upstream}, needs a human"
                return False
            log(f"[batch] merged {upstream} into local {self.main}")
        if (b.get("held") or "").startswith("[batch] merge conflict"):
            b["held"] = None
        return True

    # ---- batches (OPERATING.md # Batches): gate main before a batch, never close for new merges,
    # re-run flaky jobs twice, then fix task (one part) or bisect (several parts) ------------------------
    FAILED_CHECK = ("FAILURE", "CANCELLED", "TIMED_OUT", "ERROR", "STARTUP_FAILURE")
    RUNNER_DISK = r"ENOSPC|No space left on device"
    PENDING_CHECK = ("", "PENDING", "EXPECTED", "IN_PROGRESS", "QUEUED", "WAITING", "REQUESTED")

    def _parts(self, good: str, bad: str) -> list[str]:
        """Batch points between good (exclusive) and bad (inclusive), oldest first: each merged task's tip
        on the first-parent line, plus bad itself. Any commit on local main is a valid batch point."""
        tips = {st.get("merged_sha") for st in self.state.data["tasks"].values() if st.get("merged_sha")}
        line = git(self.repo, "rev-list", "--reverse", "--first-parent", f"{good}..{bad}").stdout.split()
        return [c for c in line if c in tips or c == bad]

    def _tasks_between(self, good: str, bad: str) -> list[str]:
        return [tid for tid, st in self.state.data["tasks"].items() if st.get("merged_sha") and st["status"] == "done"
                and self._is_ancestor(st["merged_sha"], bad) and not self._is_ancestor(st["merged_sha"], good)]

    def _ci_failure_text(self, url: str, checks: list[dict]) -> str:
        """The failing lines of every failed GitHub Actions job (for a fix task's body)."""
        slug = "/".join(url.split("github.com/", 1)[-1].split("/")[:2])
        out = []
        for c in checks:
            if str(c.get("conclusion") or c.get("state") or "").upper() not in self.FAILED_CHECK:
                continue
            m = re.search(r"/job/(\d+)", str(c.get("detailsUrl") or ""))
            text = sh(["gh", "api", "--allow-escape-sequences", f"repos/{slug}/actions/jobs/{m[1]}/logs"],
                      cwd=self.repo, check=False).stdout if m else ""
            text = re.sub(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m", "", text)
            hits = [l[29:] if re.match(r"\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT", l) else l for l in text.splitlines()
                    if re.search(r"✗|\(fail\)|error:|FAILED|##\[error\]|" + self.RUNNER_DISK, l)]
            out.append(f"## {c.get('name') or c.get('context')}\n" + ("\n".join(hits[:60]) or "(no failing lines found)"))
        return "\n\n".join(out)[-6000:]

    def _fix_task(self, tid: str, what: str, output: str) -> str:
        """An implement task that makes main pass again. Written once; the file is flood's only record.
        A fix task of that name that is already done fixed an earlier failure of the same commit, and holding on
        it would resume batches at once and send the same red batch again (batch 289, 2026-10-12): use a new name."""
        base, n = tid, 1
        while any(self.tasks_dir.glob(f"{tid}.md*")) and self.state.data["tasks"].get(tid, {}).get("status") == "done":
            n += 1
            tid = f"{base}-{n}"
        if not any(self.tasks_dir.glob(f"{tid}.md*")):
            self.tasks_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            atomic_write(self.tasks_dir / f"{tid}.md", "\n".join([
                "---", f"id: {tid}", "depends_on: []", "max_minutes: 45", "kind: implement", "---",
                f"# Fix: {what}", "", f"{what}. Make it pass without weakening, skipping or deleting the failing check;",
                "fix the code (or the test, only when the test itself is wrong). Failing output:", "",
                "```", failure_excerpt(output), "```", "",
                "Done when: the check above passes in the full test gate.", "", "Do not touch: unrelated files.", ""]))
            log(f"[batch] fix task {tid}: {what}")
        return tid

    def _gate(self, b: dict, sha: str, up: str | None = None) -> bool | None:
        """Pre-batch gate: the test gate on a local main commit. True/False when finished, None while running.
        `up` (GitHub main) reaches the gate as FLOOD_GATE_BASE: oh-my-pi-test.sh then takes the batch PR's own
        installed-qualification choice over up...sha, as CI does; without it the gate runs the full set."""
        if up:
            b["gate_base"] = up
        g = b.get("gate") or {}
        if g.get("sha") == sha and "ok" in g:
            return g["ok"]
        if g.get("sha") == sha and g.get("pid"):
            alive, _ = adopted_status(int(g["pid"]))
            budget = float(g.get("budget") or 2 * 60 * float(self.cfg.get("test_max_minutes", 20)))
            started = float(g.get("started") or g["deadline"] - budget)
            if alive and g.get("log") and os.path.exists(g["log"]) and os.path.getsize(g["log"]) == 0 \
                    and time.time() < started + self.lock_line_cap(budget):
                g["deadline"] = time.time() + budget   # still queued behind the shared test lock: the clock
                return None                            # starts at the gate's first line (as for test jobs)
            if alive and time.time() < g["deadline"]:
                return None
            if alive:
                kill_group(int(g["pid"]))
                log(f"[batch] pre-batch gate on {sha[:12]} timed out; running it again")
                b["gate"] = None
                return None
            try:
                rc = int(Path(g["rc_file"]).read_text().strip())
            except (OSError, ValueError):
                return self._gate_lost(b, g)         # exit code lost (restart): run it again
            if rc == SLOT_TAKEN and g.get("slot") is not None:
                return self._gate_lost(b, g)         # a run flood did not start took the slot first: queue again
            g["ok"] = rc == 0
            self.cache_put(g.get("tree"), g.get("cmd"), g["ok"], g["log"])
            log(f"[batch] pre-batch gate on {sha[:12]}: {'green' if rc == 0 else 'RED'} "
                f"in {time.time() - float(g.get('started') or time.time()):.0f}s (log {g['log']})")
            return g["ok"]
        cmd = self.slotted(self.cfg.get("default_test")) or self.cfg.get("default_test") or "true"
        tree = self.tree_of(self.repo, sha)
        hit = self.cache_get(tree, cmd)
        # a task run that took the installed-qualification subset or a task scope (oh-my-pi-test.sh, OMP-344)
        # is not this gate: the pre-batch gate always runs every check and the full qualification
        if hit and self.qualified_subset(hit.get("log")):
            hit = None
        if hit:     # the task merged right after its own test with nothing in between: that run was this gate
            b["gate"] = {"sha": sha, "ok": True, "cached": True, "log": hit["log"]}
            b.pop("gate_want", None)                 # a queued run is no longer wanted; its clock must not carry
            b.pop("gate_want_at", None)              # over to the next queue (21:13Z gate "aged" on 20:42Z's clock)
            log(f"[batch] pre-batch gate on {sha[:12]}: green from cache (tree {tree[:12]} passed at {hit['at']})")
            return True
        if self.slotted(self.cfg.get("default_test")) is not None:
            if b.get("gate_want") != sha:
                log(f"[batch] pre-batch gate on {sha[:12]} queued for the next test slot (first in line once no test waits or after gate_max_wait_min)")
            b["gate_want"] = sha
            b.setdefault("gate_want_at", time.time())
            return None
        self._start_gate(b, sha, None)
        return None

    def _gate_lost(self, b: dict, g: dict) -> None:
        """Queue a gate run that never finished again with the wait it had already served (11Z pass 2026-10-10:
        a flood restart one minute into an aged gate queued it again on a fresh 45-minute clock)."""
        b["gate"] = None
        if g.get("want_at"):
            b["gate_want_at"] = g["want_at"]
        return None

    def _start_gate(self, b: dict, sha: str, slot: int | None) -> None:
        wt = self.wt_dir / "_main-gate"
        if not (wt / ".git").exists():
            git(self.repo, "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(wt), sha)
        sh(["git", "checkout", "-q", "-f", "--detach", sha], cwd=wt)
        sh(["git", "clean", "-q", "-fd"], cwd=wt, check=False)
        logf = self.logs_dir / f"_main-gate.{sha[:12]}.log"
        rc_file = logf.with_suffix(".rc")
        rc_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in TERMINAL_VARS + CREDENTIAL_VARS}
        env.update(self.fence, FLOOD_TASK="_main-gate", FLOOD_PHASE="gate", FLOOD_WORKTREE=str(wt))
        if b.get("gate_base"):
            env["FLOOD_GATE_BASE"] = b["gate_base"]
        cmd = self.slotted(self.cfg.get("default_test")) or self.cfg.get("default_test") or "true"
        run = cmd if slot is None else f"flock -n -E {SLOT_TAKEN} {shlex.quote(self.slot_path(slot))} {cmd}"
        with open(logf, "w") as fh:
            proc = subprocess.Popen(["sh", "-c", '"$@"; rc=$?; printf %s "$rc" > "$0"; exit "$rc"', str(rc_file),
                                     *self.sandbox_prefix(), "bash", "-lc", run],
                                    cwd=wt, stdout=fh, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                                    start_new_session=True, env=env)
        self.procs["_main-gate"] = proc              # keeps the child reaped while flood runs
        self._last_start = time.time()
        budget = 2 * 60 * float(self.cfg.get("test_max_minutes", 20))
        b["gate"] = {"sha": sha, "pid": proc.pid, "log": str(logf), "rc_file": str(rc_file), "slot": slot,
                     "tree": self.tree_of(self.repo, sha), "cmd": cmd, "base": env.get("FLOOD_GATE_BASE"),
                     "started": time.time(), "budget": budget, "deadline": time.time() + budget}
        log(f"[batch] pre-batch gate started on {sha[:12]} (log {logf.name})")
        return None

    def _batch(self, remote: str, base: str, prefix: str, b: dict) -> None:
        upstream = f"{remote}/{base}"
        git(self.repo, *self.remote_auth, "fetch", "-q", remote, base)
        if b.get("pr"):
            self._poll_batch(remote, base, upstream, b)
            return
        if not self._sync_main(upstream, b):
            return
        up = git(self.repo, "rev-parse", upstream).stdout.strip()
        if b.get("hold_fix"):                        # a red main or red batch waits for its fix to merge locally
            if self.state.task(b["hold_fix"]).get("status") != "done":
                b["held"] = f"[batch] held until fix task {b['hold_fix']} merges"
                return
            log(f"[batch] fix task {b['hold_fix']} merged; batches resume")
            b.update(hold_fix=None, held=None)
            # Resume from HEAD: a gate kept from before the hold ran on the point CI failed, and the
            # earlier-gate shortcut below would cut the next batch there again (batch 148, 2026-09-29).
            g = b.get("gate") or {}
            if g.get("sha") and g["sha"] != git(self.repo, "rev-parse", self.main).stdout.strip():
                if g.get("pid") and "ok" not in g:
                    kill_group(int(g["pid"]))
                b["gate"] = None
        bis = b.get("bisect")
        if bis and self._is_ancestor(bis["bad"], up):   # the bad point reached GitHub after all (a flake): done
            b["bisect"] = bis = None
        if bis:
            parts = self._parts(up, bis["bad"])
            if len(parts) <= 1:
                culprit = self._tasks_between(up, bis["bad"])
                log(f"[batch] bisect: isolated {bis['bad'][:12]} ({', '.join(culprit) or 'no task'})")
                b["hold_fix"] = self._fix_task(f"fix-ci-{bis['bad'][:10]}",
                                               f"CI fails on local main commit {bis['bad'][:12]} (merge of {', '.join(culprit) or 'unknown'})",
                                               bis.get("ci", ""))
                b["bisect"] = None
                return
            target = parts[(len(parts) + 1) // 2 - 1]
        else:
            if int(git(self.repo, "rev-list", "--count", f"{up}..{self.main}").stdout) == 0:
                return
            target = git(self.repo, "rev-parse", self.main).stdout.strip()
            # A PR with no net change (a merge and its revert) starts no CI workflow, so its required checks
            # never report and the batch would stay open forever (batch 122, 2026-09-28). Ship it with the next change.
            if git(self.repo, "rev-parse", f"{target}^{{tree}}").stdout == git(self.repo, "rev-parse", f"{up}^{{tree}}").stdout:
                if b.get("no_change_head") != target:
                    b["no_change_head"] = target
                    log(f"[batch] local main {target[:12]} has no net change against GitHub main; waiting for the next merge")
                return
            g = b.get("gate") or {}
            if g.get("sha") and g["sha"] != target and self._is_ancestor(g["sha"], target) \
                    and self._is_ancestor(up, g["sha"]) and not self._is_ancestor(g["sha"], up) \
                    and ("ok" not in g or g["ok"]):
                target = g["sha"]                    # finish (or use) the gate already run on an earlier main
        ok = self._gate(b, target, up)
        if ok is None:
            return
        if not ok:
            out = Path(b["gate"]["log"]).read_text(errors="replace")
            if DISK_FULL_RE.search(out):             # systemic, as for task tests: no fix task, run it again in line
                log(f"[batch] pre-batch gate on {target[:12]} hit a full disk (systemic): queued again, no fix task")
                self._gate_lost(b, b["gate"])
                return
            # the whole log: _fix_task's failure_excerpt finds the failing lines; a 6000-character tail held only
            # later checks' output (fix-main-3c9dc70d4f, 2026-10-12)
            b["hold_fix"] = self._fix_task(f"fix-main-{target[:10]}", f"Local main {target[:12]} fails the test gate", out)
            return
        self._cut_batch(remote, base, prefix, b, up, target)

    def _cut_batch(self, remote: str, base: str, prefix: str, b: dict, up: str, head: str) -> None:
        tasks = self._tasks_between(up, head)
        push_sha = head
        if not self._is_ancestor(up, head):          # an older batch point (bisect): bring GitHub main into it
            mt = git(self.repo, "merge-tree", "--write-tree", up, head, check=False)
            if mt.returncode != 0:
                b["held"] = f"[batch] batch point {head[:12]} conflicts with {up[:12]}, needs a human"
                return
            push_sha = git(self.repo, "-c", "user.name=flood", "-c", "user.email=flood@localhost", "commit-tree",
                           mt.stdout.split()[0], "-p", head, "-p", up, "-m",
                           f"flood batch point {head[:12]} on {up[:12]}").stdout.strip()
        b["n"] += 1
        branch = f"{prefix}{b['n']}"
        git(self.repo, *self.remote_auth, "push", remote, f"{push_sha}:refs/heads/{branch}")   # a new branch; never force
        commits = git(self.repo, "log", "--oneline", f"{up}..{head}").stdout.strip()
        body = "\n".join([f"flood integration batch {b['n']}.", "", "Tasks:",
                          *(f"- {tid} ({self.state.task(tid)['merged_sha'][:12]})" for tid in tasks),
                          "", "Commits:", "```", commits, "```"])
        url = sh(["gh", "pr", "create", "--base", base, "--head", branch,
                  "--title", f"flood batch {b['n']}: {', '.join(tasks) or 'local merges'}", "--body", body],
                 cwd=self.repo).stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1]
        b.update(pr=int(url.rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]), head=head, branch=branch, tasks=tasks, url=url,
                 reruns=0, opened=time.time(), held=None)
        log(f"[batch {b['n']}] opened {url} at {head[:12]} with {len(tasks)} part(s): {', '.join(tasks) or 'local merges'}"
            + (" (bisect)" if b.get("bisect") else ""))

    def _required_green(self, pr: str) -> bool:
        """Every check GitHub marks required for this PR passed (or was skipped), at least one, and no review
        blocks it. Readable with a token without Administration (the automation user's, OMP-402)."""
        try:
            checks = json.loads(sh(["gh", "pr", "checks", pr, "--required", "--json", "name,bucket"],
                                   cwd=self.repo, check=False).stdout or "[]")
            review = json.loads(sh(["gh", "pr", "view", pr, "--json", "reviewDecision"],
                                   cwd=self.repo).stdout or "{}").get("reviewDecision")
        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            return False
        return bool(checks) and all(c.get("bucket") in ("pass", "skipping") for c in checks) \
            and review not in ("REVIEW_REQUIRED", "CHANGES_REQUESTED")

    def _ruleset_bypass(self, base: str, pr: str | None = None) -> bool:
        """A green PR GitHub reports BLOCKED only because of rulesets flood's gh user always bypasses.
        The 2026-10-02 10:31Z ruleset "omp-runtime-default-branch" (OMP-494) restricts updates of main to
        admins and the merge deploy key, so batch 250 sat BLOCKED with every check green. Classic protection
        must enforce admins, so `gh pr merge --admin` still skips no required check or review."""
        api = lambda path: json.loads(sh(["gh", "api", f"repos/{{owner}}/{{repo}}/{path}"], cwd=self.repo).stdout)
        try:
            try:
                enforced = (api(f"branches/{base}/protection").get("enforce_admins") or {}).get("enabled") is True
            except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
                # A token without Administration (ompbot's, owner 2026-10-10) cannot read protection (HTTP 403):
                # then flood checks the PR's required checks and review itself before it uses --admin.
                if "403" not in (getattr(e, "stderr", "") or "") or not pr:
                    return False
                enforced = self._required_green(pr)
            if not enforced:
                return False
            ids = {r["ruleset_id"] for r in api(f"rules/branches/{base}") if r.get("ruleset_id")}
            return bool(ids) and all(api(f"rulesets/{i}").get("current_user_can_bypass") == "always" for i in ids)
        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError):
            return False

    def _poll_batch(self, remote: str, base: str, upstream: str, b: dict) -> None:
        n, pr = b["n"], str(b["pr"])
        v = json.loads(sh(["gh", "pr", "view", pr, "--json", "state,mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup,url,mergeCommit"],
                          cwd=self.repo).stdout)
        checks = v.get("statusCheckRollup") or []
        # ACTION_REQUIRED is a third-party app (Codacy) asking a human to look; required checks gate
        # the merge through mergeStateStatus, so it neither fails nor blocks a batch here.
        results = [str(c.get("conclusion") or c.get("state") or "").upper() for c in checks]
        ci_min = (time.time() - b.get("opened", time.time())) / 60
        if v["state"] == "MERGED":
            log(f"[batch {n}] merged: {v['url']}")
            b.update(pr=None, held=None)
            self._sync_main(upstream, b)
            self.ride_merged_batch(n, pr, (v.get("mergeCommit") or {}).get("oid") or "", b.get("tasks") or [], upstream)
            return
        if v["state"] == "CLOSED":
            log(f"[batch {n}] closed outside flood: {v['url']}")
            b.update(pr=None, held=None)
            return
        if v["mergeStateStatus"] in ("BEHIND", "DIRTY"):                 # someone else merged to base
            if self._sync_main(upstream, b):
                sh(["gh", "pr", "close", pr, "--delete-branch"], cwd=self.repo)
                b["stale"] = b.get("stale", 0) + 1 if b.get("stale_head") == b["head"] else 1
                b["stale_head"] = b["head"]
                log(f"[batch {n}] stale ({v['mergeStateStatus']}), closed; cutting a new batch")
                b.update(pr=None)
                if b["stale"] >= 3:                   # the same point going stale again and again is a flood bug
                    b["held"] = f"[batch] batch point {b['head'][:12]} went stale 3 times in a row, needs a look"
                    b["hold_fix"] = b.get("hold_fix") or "_stale-loop"
            return
        if any(r in self.PENDING_CHECK for r in results) or not results:
            return                                                        # CI still running: never closed early
        if any(r in self.FAILED_CHECK for r in results):
            runs = sorted({m.group(1) for c in checks
                           if str(c.get("conclusion") or c.get("state") or "").upper() in self.FAILED_CHECK
                           for m in [re.search(r"/actions/runs/(\d+)", str(c.get("detailsUrl") or ""))] if m})
            if runs and b.get("reruns", 0) < 2:
                refused = [r for r in (sh(["gh", "run", "rerun", run, "--failed"], cwd=self.repo, check=False)
                                       for run in runs) if r.returncode]
                if not refused:
                    b["reruns"] = b.get("reruns", 0) + 1
                    log(f"[batch {n}] checks failed, re-running failed jobs ({b['reruns']}/2, run {', '.join(runs)}): {v['url']}")
                    return
                # GitHub refused the re-run (ompbot's token has no actions write since OMP-402): asking again every
                # poll never ends, so the batch is handled as red after its re-runs.
                why = (refused[0].stderr or refused[0].stdout or "").strip().splitlines()
                log(f"[batch {n}] re-run refused ({why[-1] if why else 'rc ' + str(refused[0].returncode)}); "
                    f"handling the red checks without a re-run")
            ci = self._ci_failure_text(v["url"], checks)
            up = git(self.repo, "rev-parse", upstream).stdout.strip()
            parts = self._parts(up, b["head"])
            sh(["gh", "pr", "close", pr, "--delete-branch"], cwd=self.repo)
            if len(parts) <= 1:
                culprit = self._tasks_between(up, b["head"])
                log(f"[batch {n}] red after {b.get('reruns', 0)} re-run(s) with 1 part, closed: {v['url']}")
                b["hold_fix"] = self._fix_task(f"fix-ci-{b['head'][:10]}",
                                               f"CI fails on batch {n} ({', '.join(culprit) or b['head'][:12]})", ci)
                b["bisect"] = None
            else:
                b["bisect"] = {"bad": b["head"], "ci": ci}
                log(f"[batch {n}] red after {b.get('reruns', 0)} re-run(s) with {len(parts)} parts, closed; "
                    f"bisect between {up[:12]} and {b['head'][:12]}: {v['url']}")
            b.update(pr=None, held=None)
            return
        green = all(r in ("SUCCESS", "NEUTRAL", "SKIPPED", "ACTION_REQUIRED") for r in results)
        bypass = green and v["mergeStateStatus"] == "BLOCKED" and self._ruleset_bypass(base, pr)
        if green and (bypass or v["mergeStateStatus"] in ("CLEAN", "HAS_HOOKS", "UNSTABLE")):   # UNSTABLE: only a non-required check (Codacy) is not green
            r = sh(["gh", "pr", "merge", pr, "--merge", *(["--admin"] if bypass else [])], cwd=self.repo, check=False)
            if r.returncode:
                if b.get("merge_err") != r.stderr.strip():
                    b["merge_err"] = r.stderr.strip()
                    log(f"[batch {n}] merge refused{' (ruleset bypass)' if bypass else ''}: {r.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
                return
            log(f"[batch {n}] checks green, merged: {v['url']} ({len(b.get('tasks') or [])} part(s), "
                f"CI {ci_min:.0f} min, {b.get('reruns', 0)} re-run(s))")
            b.update(pr=None, held=None)
            git(self.repo, *self.remote_auth, "fetch", "-q", remote, base)
            self._sync_main(upstream, b)
            if b.get("bisect") and self._is_ancestor(b["bisect"]["bad"], b.get("head", "")):
                b["bisect"] = None
            if self.cfg.get("codacy_repo"):    # before the deploy and the ride: an error there lost PR #362's check
                self.state.data.setdefault("codacy_due", []).append(pr)
            self.post_merge()
            self.write_report(f"batch {n} merged")
            merged = json.loads(sh(["gh", "pr", "view", pr, "--json", "mergeCommit"], cwd=self.repo).stdout)
            self.ride_merged_batch(n, pr, (merged.get("mergeCommit") or {}).get("oid") or "", b.get("tasks") or [], upstream)

    def reload_tasks(self) -> None:
        """Pick up task files the exporter (or the operator) added, renamed, parked or rewrote. Content counts,
        not only names: an operator who puts a <id>.md.failed back over a converted plan file keeps the name set
        unchanged, and flood ran the plan again (OMP-315-s05-s02, 2026-10-10)."""
        names = sorted((p.name, st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size) for p in self.tasks_dir.glob("*.md") for st in [p.stat()])
