        if names == getattr(self, "_task_names", None):
            return
        try:
            self.tasks = load_tasks(self.tasks_dir)
            self._task_names = names
        except SystemExit as e:                  # e.g. a dependency whose file is parked: keep the old set
            if getattr(self, "_reload_error", None) != str(e):
                log(f"[tasks] reload refused, keeping the loaded set: {e}")
                self._reload_error = str(e)

    # ---- REPORT.md: rewritten at every event (promotion, completion, merge, audit flag) -----
    def write_report(self, event: str, save: bool = True) -> None:
        tasks = self.state.data["tasks"]
        ended = self.state.data.get("outcomes", [])       # as they happened, resets included
        def rate(xs: list[dict]) -> str:
            d = sum(x["status"] == "done" for x in xs)
            return f"{d}/{len(xs)} ({100 * d // len(xs)}%)" if xs else "n/a"
        push = self.cfg.get("push") or {}
        upstream = f"{push.get('remote', 'origin')}/{push.get('base', self.main)}"
        last = self.state.data.get("report_main")
        merges = git(self.repo, "log", "--oneline", "--first-parent", f"{last}..{upstream}" if last else "-5", upstream,
                     check=False).stdout.strip() if last != git(self.repo, "rev-parse", upstream, check=False).stdout.strip() else ""
        self.state.data["report_main"] = git(self.repo, "rev-parse", upstream, check=False).stdout.strip()
        created = [l for l in (self.findings_file.parent / "ledger-writes.log").read_text().splitlines()] \
            if (self.findings_file.parent / "ledger-writes.log").exists() else []
        riders = sorted({e["key"] for f in (self.rider_dir.glob("*.json") if self.rider_dir.is_dir() else [])   # still staged
                         for e in json.loads(f.read_text() or "[]") if isinstance(e, dict) and "key" in e})
        closed = [l for l in created if l.startswith("closed ")]
        needs = [f"- {t}: {st['stuck'] if isinstance(st['stuck'], str) else (st.get('last_error') or '').split(chr(10))[0][:150]}"
                 for t, st in tasks.items() if st.get("stuck") and "Chris's" not in str(st["stuck"])]
        # a digest park on Chris's approval (D30) is not a ladder item: it is on the Waiting for Chris list
        dfile = self.findings_file.parent / "deferred.json"      # {ledger key: reason}, written by the operator
        deferred = [f"- {k}: {v}" for k, v in sorted(json.loads(dfile.read_text()).items())] if dfile.exists() else []
        prov = [f"| {n} | {p.get('max_parallel', 1)} | {self.state.provider(n)['runs']} | {self.state.provider(n)['failures']} |"
                f" {'benched until ' + dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(self.state.provider(n)['cooldown_until'], dt.timezone.utc).strftime('%H:%MZ') if self.state.provider(n)['cooldown_until'] > time.time() else 'ok'} |"
                for n, p in self.providers.items()]
        rows = [f"| {t} | {st['status']} | {st['attempts']} | {' '.join(((self.owner_wait(self.tasks[t]) if st['status'] == 'owner' else '') or st.get('last_error') or st.get('done_ref') or st.get('merged_sha') or '').split()).replace('|', '/')[:120]} |"
                for t, st in sorted(tasks.items()) if t in self.tasks]
        text = "\n".join([
            "# flood report", "", f"Last event: {event} ({now()})", "",
            "## Status", "", "| task | status | att | info |", "|---|---|---|---|", *rows, "",
            "## Merges to GitHub main since the last report", "", "```", merges or "(none)", "```", "",
            f"## Merge rate", "", f"- last 10 outcomes: {rate(ended[-10:])}", f"- all time: {rate(ended)}", "",
            "## Ledger", "", f"- staged in rider batches (closure pending): {', '.join(riders) or 'none'}",
            f"- closed in the ledger by flood (record_external_delivery): {len(closed)} all time",
            *[f"- {l}" for l in created[-20:]], "",
            "## Stuck (the operator takes one ladder rung per pass: scope ruling, split, missing input, defer)", "",
            *(needs or ["(none)"]), "",
            "## Deferred (ledger state DEFERRED; not exported, nobody waits on it)", "", *(deferred or ["(none)"]), "",
            "## Provider failures (for Chris: recent failures demote a provider in routing)", "",
            *(self.failure_report() or ["(no provider has failures in the window)"]), "",
            "## Providers", "", "| provider | max_parallel | runs | failures | state |", "|---|---|---|---|---|", *prov, ""])
        notes = self.findings_file.parent / "report-notes.md"    # operator sections (roster check, pass summary) kept across rewrites
        if notes.exists():
            text += "\n" + notes.read_text().strip() + "\n"
        atomic_write(self.findings_file.parent / "REPORT.md", text)
        if save:
            self.state.save()

    def failure_report(self) -> list[str]:
        n, hours = self.demote_cfg()
        out = []
        for name in self.providers:
            fails = self.recent_failures(name)
            if fails:
                out.append(f"- {name}: {len(fails)} in {hours:g} h" + (f" — DEMOTED (threshold {n})" if len(fails) >= n else "")
                           + ": " + "; ".join(f"{e['when'][11:16]}Z {e['kind']} {e['task']}" for e in fails[-5:]))
        return out

    def all_terminal(self) -> bool:
        return all(self.state.task(t)["status"] in TERMINAL for t in self.tasks) and not self.running_ids()

    @property
    def requests_dir(self) -> Path:
        return Path(self.cfg_dir) / "requests"

    def apply_requests(self) -> None:
        """State commands queued by the CLI while flood runs (queue_request), applied between ticks."""
        d = self.requests_dir
        if not d.is_dir():
            return
        for p in sorted(d.glob("*.json")):
            try:
                a = argparse.Namespace(**({k: None for k in REQUEST_FIELDS} | json.loads(p.read_text())))
            except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError) as e:
                log(f"[request] {p.name} unreadable, dropped: {e}")
                p.unlink(missing_ok=True)
                continue
            try:
                rc, out = 0, state_command(self, a)
            except CmdError as e:
                rc, out = 2, f"flood.py {a.cmd}: error: {e}"
            log(f"[request] {a.cmd} {a.task or ''}: {out}")
            atomic_write(p.with_suffix(".result"), json.dumps({"rc": rc, "out": out}))
            p.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        for r in d.glob("*.result"):         # answers nobody waited for
            if time.time() - r.stat().st_mtime > 3600:
                r.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    def code_signature(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        files = [Path(__file__).resolve()] + ([Path(self.cfg_file)] if getattr(self, "cfg_file", None) else [])
        out = {}
        for p in files:
            try:
                out[str(p)] = hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            except OSError:
                out[str(p)] = ""
        return out

    def reload_if_changed(self) -> None:
        """Load a changed flood.py or flood.json by exec'ing in place: same pid, same cgroup, so running jobs are
        not touched and are adopted as after a restart. A systemd restart ends every job under the stop guard's
        KillMode=control-group (2026-10-10). A file that does not compile or parse is not loaded; logged once."""
        sig = self.code_signature()
        if sig == self._code_sig:
            return
        # only committed code loads: an edit in progress can compile and still be half done; commit = release
        r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(self.cfg_dir), "status", "--porcelain", "--", *sig],
                           capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.returncode == 0 and r.stdout.strip():
            if getattr(self, "_uncommitted_sig", None) != sig:
                self._uncommitted_sig = sig
                log("[reload] flood.py or flood.json has uncommitted changes: not loaded until committed")
            return
        try:
            for f in sig:
                if f.endswith(".py"):
                    compile(Path(f).read_text(), f, "exec")
                else:
                    json.loads(Path(f).read_text())
        except (SyntaxError, ValueError, OSError) as e:
            if getattr(self, "_bad_sig", None) != sig:
                self._bad_sig = sig
                log(f"[reload] changed code or config does not load, keeping the running version: {e}")
            return
        self.state.save()
        log("[reload] flood.py or flood.json changed: exec in place (running jobs continue)")
        sys.stdout.flush()
        os.execv(sys.executable, [sys.executable] + sys.argv)

    def run(self, once: bool = False, forever: bool = False) -> int:
        log(f"flood: {len(self.tasks)} tasks, {self.slots} slots, repo={self.repo}")
        for tid in self.running_ids():          # nothing is spawned yet, so every running job is a previous run's
            job = self.state.task(tid)["job"] or {}
            log(f"[{tid}] adopted pid={job.get('pid')} phase={job.get('phase')} provider={job.get('provider')}")
        self._code_sig = self.code_signature()
        while True:
            self.apply_requests()
            self.tick()
            if once:
                return 0
            if not forever and self.all_terminal():
                self.status()
                return 0 if all(self.state.task(t)["status"] == "done" for t in self.tasks) else 1
            if forever:
                self.reload_tasks()
                self.reload_if_changed()
            time.sleep(self.poll)

    def status(self) -> None:
        rows = []
        for tid, task in self.tasks.items():
            st = self.state.task(tid)
            job = st.get("job") or {}
            extra = ""
            if st["status"] == "running":
                extra = f"{job.get('phase')} {job.get('provider') or ''} {int(time.time() - job.get('started', time.time()))}s pid={job.get('pid')}"
            elif st["status"] == "done" and st.get("done_ref"):
                extra = f"delivered outside flood ({st['done_ref']})" if not st.get("slices") else st["done_ref"]
            elif st["status"] == "done":
                extra = f"merged {str(st.get('merged_sha', ''))[:12]}"
            elif st["status"] == "planned":
                n_done = sum(self.state.task(sl)["status"] == "done" for sl in st.get("slices", []))
                extra = f"planned: {n_done}/{len(st.get('slices', []))} slices done"
            elif st["status"] == "owner":
                extra = self.owner_wait(task)
            elif st["status"] == "plan_ready":
                extra = f"plan ready: {len(list(self.proposed_dir(tid).glob('*.md')))} slices await `flood.py promote {tid}`"
            elif st.get("last_error"):
                extra = st["last_error"].splitlines()[0][:80]
            rows.append((tid, st["status"], str(st["attempts"]), ",".join(task.get("depends_on", [])), extra))
        # show slices directly under their parent (<parent>-sNN sorts before <parent>.md on disk)
        # at every depth, so slices of slices are listed too
        parents = {r[0] for r in rows}
        kids: dict[str, list] = {}
        for r in rows:
            if re.fullmatch(r".+-s\d{2}", r[0]) and r[0].rsplit("-s", 1)[0] in parents:
                kids.setdefault(r[0].rsplit("-s", 1)[0], []).append(r)

        def tree(r: tuple, depth: int) -> list:
            head = [(f"{'  ' * depth}└ {r[0]}" if depth else r[0],) + r[1:]]
            return head + [x for k in kids.get(r[0], []) for x in tree(k, depth + 1)]
        tops = [r for r in rows if not (re.fullmatch(r".+-s\d{2}", r[0]) and r[0].rsplit("-s", 1)[0] in parents)]
        rows = [x for r in tops for x in tree(r, 0)]
        w = [max(len(r[i]) for r in rows + [("task", "status", "att", "deps", "info")]) for i in range(5)]
        for r in [("task", "status", "att", "deps", "info")] + rows:
            print("  ".join(c.ljust(w[i]) for i, c in enumerate(r)))
        prov = ", ".join(f"{n}:{self.provider_load().get(n, 0)}/{p.get('max_parallel', 1)}"
                         for n, p in self.providers.items())
        print(f"running {len(self.running_ids())} ({self.occupied_slots()}/{self.slots} slots; test-phase jobs share one)  providers {prov}")
        b = self.state.data.get("batch")
        if self.cfg.get("push") and b:
            print(f"batch {b['n']}: " + (f"PR #{b['pr']} open ({', '.join(b.get('tasks') or [])})" if b.get("pr") else "no PR open")
                  + (f"; HELD: {b['held']}" if b.get("held") else ""))




class CmdError(Exception):
    """A state command refused; the message says why."""


STATE_CMDS = ("reset", "retest", "mark-done", "forget", "hold-fix")


def state_command(f: "Flood", a: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    """reset / retest / mark-done / forget on f's state. The CLI calls it while flood is stopped; the running loop
    calls it for a queued request (requests/), so these commands no longer need a flood stop (2026-10-10: nine
    restarts in 85 minutes, each ending every running job under the stop guard's KillMode=control-group)."""
    if a.task and a.task not in f.tasks and a.task not in f.state.data["tasks"]:
        raise CmdError(f"unknown task {a.task}")        # state.task() would add an empty entry for a typo
    if a.cmd == "forget":
        st = f.state.data["tasks"].get(a.task or "")
        if not st or not a.yes:
            raise CmdError("forget needs a known task id and --yes (drops that ONE task's state, worktree and branch)")
        if st["status"] == "running":
            raise CmdError(f"{a.task} is running")
        f.forget(a.task)
        f.state.save()
        return (f"{a.task} removed from state (worktree and branch dropped)")
    if a.cmd == "mark-done":
        if not a.task or not a.ref:
            raise CmdError("mark-done needs a task id and --ref <sha-or-PR>")
        st = f.state.task(a.task)
        if a.task not in f.tasks or st["status"] == "running":
            raise CmdError(f"mark-done needs a known task that is not running; {a.task} is {st['status']}")
        st.update(status="done", phase=None, job=None, done_ref=a.ref, finished=now())
        unblocked = f.unblock_dependents(a.task)
        f.state.save()
        push = f.cfg.get("push") or {}
        upstream = f"{push.get('remote', 'origin')}/{push.get('base', f.main)}"
        if f.write_rider([(a.task, a.ref, f"delivered outside flood: {a.ref}; {f.task_title(a.task)}")]
                         + f.parents_complete(upstream, f"owner step {a.task}: {a.ref}")):
            f.close_delivered()        # an owner step may finish a parent: close it now, not at the next batch
        return (f"{a.task} marked done (ref {a.ref}, delivered outside flood)"
              + (f"; unblocked {', '.join(unblocked)}" if unblocked else ""))
    if a.cmd == "retest":
        if not a.task:
            raise CmdError("retest needs a task id")
        st = f.state.task(a.task)
        if a.gate_bug and st["status"] == "running" and st.get("phase") == "test-wait":
            pass                       # already queued for tests: only restore attempts and move it up
        elif a.task not in f.tasks or st["status"] not in ("failed", "pending"):
            raise CmdError(f"retest needs a known failed or pending task; {a.task} is {st['status']}")
        if not (f.worktree_path(a.task) / ".git").exists():
            raise CmdError(f"retest needs the task's worktree; {f.worktree_path(a.task)} is gone (use reset)")
        if a.gate_bug:                 # a gate/script bug is never charged: back to the count before that failure
            fails = [h for h in st.get("history", []) if h.get("phase") == "test" and h.get("ok") is False
                     and not h.get("main_red")]
            before = fails[-1].get("attempt", st["attempts"]) if fails else st["attempts"]
            st["history"].append({"phase": "uncharged", "at": now(), "attempts": before, "was": st["attempts"],
                                  "reason": a.note or "test failure caused by a gate/script bug"})
            st.update(attempts=before, gate_bug=True)
        if st.get("phase") != "test-wait":
            st.update(status="pending", phase=None, job=None, retest=True)
        st.pop("stuck", None)                     # the operator acted on it: off the stuck list
        unblocked = f.unblock_dependents(a.task) + f.reopen_parents(a.task)
        f.state.save()
        return (f"{a.task} queued for a test re-run on its current worktree (attempts stay {st['attempts']})"
              + (f"; unblocked {', '.join(unblocked)}" if unblocked else ""))
    if a.cmd == "reset":
        if not a.task:
            raise CmdError("reset needs a task id")
        st = f.state.task(a.task)
        if st["status"] == "running" and st.get("job", {}).get("pid"):
            kill_group(int(st["job"]["pid"]))
        st.update(status="pending", phase=None, job=None, attempts=0)   # plain: keep last_error + history for the prompt
        st.pop("stuck", None)
        dropped = f.drop_slices(a.task) if a.task in f.tasks and f.tasks[a.task].get("kind") != "plan" else []
        if a.note:
            st["note"] = a.note
        if a.fresh:                    # the dropped branch's makers wrote nothing that stays: the maker rule
            st.update(last_error=None, history=[])   # forgets them (OMP-344-s01-s01: 7 authors, no reviewer left)
            st.pop("authors", None)
            f.drop_worktree_and_branch(a.task)
        unblocked = f.unblock_dependents(a.task) + f.reopen_parents(a.task)
        f.state.save()
        kept = "branch and worktree deleted; next attempt starts from main" if a.fresh else "branch and worktree kept"
        return (f"{a.task} reset to pending ({kept})" + (f"; unblocked {', '.join(unblocked)}" if unblocked else "")
                + (f"; dropped the old plan's slices {', '.join(dropped)}" if dropped else ""))
    if a.cmd == "hold-fix":
        # The operator found the cause of a red batch in the CI log (e.g. CI changed, not a merge): hold batches on
        # its fix task instead of a multi-hour bisect that can only blame the first merge (batch 258, 2026-10-10).
        if not a.task or a.task not in f.tasks:
            raise CmdError("hold-fix needs the id of a written fix task (tasks/<id>.md)")
        if f.state.task(a.task)["status"] == "done":
            raise CmdError(f"{a.task} is already done")
        b = f.state.data.setdefault("batch", {"n": 0, "pr": None})
        if b.get("pr"):
            raise CmdError(f"batch PR {b['pr']} is open; hold-fix acts only between batches")
        before = {k: b.get(k) for k in ("bisect", "hold_fix")}
        g = b.get("gate") or {}
        if g.get("sha") and g["sha"] != git(f.repo, "rev-parse", f.main).stdout.strip():
            if g.get("pid") and "ok" not in g:
                kill_group(int(g["pid"]))
            b["gate"] = None                       # a bisect midpoint gate is no longer wanted
        b.pop("gate_want", None)
        b.pop("gate_want_at", None)
        b.update(bisect=None, hold_fix=a.task, held=f"[batch] held until fix task {a.task} merges")
        f.state.save()
        return (f"batches held on {a.task}" + (f" ({a.note})" if a.note else "")
                + f"; before: bisect={(before['bisect'] or {}).get('bad', 'none')[:12]}, hold_fix={before['hold_fix']}")
    raise CmdError(f"not a state command: {a.cmd}")


REQUEST_FIELDS = ("cmd", "task", "note", "ref", "gate_bug", "fresh", "yes")


REQUEST_WAIT_SEC = 300.0


def queue_request(f: "Flood", a: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Hand a state command to the running loop (requests/<id>.json) and print its answer when it comes."""
    d = f.requests_dir
    d.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    rid = f"{time.time_ns()}-{os.getpid()}"
    atomic_write(d / f"{rid}.json", json.dumps({k: getattr(a, k, None) for k in REQUEST_FIELDS}))
    res = d / f"{rid}.result"
    end = time.time() + REQUEST_WAIT_SEC
    while time.time() < end:
        if res.exists():
            r = json.loads(res.read_text())
            res.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            print(r["out"], file=sys.stdout if r["rc"] == 0 else sys.stderr)
            return r["rc"]
        time.sleep(1)
    print(f"flood is running: request {rid} queued; it is applied on flood's next tick (see flood.log)")
    return 0


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- cli
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("cmd", choices=["run", "status", "report", "reset", "retest", "mark-done", "promote", "audit", "wipe",
                                    "forget", "hold-fix", "hygiene", "teststats", "check-plan"])
    ap.add_argument("task", nargs="?")
    ap.add_argument("--config", default="flood.json")
    ap.add_argument("--once", action="store_true", help="one scheduling tick, then exit")
    ap.add_argument("--forever", action="store_true", help="keep polling for new task files")
    ap.add_argument("--yes", action="store_true", help="confirm a destructive command")
    ap.add_argument("--note", help="reset: an instruction added to the next attempt's continuation; hold-fix: why")
    ap.add_argument("--ref", help="mark-done: where the work landed (commit SHA or PR, e.g. a5609b58 or PR #33)")
    ap.add_argument("--gate-bug", action="store_true",
                    help="retest: the failure was a gate/script bug; restore the pre-failure attempt count, test first")
    ap.add_argument("--hours", type=float, default=24, help="teststats: window length")
    ap.add_argument("--fresh", action="store_true",
                    help="reset: also delete the task's worktree and branch (use when the task spec changed)")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    cfg_path = Path(a.config).resolve()
    cfg = json.loads(cfg_path.read_text())
    f = Flood(cfg, cfg_path.parent)
    f.cfg_file = cfg_path
    if a.cmd == "check-plan":      # read-only: the planner runs this on its own slice files before finishing
        if not a.task:
            ap.error("check-plan needs the plan task's id")
        violations, slices = f.check_plan(a.task)
        print("\n".join(f"- {x}" for x in violations) if violations else f"OK: {len(slices)} slices pass the plan gate")
        return 1 if violations else 0
    # `run` keeps its whole state in memory and saves over the file, so a state change made by another
    # process while it runs is silently lost. `run` holds this lock; commands that write state refuse.
    lock = open(f.state.path.with_name(f.state.path.name + ".lock"), "a")
    running = False
    if a.cmd in ("run", "reset", "retest", "mark-done", "wipe", "report", "forget", "hold-fix", "hygiene"):
        try:
            fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except BlockingIOError:
            running = True
        if running and a.cmd not in ("report", "hygiene") + STATE_CMDS:   # report: REPORT.md only; hygiene shows only
            ap.error(f"flood is running and would overwrite this {a.cmd}; stop it first "
                     "(systemctl --user stop flood; this ends every running job), then start it again")
    if a.cmd == "status":
        f.status()
        return 0
    if a.cmd == "hygiene":         # flood applies this itself hourly; while it runs, this only shows what it will do
        acts = f.hygiene(apply=not running)
        print("\n".join(acts) or "hygiene: nothing to do")
        if running and acts:
            print("(flood is running: shown only; its hourly sweep applies these)")
        return 0
    if a.cmd == "teststats":
        end = time.time()
        for name, (lo, hi) in (("last", (end - a.hours * 3600, end)), ("before", (end - 2 * a.hours * 3600, end - a.hours * 3600))):
            print(name, json.dumps(f.teststats(lo, hi)))
        return 0
    if a.cmd == "wipe":
        if not a.yes:
            ap.error("wipe deletes every task's worktree and branch and the state file; add --yes")
        for tid, st in f.state.data["tasks"].items():
            if st.get("status") == "running" and (st.get("job") or {}).get("pid"):
                kill_group(int(st["job"]["pid"]))
        for tid in f.tasks:
            f.drop_worktree_and_branch(tid)
        # rotate logs so the next run's attempt-numbered files do not append onto this run's
        rotated = f.logs_dir.with_name(f"{f.logs_dir.name}.{dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc):%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ}")
        f.logs_dir.rename(rotated)
        if f.state.path.exists():
            shutil.copy2(f.state.path, rotated / f.state.path.name)
            f.state.path.unlink()
        print(f"wiped {len(f.tasks)} task worktrees/branches and {f.state.path.name}; "
              f"{f.logs_dir.name}/ rotated to {rotated.name}/ (state copied in); {f.main} untouched")
        return 0
    if a.cmd == "report":
        f.write_report("operator pass" if not a.task else a.task, save=not running)
        print(f"wrote {f.findings_file.parent / 'REPORT.md'}")
        return 0
    if a.cmd == "audit":           # every job log flood ever wrote next to this config, current and rotated
        logs = sorted({*f.logs_dir.glob("*.log"), *f.logs_dir.parent.glob(f"{f.logs_dir.name}.*/*.log"),
                       *f.logs_dir.parent.glob("archive-*/**/*.log")})
        hits = 0
        for lf in logs:
            for n, line in enumerate(lf.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines(), 1):
                if EXTERNAL_CALL_RE.search(line):
                    hits += 1
                    print(f"{lf.relative_to(f.logs_dir.parent)}:{n}: {line.strip()[:220]}")
        print(f"audit: {hits} matching line(s) in {len(logs)} log file(s)")
        return 0
    if a.cmd == "promote":
        if not a.task or f.state.task(a.task)["status"] != "plan_ready":
            ap.error(f"promote needs a task whose plan passed gate and review; {a.task} is {f.state.task(a.task or '')['status']}")
        violations, _ = f.check_plan(a.task)
        if violations:
            print("plan gate failed:\n- " + "\n- ".join(violations))
            return 1
        (f.proposed_dir(a.task) / "PROMOTE").touch()
        print(f"{a.task}: promotion approved; flood moves the slices into {f.tasks_dir.name}/ on its next tick")
        return 0
    if a.cmd in STATE_CMDS:
        if running:
            return queue_request(f, a)
        try:
            print(state_command(f, a))
        except CmdError as e:
            ap.error(str(e))
        return 0
    return f.run(once=a.once, forever=a.forever)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
